2324629.title: Connecting Kashmir: Building the Infrastructure for Growth
2324629.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Connecting Kashmir: Building the Infrastructure for Growth
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 11:21AM by PIB Delhi

Jammu and Kashmir's challenging terrain is steadily yielding to a new era of connectivity. The Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link has connected the valley to India's rail network. Its centrepiece, the Chenab Bridge, stands as the world's highest railway arch bridge. Expanded Vande Bharat services are improving passenger mobility. New freight terminals are carrying Kashmiri apples, saffron and handicrafts to national markets, opening opportunities for farmers and businesses. On land, the Sonamarg and Zojila tunnels promise year-round passage into Ladakh. In the air, Srinagar's expanding airport is complemented by nascent hubs at Udhampur and Kishtwar. Together, these advances are drawing Kashmir's produce, trade and tourism firmly into the national mainstream.

 

A Region Reconnected

Jammu and Kashmir's mountainous terrain has long made connectivity a major infrastructure challenge. Over the years, this has been steadily changing, with a wave of infrastructure investment reshaping how the region connects with the rest of the country. The Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project is a major part of this expansion. It is one of the most challenging railway line projects undertaken in the country post-independence. Today it stands as one of India’s engineering marvels, linking the Kashmir Valley to the rest of the country by rail.

The USBRL project has also been accompanied by sustained expansion of roads, tunnels and airport infrastructure. The network now includes new train services such as the Vande Bharat Express. It also includes major road corridors and tunnels. Airport capacity is being expanded at Srinagar, with regional airports planned under UDAN, increasing passenger movement. Multimodal cargo terminals and enhanced freight services support goods movement across the region. These developments have progressively expanded all-weather connectivity infrastructure across Jammu and Kashmir.

Railways: Connecting Kashmir to the National Rail Network

Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) National Project

The USBRL project was inaugurated in June 2025, improving connectivity infrastructure in the Himalayan region. Built at a cost of ₹43,780 crore, the USBRL project covers the districts of Udhampur, Reasi, Ramban, Srinagar, Anantnag, Pulwama, Budgam and Baramulla of Jammu and Kashmir.

The project stretches 272 kilometres through the rugged Himalayas; it includes 36 tunnels that span 119 kilometres and 943 bridges. Designed to overcome the region’s challenging terrain, it connects remote areas with the national rail network. It is opening new opportunities for mobility, trade and tourism. As part of the USBRL project, over 215 km (including a tunnel and 320 bridges) of roads have been constructed, which are useful for communities. Additionally, the USBRL project is fully electrified both in tunnels and in open stretches.

The USBRL project has made substantial socio-economic contributions to the region, with employment generation being a significant aspect of its impact. The project has generated more than 5 crore man-days of employment.

Vande Bharat Express

Image 1: Vande Bharat Express, Jammu and Kashmir

The Vande Bharat Express in Jammu and Kashmir first began operations in June 2025, between Katra and Srinagar. To further enhance railway connectivity, the Srinagar-Katra Vande Bharat Express service was extended to Jammu Tawi Railway Station in April 2026. 

The distance from Jammu to Srinagar is now covered in less than five hours. The trains have been augmented from 8 to 20 coaches. They are specially designed to operate in extreme weather conditions. The trains are equipped with advanced operating systems and electronics suited for high-altitude conditions.

Supporting this route is a snow removal train that moves ahead to clear the tracks, ensuring year-round services. Seismic dampers have also been installed to absorb tremors, offering a safer and smoother journey in this high-risk zone.

Engineering Marvels under the USBRL Project  

The USBRL project includes several major engineering achievements, including the Chenab Rail Bridge, Anji Khad Bridge and Tunnel T50.

Chenab Rail Bridge

Under the USBRL project, the world’s highest railway arch bridge has been built over the Chenab River in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab bridge, inaugurated in June 2025, is 1,315 m long. It has an arch span of 467 metres and rises 359 metres above the riverbed, making it higher than the Eiffel Tower. The bridge is designed to withstand strong seismic and wind forces. With Vande Bharat services running over the bridge, connectivity has significantly improved between Jammu and Kashmir.

Image 2: Chenab Rail Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir

 

Anji Khad Bridge

Image 3: Anji Khad Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir

The Anji Khad bridge is India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge built above the Anji River gorge, a tributary of the Chenab River. The Anji Khad bridge is part of the USBRL project and was inaugurated in June 2025.

The bridge is located in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir. It is supported by a single 193-metre-high tower shaped like an inverted ‘Y’, with cables supporting the bridge. The main bridge has a total length of 473.25 metres, designed for the region’s challenging terrain and seismic conditions.

Tunnel T50

Image 4: Tunnel T50 in Jammu and Kashmir

Tunnel T50, inaugurated in 2024, is a 12.77-km rail tunnel linking Khari and Sumber in Jammu and Kashmir. It is India’s longest transportation tunnel, built under the USBRL project. The tunnel provides a vital rail link between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of India.

The New Austrian Tunnelling Method has been used to construct the tunnel through the challenging Himalayan geology. The tunnel engineering overcame the challenges of high-water ingress, landslides, shear zones, and jointed volcanic rocks. The tunnel features a main tube paired with a parallel escape tunnel, linked every 375 metres for safety. CCTV cameras are placed every 50 metres, which help monitor from a central control room.

Supporting Railway Infrastructure

Railway connectivity in Jammu and Kashmir is being strengthened through increased investment in supporting infrastructure and network development. The annual average budget of railways for Jammu and Kashmir has increased from ₹1,044 crore in 2009–14 to ₹1,086 crore in 2026–27.

Electrification

Indian Railways has pursued railway electrification in mission mode, with about 99.6% of the Broad Gauge (BG) network now electrified. In Jammu and Kashmir, the entire existing BG network is electrified. All new-line and multi-tracking projects are being sanctioned and built with electrification from the outset.

Station Redevelopment

Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, 1,340 stations have been identified for redevelopment across Indian Railways. Among them, four stations are in Jammu and Kashmir. The stations are Budgam, Jammu Tawi, Martyr Captain Tushar Mahajan (Udhampur) and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra station.

Other Regional Railway Initiatives

To strengthen railway connectivity in border areas and areas of strategic significance in Jammu and Kashmir, several projects are in the pipeline. These include

  1. A third line between Jalandhar Cantt. and Jammu Tawi (216 km).
  2. An additional line between Jammu and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra (78 km).
  3. A new railway line between Jammu/Reasi and Poonch (190 km).

 

Roads: Strengthening Surface Connectivity

Roads as a complement to Rail

In Jammu and Kashmir, road infrastructure is expanding alongside railway infrastructure. Roads remain essential for last-mile access to places outside the railway network. In August 2026, foundation stones were laid for 110 road projects covering 598.455 km under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)-IV. Costing more than ₹1,500 crore, the projects are expected to benefit 46,972 people across the Udhampur–Kathua–Doda–Kishtwar region. The projects also include the use of waste plastics in several road packages, supporting more sustainable road construction.

Tunnel construction has also become a key component of development in the Himalayan region to ensure all-weather connectivity, improve road safety, and enhance strategic mobility.

Sonamarg (Z-Morh) Tunnel

Image 5: Sonamarg Tunnel, Jammu and Kashmir

The Sonamarg tunnel project, also known as the Z-Morh, inaugurated in January 2025, is a 6.4 km bi-directional tunnel with a parallel escape tunnel of length 6.4 km and an approach road of length 5.5km. Constructed at a cost of over ₹2,700 crore, the tunnel sits at an altitude of 2634 meters above sea level. The tunnel provides all-weather connectivity between Srinagar and Sonamarg enroute to Leh. It bypasses parts of the road hit by major avalanches and landslides. It promotes tourism by transforming Sonamarg into a year-round destination, boosting winter tourism, adventure sports and local livelihoods. Along with the Zojila Tunnel, it will cut the NH-1 section of this project from 13 km to 11.98 km.

Zojila Tunnel

The Zojila Tunnel is a 13.153-kilometre-long bi-directional tunnel being constructed between Baltal and Minamarg on National Highway-1 by NHIDCL. Elevated at 2,900–3,310 metres, the ₹6,808-crore project will provide all-weather year-round road connectivity between Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. With construction beginning in October 2020, the main tunnel achieved breakthrough in June 2026.

 

Image 6: Zojila Tunnel, Jammu and Kashmir

The tunnel will be equipped with modern ventilation systems, automatic fire detection and suppression systems, CCTV surveillance, a Variable Message Sign (VMS) system, SCADA system, and other advanced safety and traffic management systems. The project also includes two twin tube uni-directional Nilgari tunnels of total length 4.8 km,  eight cut-and-cover sections with a total length of 2.350 km, four bridges with a total length of 810 m, 40 culverts, snow galleries, catch dams, deflector dams, air-blast walls, and other avalanche protection structures along the approach road of length 16.964 km.

Upon completion, the project is expected to reduce the travel time between Sonamarg and Minamarg from approximately two hours to around 30 minutes. The project will also reduce the risks of accidents and disruptions associated with the treacherous Zojila Pass, which remains vulnerable to heavy snowfall and avalanches during the winter months. The tunnel will boost tourism, trade, and access to remote and border areas. Year-round connectivity will strengthen defence logistics and strategic preparedness. It will also create employment opportunities, support economic growth, and improve livelihoods and quality of life for local communities.

Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (earlier known as Chenani-Nashri Tunnel)

The 9 km tunnel, opened in 2017, is India's longest operating highway tunnel and Asia's longest bi-directional tunnel. It connects Udhampur to Ramban in Jammu and Kashmir.  Built at a cost of ₹2500 crore, it reduces travel distance by 31 km and cuts the travel time by two hours, saving fuel costs.

Expanding the Highway Network

  • Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway: The expressway is a 667-km greenfield highway connecting Delhi with Amritsar and Katra. It is designed to provide a faster road link, reduce congestion on NH-44, and improve access to major destinations, including the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi shrine. In July 2026, key sections of the expressway were inaugurated, marking a major step towards improving connectivity between Delhi and Katra. The completed sections are expected to reduce travel time between Delhi and Katra from about 14 hours to nearly six hours. The corridor will also strengthen connectivity for pilgrims and facilitate industrial and logistics activity along the route.
  • Rafiabad–Kupwara Road (NH-701): The foundation stone for the widening and strengthening of the Rafiabad–Kupwara section of NH-701 was laid in June 2025 to strengthen last-mile connectivity, particularly in border areas. The project forms part of the Rafiabad–Kupwara–Chowkibal–Tangdhar–Chamkot corridor under Project Beacon.
  • Shopian Bypass (NH-444): Sanctioned in March 2024 at a cost of ₹224.44 crore, the 8.925-km Shopian bypass had its foundation stone laid in June 2025. The bypass will improve connectivity between Shopian, Pulwama and Kulgam and facilitate faster transportation of agricultural produce.

Airports: Expanding Air Connectivity

Expansion of Srinagar International Airport

A ₹1,677 crore expansion of the Civil Enclave at Srinagar International Airport was approved in February 2026. The project is operated by the Airports Authority of India within Budgam Airbase of the Indian Air Force (IAF). It will strengthen aviation connectivity in the Kashmir Valley.

Spread over 73.18 acres, the development includes a new 71,500 square metre terminal building. The terminal will handle up to 2,900 passengers during peak hours and 10 million passengers annually. The airport will also have 15 aircraft parking bays, including space for one widebody aircraft. Its existing 3,658-metre runway will continue to be operated by the Indian Air Force. A new multi-level parking facility will also provide space for 1,000 cars. The project also includes barracks for security personnel.

The new terminal will combine modern airport facilities with elements of Kashmir’s traditional architecture, including local woodwork and craftsmanship. Sustainability is a core part of the project. It includes water harvesting, greater use of natural light, and locally sourced eco-friendly materials. The project is targeted to achieve a 5-star Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment (GRIHA) for sustainable building practices.

Extending Regional Air Connectivity

The Government is focusing on improving regional connectivity and providing affordable and secure travel options to residents of Jammu and Kashmir.

  • Udhampur and Kishtwar reflect how regional aviation can extend access to areas beyond the region’s major urban centres. The two airports are planned under the UDAN scheme to extend regional air connectivity in Jammu and Kashmir. Greater airport capacity is expected to support tourism, create employment, encourage investment and strengthen Srinagar’s role as an economic destination.

From Connectivity to Economic Integration

Multimodal Logistics

PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, launched in October 2021, brought railways, roads, ports, waterways, airports and logistics infrastructure onto a single, Geographic Information System (GIS) based planning platform. It spans 44 Central Ministries and 36 States and UTs. Building on this framework, the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT) policy, launched in December 2021, encourages the development of modern, rail-linked cargo terminals through private investment.

So far, 142 Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals have been commissioned in the country. In 2024, a Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT) was commissioned in Samba in Jammu and Kashmir and is now fully operational. In addition, In-Principle Approvals have been granted for the development of GCTs at 310 more locations, including three at Kathua, Anantnag and Jammu districts in Jammu and Kashmir.

The GCT policy has benefited key sectors such as cement, steel, power, mining, agriculture, logistics and manufacturing. It has enabled modern multimodal cargo terminals with warehousing, silos, cold storage and other value-added logistics facilities. This has increased the competitiveness of local industries and farmers while generating employment and promoting regional economic development.

From Access to Opportunities

A region once defined by seasonal isolation is emerging as a connected part of India's economic geography. Rail, road and air projects are no longer separate initiatives; together, they now function as one integrated network. This convergence is reshaping daily life for residents, farmers, traders and tourism operators alike. The expansion is increasing the access of farmers and local businesses to markets beyond the region. Signature Kashmir products, including apples, dry fruits, pashmina shawls and handicrafts, are being sold at larger markets, promoting economic diversity. At the same time, improved connectivity is strengthening the region's strategic position, including border security and disaster response.

2324612.title: Clarification on Legislative Developments concerning Government’s shareholding in IDBI
2324612.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Clarification on Legislative Developments concerning Government’s shareholding in IDBI
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 7:41AM by PIB Delhi

Certain sections of press and media have brought out reports, which inter alia have comments/ views regarding the legislative developments in 2003 concerning the Government’s shareholding in IDBI. It is reiterted that during the disucssions of Union Budget, 2003 and the parliamentary debate on the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of the Government’s stake was moved but was ultimately rejected and did not form part of the enacted legislation.

The matter was subsequently examined by the Delhi High Court in All India IDBI Officers’ Association v. Union of India & Others, decided on 17 December 2018. The Court, while dismissing the writ petition, adjudicated in paragraphs 41 and 42 as follows:

Paragraph 41:

“This Court is of the view that the statements made before the House almost 15 years earlier, in a debate relating to a legislative activity, would not preclude the Central Government from diluting its stake in IDBI Ltd. Indisputably, the legislation enacted by the Parliament after the debate did not contain the amendment that was sought to be introduced. The statements made before the House cannot substitute or override the statue so enacted by the Parliament. Surely, the Parliament was conscious of the import of not including the proviso as proposed. The principles of promissory estoppel are wholly inapplicable in the aforesaid context. It is not possible to accept that the statements made in Parliament amounted to a representation made to the employees and they had acted to their prejudice based on such representation. The statements made before the House were in the context of enacting a legislation (the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003), and the said Act has to be interpreted in conformity with the settled principles of statutory interpretation.”

Paragraph 42:

“There is no ambiguity in the language of the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003 and there is no scope to read any provision into the said enactment which proscribes the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd.”

The aforesaid judgment is significant as it specifically addresses the doctrine of promissory estoppel, which was relied upon in challenging the Government’s decision to dilute its shareholding. The doctrine could not be invoked to prevent the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd.

The Government’s policy towards the transformation and strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank was reiterated in successive Union Budget Speeches in the Parliament:

Union Budget 2016–17 — Speech of the then Hon’ble Finance Minister, Shri Arun Jaitley (Paragraph 93) said:

“Our Public Sector Banks will have to be strong and competitive. The Bank Board Bureau will be operationalized during 2016-17 and a roadmap for consolidation of Public Sector Banks will be spelt out. The process of transformation of IDBI Bank has already started. Government will take it forward and also consider the option of reducing its stake to below 50%.”

Union Budget 2021–22 — Speech of the then Hon’ble Finance Minister, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman (Paragraph 84) said:

“In spite of COVID-19, we have kept working towards strategic disinvestment. A number of transactions namely BPCL, Air India, Shipping Corporation of India, Container Corporation of India, IDBI Bank, BEML, Pawan Hans, Neelachal Ispat Nigam limited among others would be completed in 2021-22. Other than IDBI Bank, we propose to take up the privatization of two Public Sector Banks and one General Insurance company in the year 2021-22. This would require legislative amendments and I propose to introduce the amendments in this Session itself.”

The legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, the judicial pronouncement of the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and successive Union Budget Speeches collectively demonstrate the evolution of the Government’s policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank. The Judgment dated 17 December 2018 clarifies beyond doubt that the doctrine of promissory estoppel cannot be invoked on the basis of statements made during parliamentary debates to restrict the Government’s power to dilute its shareholding in the IDBI Bank Ltd.The Court further held that the enacted legislation contained no prohibition against reducing the Government’s stake in the IDBI Bank Ltd.

2324601.title: ITRA Jamnagar Hosts National Conference “Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026” on the Integration of Ayurveda and Artificial Intelligence
2324601.body_html:
AYUSH
ITRA Jamnagar Hosts National Conference “Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026” on the Integration of Ayurveda and Artificial Intelligence
National and International Experts Deliberate on Responsible AI and Digital Innovation in Ayurveda at ITRA Jamnagar
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi

A national conference on “AI and Ayurveda” was held under “Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026” on the occasion of the 6th Foundation Day of the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar. The conference held extensive deliberations on integrating Ayurveda with modern digital technology, the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in research, and the possibilities for its responsible use in healthcare services.

In a conversation with ITRA’s channel Ayush Next Communication Network (ANCN) on the sidelines of the event, Dr. Geetha Krishnan, Head of the Traditional Medicine Research, Data and Innovation Unit, WHO-GTMC, said: “Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds immense potential to understand Ayurveda better and make its application more effective. However, before adopting any new technology, a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of Ayurveda science is essential. AI should work as a complement to Ayurveda, not replace its core knowledge and wisdom. Maintaining the authenticity of Ayurveda while exploring the possibilities of modern technologies is an important responsibility of the Ayurveda world. By adopting a balanced approach, we can harness the potential of AI without compromising the core principles of Ayurveda. Establishing the right balance between tradition and innovation is our collective responsibility. Only by doing so can we take Ayurveda forward in a meaningful, effective and sustainable manner.”

Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA Jamnagar, said that Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026 has proved to be an important platform for innovation and collaboration for the future of Ayurveda. She said it provided an important platform to encourage dialogue between traditional Ayurvedic knowledge and advanced technology, and furthered discussion on the ethical, scientific and practical aspects of the potential use of AI in Ayurvedic research, education, drug development and healthcare services.

Shri Sameer Pujari, AI Lead, Digital Health and Innovation (DHI), WHO Headquarters, highlighted the potential of AI in the preservation of knowledge. He emphasised the global collaboration among WHO, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), ongoing since 2018, to advance AI applications in health. He also discussed the risks and challenges associated with AI, including ethical aspects, data privacy and regulatory barriers, particularly in the context of traditional medicine.

Shri Naman Goyal, Officer on Special Duty (OSD), Ayush Grid, Ministry of Ayush, said that the basic concepts, applications and working of AI and Machine Learning (ML) were covered, including key processes such as data collection, data processing, model training, testing and prediction. AI-driven chatbots and key digital tools under Ayush Grid were also showcased, and the presentation underlined the important role of these tools in strengthening digital health services and advancing technology-based Ayush services.

The conference aimed to link Ayurveda’s rich traditional knowledge with modern digital technology and encourage new possibilities in research, innovation and healthcare services. Ayurveda scholars, researchers, academicians, technology experts and national and international delegates shared their views, in person and online, across the sessions on the effective, ethical and scientific use of AI. Discussions covered potential applications of AI in Ayurvedic drug research and development, quality assurance, clinical trials and education, with special emphasis on integrating traditional knowledge with modern data-based methods, making research more effective, encouraging new product development and advancing technology-based healthcare services.

Thematic Sessions and Expert Participation

Sessions and expert discussions were held on the following themes:

  • Artificial Intelligence, digital knowledge and global transformation in traditional medicine systems
  • Responsible AI for Ayurveda: ethics, scientific evidence and innovation
  • The potential of AI-based Ayurveda, from traditional practices to intelligent healthcare services
  • Use of AI for innovation, product development and responsible clinical trials in Ayurveda

Experts from various reputed national and international institutions participated as keynote and principal speakers. They included Prof. Shubhada Nagarkar (Professor and Head, Department of Library and Information Science, and Coordinator, Centre for Publication Ethics (CPE), Savitribai Phule Pune University); Dr. Rajiv Vasudevan (Founder, Managing Director and CEO, Apollo Ayurveda Hospitals, Bengaluru); and Dr. Sumer Singh (Associate Professor, Department of Design, IIT Delhi).

Other speakers from the fields of Ayurveda and AI included Dr. Maki Kajiwara (Technical Officer, WHO-GTMC); Dr. Girish Tillu (Principal Investigator–Ayush, Centre of Excellence, Department of Health Sciences, Savitribai Phule Pune University); Dr. Sandeep Kale (Assistant Professor, Department of Rasashastra and Vikriti Vigyan, R. A. Podar Government Ayurved Medical College, Mumbai); Dr. Rajeshwari Singh (Senior Adviser, Data, Digital Health, Analytics and AI, Health Systems Division, WHO, Switzerland); Prof. (Dr.) Mitali Mukherjee (Professor, Department of Biosciences and Bioengineering, IIT Jodhpur); Dr. Santosh Dixit (Principal Domain Expert, Healthcare and Life Sciences, Persistent Systems); Dr. Ganesh Karaikhede (Healthcare Domain Expert, AI QT Group, C-DAC, Pune); and Dr. Bala Pesala (Founder and CEO, Ayur.AI).

The 6th Foundation Day of ITRA Jamnagar was celebrated yesterday, 15 October 2026, as “ITRA Day”, with strategic MoUs and collaborative initiatives, expert lectures, discussions on AI and Ayurveda, and institutional honours and awards. ITRA is the country’s first Ayurveda institute to be granted the status of Institute of National Importance, dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 15 October 2020. Over the past six years, its NABH-accredited 300-bed hospital has provided consultation and treatment to 18,47,807 patients through 22 OPDs and treated 27,520 patients in the IPD. The Institute also marked one year of its official TV channel, ANCN, and offers courses in Ayurveda, Ayurveda pharmacy, Yoga and Naturopathy.

The conference reaffirmed the commitment of ITRA to advancing Ayurveda through responsible AI, with tradition and innovation moving forward together.

2324593.title: Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 10th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
2324593.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 10th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
Over 1.93 lakh additional houses approved under the scheme, total houses sanctioned reach 20.80 lakh
Empowering Women, Strengthening Families: 97% of Houses Allotted in Women’s Name or Joint Ownership
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi

Over 1.93 lakh additional houses were approved under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) during the 10th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held in New Delhi on 16th October 2026 under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA); Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary and Financial Advisor (JS&FA); Shri Vaibhav Rundwal, Director, HFA, officials from the Ministry; and Mission Directors, representatives from the participating 11 States were among those present in the meeting.

With the approval of 1.93 lakh additional houses, the cumulative number of houses sanctioned under the Mission is now at 20.80 lakh. In today’s meeting, houses have been sanctioned under Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh (6,560 houses), Bihar (52,866 houses), Chhattigarh (4,670 houses), Gujarat (14,290 houses), Karnataka (3,116 houses), Mizoram (1,003 houses), Odisha (3,126 houses), Sikkim (29 houses), Telangana (18,120 houses), Uttar Pradesh (73,182 houses) and West Bengal (16,559 houses) for eligible urban families belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).

During the meeting, the Committee discussed measures to accelerate the implementation of PMAY-U 2.0, with emphasis on timely approvals, effective monitoring and delivery of housing benefits to eligible beneficiaries.

Expanding Access to Affordable Housing

Launched in September 2024, PMAY-U 2.0 aims to provide financial assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh each to 1 crore additional urban poor and middle-class families to construct or purchase a pucca house. The scheme extends support to eligible EWS, LIG and MIG families with an annual household income of up to ₹9 lakh.

PMAY-U 2.0 provides assistance through four verticals: Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The verticals cater to different housing needs of citizens as per their eligibility and requirement.

BLC: Eligible families can construct a pucca house on their own land;

AHP: A beneficiary can purchase their own home in public/private housing projects;

ARH: For those requiring affordable rental accommodation in cities; and

ISS: Interest subsidy of up to ₹1.80 lakh is provided to EWS/LIG and MIG families availing housing loans of up to ₹25 lakh.

 

Strengthening Implementation through Cooperative Federalism

During the meeting, Secretary, UD underscored the need for close coordination between the Ministry and States/UTs/ULBs to ensure the timely submission and processing of housing proposals. States/UTs were encouraged to address implementation bottlenecks, strengthen project monitoring, identify eligible beneficiaries and expedite the completion and occupancy of houses under approved projects. He further emphasised that the occupancy of already completed AHP houses under PMAY-U should be expedited to ensure that eligible beneficiaries can avail the benefits for their ease of living.

Focus on Timely Approvals and Regular Monitoring

Further, Secretary, UD highlighted the need for regular meetings, timely submission of proposals and sustained monitoring to facilitate effective implementation of the scheme. He stressed that States/UTs must exercise due diligence while preparing and submitting proposals to ensure completeness, accuracy and compliance with prescribed PMAY-U 2.0 guidelines, thereby avoiding delays and procedural hassles.

He directed States/UTs to work closely with the Ministry to resolve implementation-related issues, address matters requiring intervention and ensure that approved projects progress within the prescribed timelines, enabling eligible beneficiaries to receive the intended benefits of the scheme.

Women-Centric and Inclusive Development

PMAY-U 2.0 prioritises women-led development by providing women of the family with ownership or co-ownership of houses. The approach seeks to strengthen women's financial security, improve their role in household decision-making and provide families with a stronger foundation for long-term stability.

The Mission also seeks to extend the benefits of affordable housing to eligible families from vulnerable and underserved sections of urban society. By facilitating access to formal housing, the scheme contributes to improved living conditions and supports the social and economic well-being of beneficiary households.

Of the 20.80 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0, 20.16 lakh houses (97%) have been allotted to women (ownership or joint ownership).

Further, to promote inclusivity, 1.81 lakh houses have been sanctioned to senior citizens; 3.61 lakh houses for SC beneficiaries, 1.06 lakh for ST beneficiaries and 9.14 lakh for OBC beneficiaries, reaffirming the scheme’s commitment to equitable access to safe, affordable and dignified housing.

Towards the Goal of ‘Housing for All’

The approval of 20.80 lakh houses under PMAY-U 2.0 represents continued progress towards the Mission's objective of extending affordable housing support to eligible urban families. Overall, under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, more than 1.27 crore houses have been sanctioned by the Government while 1.01 crore houses are already completed.

PMAY-U 2.0 continues to turn the vision of ‘Housing for All’ into reality, bringing millions of urban families closer to a secure home, a dignified life and a brighter future.

2324581.title: INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS SAMARTHAK, THE FIRST INDIGENOUS MULTI-PURPOSE VESSEL
2324581.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS SAMARTHAK, THE FIRST INDIGENOUS MULTI-PURPOSE VESSEL
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Samarthak, the first of class Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs), was commissioned into the Indian Navy on 16 Oct 2026. The ceremony was presided over by the Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri Chandrapuram Ponnusamy Radhakrishnan, in the presence of Adm Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff. The Hon’ble ​M​inister for Labour and Employment, Govt of Karnataka, along with senior naval and defence officials and dignitaries from the Ministry of Defence, also graced the occasion. Key representatives of Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) and OEMs associated with indigenous equipment were also present during the commissioning ceremony.

Designed and constructed by L&T Shipyard, INS Samarthak marks a significant milestone in India’s indigenous shipbuilding journey as the first major warship to be built by an Indian private shipyard. The commissioning is a powerful testament to the growing maturity and capability of the nation’s private shipbuilding industry and reflects the deepening synergy between the Indian Navy and the Indian shipbuilding industry in advancing the national vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

Conceived as a versatile platform for trials and evaluation, INS Samarthak embodies the enhanced technological and operational capabilities of the Indian Navy in the 21st century. With over 75% indigenous content, the Ship incorporates extensive modular construction and pre-outfitting, significantly optimising the build process and construction timelines. The project has also contributed to employment generation, capability development and plough back into the Indian economy.

Aptly named Samarthak, meaning ‘The Proponent’, the ship represents the spirit of a dependable enabler, capable of supporting multiple missions and has been designed with inherent versatility and adaptability, enabling it to undertake diverse range of operational and developmental tasks. True to its name, INS Samarthak is capable of undertaking maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, offshore patrolling, and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief operations, as required.

Addressing the gathering, the Chief Guest underscored the strategic significance of indigenously built naval platforms in strengthening the country’s maritime capabilities and enhancing the Indian Navy’s ability to undertake an increasingly wide spectrum of operational and testing missions. The commissioning of INS Samarthak reinforces the nation’s commitment to maritime security, regional stability and cooperative engagement across the Indian Ocean Region. The ship epitomises India’s sustained pursuit of a self-reliant and resilient domestic defence industrial ecosystem.

The induction of INS Samarthak significantly strengthens India's ability for testing and training new sensors and weapons developed indigenously by domestic industry. The ship’s versatility is an advantage in an unpredictable maritime environment, given the rise of non-traditional maritime threats.

2324557.title: CAQM expands PTZ Camera-based Remote Monitoring to all Industries covered under Direction No. 98 in NCR
2324557.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2324557.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM expands PTZ Camera-based Remote Monitoring to all Industries covered under Direction No. 98 in NCR
PTZ Cameras to be installed by 30th November 2026
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has strengthened the mechanism for remote monitoring of air-polluting industries in the National Capital Region (NCR) by extending the requirement for installation and operationalization of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras to all categories of industries covered under Statutory Direction No. 98. This will expand the scope of technology-enabled monitoring of fuel usage, industrial emissions and compliance with prescribed pollution-control measures. The Order supersedes the Commission’s earlier Order dated 05.10.2026.

The Commission has directed that all 17 categories of highly polluting industries identified by CPCB, Red Category (Medium and Large) air-polluting industries, Food & Food Processing and Textile industries having boilers/ thermic fluid heaters, and Metal industries having furnaces, operating in NCR, shall ensure compliance with the following requirements:

(i) Installation and positioning of PTZ cameras

  • PTZ cameras shall be installed at all fuel-feeding/charging points of boilers, thermic fluid heaters, furnaces, kilns and other fuel-fired industrial equipment, as applicable, to facilitate monitoring of fuel usage during operations.
  • In industrial units using gaseous fuels, PTZ cameras shall be suitably positioned to capture the gas meters/gauges and associated metering arrangements, ensuring adequate visibility for monitoring purposes.
  • Industrial units shall ensure installation of PTZ cameras for monitoring stack emissions and OCEMS sampling/port-hole locations.
  • Industrial units shall also ensure installation of PTZ cameras for monitoring fume extraction system areas, wherever applicable.
  • The number, location and field of view of the cameras shall be adequate to cover the relevant areas and operations effectively, without significant blind spots. Where a single camera cannot adequately cover the prescribed locations, additional cameras shall be installed.

(ii) Real-time video monitoring and connectivity

  • All PTZ cameras installed pursuant to the Order shall be provided with facilities for continuous, real-time transmission of video feeds through Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) to the designated servers/portals of CPCB and the respective SPCBs/DPCC.
  • Industrial units shall ensure that the cameras and associated communication systems remain functional and that video feeds are accessible to the concerned regulatory authorities for remote monitoring.
  • The cameras shall be installed and maintained in a manner that provides adequate image clarity and visibility of the relevant operations, including during night-time operations, wherever applicable.

(iii) Power backup and maintenance

  • All industrial units shall ensure adequate and uninterrupted power supply, including suitable power backup, for the PTZ cameras, communication equipment and associated connectivity systems.
  • Industrial units shall be responsible for the proper operation, maintenance and timely restoration of the cameras and connectivity arrangements in the event of any malfunction or disruption.
  • Any prolonged disruption in video transmission or malfunctioning shall be promptly reported to the concerned SPCB/DPCC, along with the corrective action undertaken.

(iv) Compliance timeline

All industrial units covered under this Order shall ensure installation and operationalization of the requisite PTZ cameras, including arrangements for real-time transmission of video feeds, by 30.11.2026.

CPCB, in coordination with the respective SPCBs/ DPCC, shall ensure necessary technical arrangements, including designated portals, servers and associated infrastructure for receiving and accessing real-time video feeds from industries. The respective SPCBs/ DPCC shall monitor compliance and ensure its effective implementation in their respective jurisdictions.

The respective State Governments of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and the GNCTD, along with CPCB and the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC, shall ensure effective implementation of the Order. The requirements under the Order shall be in addition to the existing directions relating to emission standards, use of approved fuels, OCEMS and other pollution-control measures prescribed by the Commission, CPCB and other authorities under applicable environmental laws.

Industrial emissions, including particulate matter (PM) released through stacks and fugitive emissions arising from various industrial processes, contribute significantly to air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR). Besides directly increasing particulate matter concentrations, and industrial emissions also contribute to the formation of secondary particulate matter, adversely affecting ambient air quality. The impact of such emissions becomes prominent during the winter months, when adverse meteorological conditions restrict the dispersion of pollutants.

The Commission has been undertaking several measures to mitigate industrial air pollution, including transition to cleaner fuels, prohibition of polluting fuels and prescription of stringent emission standards from time to time. The Flying Squads of the Commission, during inspections of industrial units across NCR, have reported instances of use of unapproved fuels, indicating the need for strengthening compliance monitoring and surveillance mechanisms. Accordingly, the monitoring mechanism has been further strengthened with this order.

2324555.title: CAQM team visits Punjab’s Moga District to review Enforcement Measures during Paddy Harvesting Season 2026
2324555.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2324555.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM team visits Punjab’s Moga District to review Enforcement Measures during Paddy Harvesting Season 2026
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level delegation of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), led by Dr. T.S. Panwar, Member (Technical), visited Punjab’s Moga district today to review the ground-level implementation of measures to prevent stubble burning during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.

The delegation held discussions with district officials and undertook field visits to selected hotspot villages in Moga to assess the prevailing situation, review the preparedness of the district administration and assess coordination among the departments concerned.

During the visit, the delegation reviewed the measures being undertaken for effective in-situ and ex-situ management of paddy residue, including the availability and deployment of CRM machinery, field-level surveillance and coordination among the concerned stakeholders.

The CAQM team also assessed the implementation of preventive measures at hotspot locations and emphasised the need for continuous monitoring, effective field-level coordination and timely action to prevent stubble burning incidents during the ongoing harvesting season. The visit is part of CAQM’s continued monitoring and review of paddy harvesting season management measures in hotspot districts of Punjab.

2324548.title: Union Minister Shri Hardeep Singh Puri Addresses Valedictory Session of SRCC’s Centenary Conclave ‘Pathways to Viksit Bharat’
2324548.body_html:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Union Minister Shri Hardeep Singh Puri Addresses Valedictory Session of SRCC’s Centenary Conclave ‘Pathways to Viksit Bharat’
Union Minister calls upon youth to convert challenges in energy, finance, and logistics into productive enterprises for Viksit Bharat @2047
Union Minister urges students to build Indian institutions and global enterprises capable of earning international trust.
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, delivered the Valedictory Address at the two day National Conference titled ‘Pathways to Viksit Bharat: A Centenary Conclave’, organized by Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), University of Delhi, at the Stein Auditorium, India Habitat Centre, New Delhi today.

Addressing distinguished faculty members, economic experts, policymakers and students, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri reflected on the critical interplay between continuity and change in India's developmental journey. Commemorating SRCC’s centenary year, the Minister emphasized how the institution founded during colonial rule, now prepares young Indians to lead global enterprises and shape public policy in a nation of vastly expanded possibilities.

Invoking philosopher Alfred North Whitehead, Shri Puri remarked, “The task of a university is to weld together imagination and experience. An institution that sustains this exchange keeps renewing its intellectual life. That is how knowledge advances and how societies acquire the capacity to change.” He urged students to leverage their academic training in commerce and economics to exercise critical judgment, question assumptions and transform practical challenges into productive enterprises.

The Government of India has approved the Samudra Manthan Scheme (National Offshore Exploration Scheme) with an outlay of ₹84,084 crore. This scheme aims to unlock India's vast offshore hydrocarbon potential and strengthen energy security. It focuses on accelerating exploration, deploying modern technology, creating shared infrastructure, and strengthening domestic manufacturing.

Focusing on the energy sector and sustainable economic development, Shri Puri cited the GOBARdhan scheme launched on 1 October, underscoring Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Waste to Wealth’ and ‘Annadata to Urjadata’. He stated that converting agricultural residue and organic waste into domestic energy is a practical commercial opportunity that serves farmers, generates economic returns and strengthens national energy security.

Highlighting India’s resilience amidst global economic turbulence and geopolitical disruptions, the Minister noted that India successfully maintained the continuity of essential fuel supplies during recent West Asian crises by diversifying energy sources and bolstering domestic capacities.

Reiterating Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call during his recent visit to SRCC, Shri Puri asked the young audience why Indian enterprises should not lead the world when Indian talent already leads major global corporations. He challenged the youth to build world-class Indian institutions and enterprises rooted in reliability, innovation, and international trust.

Concluding his address, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri expressed firm confidence that the youth entering their professional prime will drive India towards becoming a developed nation Viksit Bharat by 2047. The two-day Centenary Conclave brought together leading policymakers, economists, and students to deliberate on policy priorities, financial coordination and economic growth pathways for India's future.

2324520.title: AIIA Marks a Decade of Service with Over 37.74 Lakh Patients Treated Across Its Healthcare Network
2324520.body_html:
AYUSH
AIIA Marks a Decade of Service with Over 37.74 Lakh Patients Treated Across Its Healthcare Network
Decade-Long Journey Highlights Expanding Clinical Services, Research and Quality Education in Ayurveda
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, has released a report highlighting its achievements over the past decade, documenting the expansion of its clinical services and healthcare outreach. According to the report, a total of 37,74,524 patients received healthcare services across the institute’s main campus and affiliated and outreach centres between October 2016 and September 2026. The milestone reflects the institute’s growing clinical reach and its continued efforts to strengthen Ayurveda-based healthcare through quality patient care, education and research.

Of the total patients served, approximately 30,37,077 received healthcare services at AIIA’s main campus in Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. The institute’s clinical infrastructure includes outpatient department (OPD) services with the capacity to attend to approximately 3,000 patients daily and a 200-bed inpatient department (IPD), enabling it to cater to a large and diverse patient population.

Beyond its main campus, AIIA has expanded its healthcare outreach through its satellite centre in Goa and affiliated and outreach facilities at Safdarjung Hospital, the UPSC Building, the National Cancer Institute at Jhajjar, the IAS Training Centre in Mussoorie, and Kevadia, Ekta Nagar. These centres collectively served approximately 7.37 lakh patients during the reporting period, extending the reach of the institute’s clinical services to more people.

According to AIIA Director Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, public interest in Ayurveda increased significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic and in the subsequent years. He noted that patient footfall at the institute had increased more than fourfold, reflecting the growing demand for Ayurveda-based consultations and treatment. The institute attended to approximately 1.23 lakh patients in 2020, with the number rising to over 5.40 lakh by September 2026.

The release of the decade-long report on Foundation Day, alongside the organisation of KAUMARACON-2026, underscores AIIA’s focus on expanding access to clinical services while strengthening the role of Ayurveda through scientific research, quality education and institutional collaboration. The institute continues to work towards integrating traditional medical knowledge with contemporary healthcare approaches and advancing evidence-informed practices in Ayurveda.

The All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi, is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. It is dedicated to advancing healthcare, education, research and innovation in Ayurveda, while promoting the national and international recognition of India’s traditional systems of medicine.

2324508.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Meets Asian Games 2026 Gold Medal-Winning Indian Women’s Kabaddi Team at Rail Bhawan
Union Minister Congratulates Indian Railways’ Women Sportspersons on Their Gold Medal Victory, Making the Tricolour Proud
Indian Railways Continues to Nurture Sporting Talent Through the Railway Sports Promotion Board
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, today met members of the Indian women’s Kabaddi team at Rail Bhawan, New Delhi. The team won the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

देश की बेटियों ने बढ़ाया तिरंगे का मान🥇🇮🇳 https://t.co/FweYoTpsiv

— Ashwini Vaishnaw (@AshwiniVaishnaw) October 16, 2026

India’s women’s Kabaddi team secured the gold medal after defeating Iran 37-34 in a closely contested final on 26 September 2026, successfully defending its Asian Games title. Union Minister Shri Vaishnaw congratulated Indian Railways’ women sportspersons on their gold medal victory, commending the players for making the Tricolour proud and bringing laurels to the country through their dedication, determination and sporting excellence. The team was coached by Neeta Moreshwar Dadwe and captained by Pushpa Rana.

The Railway sportspersons who met the Minister included Head Coach Neeta Moreshwar Dadwe of South Central Railway; Ritu Negi of South Central Railway; Pooja of Northern Railway; Pinky Roy of South Central Railway; and Sonali Vishnu Shingate and Raj Rani of Western Railway.

Indian Railways has a long record of nurturing sporting talent through the Railway Sports Promotion Board. Its sportspersons have represented India at major international competitions, including the Olympic Games, World Championships, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. Through institutional support and opportunities to pursue sporting careers alongside employment, Indian Railways continues to contribute to the development of sporting talent in the country.

2324497.title: Vice-President Inaugurates Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode
2324497.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Inaugurates Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode
“Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi: India’s progress and cultural heritage are complementary to each other”: Vice-President
“Diverse Traditions, One Dharma: India’s Shared Civilisational Heritage Is Its Enduring Strength”: Vice-President
Navaratri reminds us that courage must overcome fear, righteousness must prevail over injustice, and knowledge must dispel ignorance: Vice-President
Vice-President Releases “Sangha Noottandile Akshara Mudrakal” at Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode, Keralam, and emphasised the importance of preserving India’s rich cultural heritage while advancing on the path of development.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode, Keralam today. Vice President expressed hope that Navaratri Sargotsavam would inspire the youth, encourage artists and strengthen efforts to preserve India’s cultural heritage while embracing innovation. He congratulated Kesari Weekly on organising the festival and commended its contribution to Malayalam journalism, democratic values and freedom of expression.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 16, 2026


Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that Navaratri celebrates the divine feminine power of Adi Parashakti, the eternal source of creation, strength, wisdom and compassion. He observed that the festival’s enduring message is that courage must overcome fear, righteousness must prevail over injustice, and knowledge must dispel ignorance. These timeless values, he said, continue to guide society towards a better future.

Highlighting India’s diverse Navaratri traditions, the Vice-President said that despite the diversity of languages, traditions and forms of worship, the country remains united by its shared civilisational heritage. This, he noted, reflects the spirit of “Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat”.

Emphasising the Prime Minister’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that India’s cultural heritage and developmental aspirations complement each other. Drawing an analogy with the banyan tree, he observed that just as a tree draws strength from its deep roots while spreading its branches, India’s traditions and values provide stability, identity and continuity as the nation embraces modernity and progress.

The Vice-President congratulated Kesari Weekly on organising the festival and commended its contribution to Malayalam journalism, democratic values and freedom of expression.

On the occasion, the Vice-President released the book “Sangha Noottandile Akshara Mudrakal”. He also presented the Sarga Kesari Award to Shri P. R. Rajendran in recognition of his contribution to the fine arts.

Shri Radhakrishnan expressed hope that Navaratri Sargotsavam would inspire the youth, encourage artists and strengthen efforts to preserve India’s cultural heritage while embracing innovation. Praying for the blessings of the Goddesses, he expressed hope that society would find the strength to fight injustice, share prosperity with the underprivileged, and apply knowledge towards building a compassionate society that cares for all.

Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Hon’ble Governor of Keralam and Tamil Nadu; Shri C. Sadanandan Master, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; Smt. Vidhu-bala, President, Navaratri Sargotsavam Samiti; Shri A. K. Prasanth, Working President, Navaratri Sargotsavam Samiti; and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

2324489.title: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 on 19th October 2026 in New Delhi
2324489.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 on 19th October 2026 in New Delhi
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Government of India will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 to 106 young artists in the field of music, dance and drama on 19 October 2026 at 10 a.m. at Meghdoot Complex, Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, will be the Guest of Honour and Dr. Sandhya Purecha, Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi will preside over the award ceremony.

The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar was instituted by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2006 to recognize young artists up to the age of 40. Since then, these awards have been presented annually to young artists at a special ceremony.

 The General Council of Sangeet Natak Akademi, at its meeting held from 22-26 March 2026 at New Delhi unanimously selected 106 young artists for Sangeet Natak Akademi, Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025.   

The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar carries a purse money of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees twenty-five thousand only) besides a Tamrapatra and an Angavastram.

2324475.title: Two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms begins in Dharamshala
2324475.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2324475.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms begins in Dharamshala
Chief Minister, Himachal Pradesh, Secretary, DARPG & Chief Secretary, Himachal Pradesh address the Inaugural Session
Day One highlights Digital Innovation, Emerging Technologies and Citizen-Centric Governance
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms kick-started today in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh, bringing together representatives of the Central, State/UT Governments and experts to deliberate on digital transformation, innovative governance practices and technology-enabled public service delivery.

The inaugural session featured a welcome address by Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG, Government of India, followed by addresses by Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant, Chief Secretary, Government of Himachal Pradesh, and Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh. Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG, delivered the vote of thanks.

In his address, the Chief Minister said, the reforms must be brought about to ensure the welfare of the beneficiaries and modern technology can prove to be a key instrument in addressing the future challenges. He said that the state Government was focusing on good governance and the departments must make earnest efforts to provide quality services to the people of the State nearer to their homes. He applauded Union Minister of State (PP) Dr Jitendra Singh and DARPG for organising the conference in Himachal Pradesh.

Citing nominations received under National Awards for e-Governance and the Prime Minister's Awards, Secretary DARPG in her address highlighted the innovative work done by Districts, States and Ministries to make governance more robust and citizen centric. She underlined that the challenge before the government was to scale up such practices and to take an innovation that works in one place and make it work in many places. She emphasized that closing the distance between a successful pilot and a national practice was the objective of the National Conference.

Expressing gratitude to the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh and the state administration for their support and hospitality in hosting the conference, the Secretary noted the visionary leadership and continuous guidance provided by Union Minister of State (PP) Dr. Jitendra Singh in driving DARPG’s governance initiatives. Acknowledgment was also extended to Union Minister for Health Shri J. P. Nadda. Both the ministers have  conveyed their best wishes for the National Conference.

Chief Secretary of Government of Himachal Pradesh, Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant highlighted how e-governance is enabling citizens to access government services at their doorsteps. He outlined various initiatives undertaken by the Himachal Pradesh government and explained how digital governance is helping reduce procedural hurdles. He emphasised that the objective is to eliminate barriers, promote equality and ensure that public services reach people more efficiently.

The session brought together senior leadership from the Central and State Governments for deliberations on governance reforms and the role of digital innovation in public administration.

The Day One of the Conference showcased five key initiatives of the Government of Himachal Pradesh, including Him Parivar, Sukhashraya, Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK), Green Himachal and the Rajiv Gandhi Van Samvardhan Yojna. The presentations highlighted the range of governance initiatives being undertaken across sectors such as health, social justice, education, environment and forest conservation.

The other sessions featured presentations on award-recognised initiatives demonstrating the use of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in governance. The initiatives included AgriStack, e-Jagriti, the AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support System in e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Service, the Multi Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System and iGOT Karmayogi. The presentations wer  also made on eAarogya Dhamni, the District Court Case Management System (DCMS), ICMR-MINDS, the India Hypertension Control Initiative and Digi Yatra.

Day Two of the conference, scheduled for 17 October 2026, will feature sessions on cybersecurity, best e-governance practices, replication, data analytics, and State-, district- and grassroots-level initiatives, followed by the valedictory session.

The National Conference on e-Governance Reforms seeks to strengthen the exchange of ideas and experiences among government institutions and promote effective, innovative and citizen-centric governance through digital transformation.

2324472.title: PM-AJAY Drives Inclusive Development Through Adarsh Grams, Socio-Economic Projects and Educational Infrastructure
2324472.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
PM-AJAY Drives Inclusive Development Through Adarsh Grams, Socio-Economic Projects and Educational Infrastructure
18,093 villages declared Adarsh Grams; Approximately Rs 1,730 Crore released under Grant In Aid directly to States And Districts
785 student hostels completed; Rs 61.46 Crore Allocated For FY 2026-27 for two hostel projects Accommodating 264 Boys/ Girls Students
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Adarsh Gram component of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, over 47,200 villages benefiting more than 47.79 lakh citizens across the country, have been covered. In addition, a total of 46,944 development works have been completed, while 27,032 Village Development Plans (VDPs) have been prepared, under the PM AJAY.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said as on September 8, 2026, 18,093 villages had been declared Adarsh Grams which reflects continued efforts of the Ministry to improve infrastructure, basic services and the quality of life in Scheduled Caste-majority villages.

He said the Scheduled Caste-dominated villages are being developed as model villages by addressing critical gaps in infrastructure and essential services and an ‘Adarsh Gram’ is envisioned as a village where people have access to basic services, the minimum needs of all sections of society are met and disparities are reduced to a minimum.

The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry, is advancing the socio-economic and educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities through infrastructure development, livelihood promotion, education and improved access to basic services.

The Official informed that the Scheme has three components including development of Scheduled Caste-dominated villages into ‘Adarsh Grams’, Grants-in-Aid for socio-economic projects at the State and District levels, and construction and repair of hostels.

He stated that the Grants-in-Aid component provides financial assistance for district and State-level projects aimed at the socio-economic advancement of Scheduled Castes. It focuses on increasing the income of the target population through comprehensive livelihood projects, skill development and related infrastructure, he added.

He said it also seeks to improve socio-economic development indicators by creating adequate infrastructure in Scheduled Caste-dominated villages and to promote literacy and school enrolment among Scheduled Caste students through residential schools wherever required.

The Official said an approximately Rs 1,730 Crore was released directly to States under this component during FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26. The support has extended skilling and livelihood opportunities to more than 2.5 lakh individual and group beneficiaries, he added.

The Official further said under the PM-AJAY’s component of construction and repair of hostels, the Ministry pursues enabling and encouraging Scheduled Caste students to pursue quality education as these hostels are particularly beneficial for students from rural and remote areas by providing access to accommodation and educational opportunities.

He said as of September 2026, a total of 785 student hostels had been completed under the scheme. For FY 2026-27, the Government has allocated Rs 61.46 crore in central assistance for two hostel projects—one for girls and one for boys—which will provide accommodation for 264 students, he further said.

The Ministry Official further said a major step towards strengthening implementation and monitoring has been the launch of the PM-AJAY Mobile App and PM-AJAY Portal, facilitating a transition from paper-based workflows to end-to-end digital processing on a real-time basis.

He said technology-enabled governance is strengthening information access, monitoring and data-driven decision-making under the scheme while as the digital framework is also aimed at improving coordination, transparency, accountability and efficiency in the delivery of welfare interventions.

The Official further stated that PM-AJAY is a 100 per cent Centrally Funded Scheme, while States and Union Territories may supplement it with additional resources wherever required. Under the funding framework, up to 50 per cent of funds may be utilised for gap-filling activities in selected Adarsh Gram villages. Up to 5 per cent is allocated for setting up and operating Technical Support Groups and Project Implementation Units at the Central, State and District levels. Up to 2 per cent is earmarked for construction and repair of hostels, including support for Central Institutions, while the remaining funds are provided as Grants-in-Aid for projects at the District and State levels.

Grants-in-Aid allocations take into account factors including the Scheduled Caste population and the ratio of State SCSP to the Annual Plan in relation to the Scheduled Caste population of States and Union Territories. Following completion of infrastructure projects, their maintenance and operation are to be undertaken by the concerned State Governments or implementing agencies. Under the hostel component, the Government of India also provides central assistance for maintenance.

As India progresses towards Viksit Bharat @2047, ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society remains central to the nation’s development journey.

PM-AJAY contributes to this objective by addressing multiple dimensions of empowerment—from village infrastructure and basic services to livelihoods, skill development and access to education.

With greater use of technology, stronger monitoring mechanisms and focused last-mile delivery, the scheme continues to strengthen opportunities for Scheduled Caste communities to participate more fully in India’s growth and development. Its integrated approach is helping create the infrastructure, capabilities and enabling environment required for individuals and communities to realise their full potential.

2324455.title: ECL generates ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal under Special Campaign 6
2324455.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
ECL generates ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal under Special Campaign 6
62,720 sq. ft. of space cleared; over 3,000 e-files reviewed
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, has generated revenue of ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal and cleared 62,720 square feet of space under Special Campaign 6, aimed at improving workplace cleanliness, resource utilisation and administrative efficiency.

According to the progress report for October 2–16, the Coal India subsidiary disposed of 413.5 metric tonnes of scrap against an identified quantity of 850 metric tonnes. The disposal of iron scrap on October 14 generated ₹2,21,31,359, contributing to resource recovery and the productive utilisation of obsolete materials.

The company has undertaken cleanliness activities at 10 identified locations, clearing 62,720 sq. ft. of space against a target of 2,08,052 sq. ft., achieving around 30 per cent of the targeted area.

On the administrative front, ECL reviewed 647 physical files against a target of 1,200 and weeded out 567 obsolete files against a target of 1,000. The exercise aims to reduce redundant records, optimise office space and strengthen records management.

Significant progress was also recorded in digital file management, with 3,098 e-files reviewed against a target of 3,800, representing over 81 per cent achievement. Of the 3,600 e-files identified for closure, 2,148 have been closed, achieving nearly 60 per cent of the target.

The campaign forms part of ECL's broader efforts to institutionalise cleanliness, streamline administrative processes and promote the efficient utilisation of resources across its establishments.

2324440.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and inhuman treatment of a woman by her husband and family members enraged by her living with another man in Surendranagar district, Gujarat
2324440.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and inhuman treatment of a woman by her husband and family members enraged by her living with another man in Surendranagar district, Gujarat
Notices issued to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Sundranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a married woman, who had been living with another man, was subjected to cruel and inhuman treatment by her husband and family in Surendranagar district, Gujarat. Reportedly, the woman and the man were tracked and brought back under the guise of conducting a 'purification ritual'. The woman was beaten with sticks, kicked and tied to a tree. The accused also allegedly forced the man accompanying her to rape her.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Accordingly, it has issued notices to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Surendranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her.

According to the media report, carried on 8th October 2026, the incident came to light when the video of the incident was circulated on social media.

2324436.title: NHRC, India takes <i>suo motu<i/> cognizance of the reported injuries to three students after a portion of the ceiling plaster of a classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government school in Udaipur district, Rajasthan
2324436.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported injuries to three students after a portion of the ceiling plaster of a classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government school in Udaipur district, Rajasthan
Issues a notice to the Udaipur District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the health status of the injured students
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that three students, aged 7 to 8 years, were injured when a portion of the ceiling plaster of their classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government primary school building in Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Reportedly, the victims sustained head injuries and teachers were not present in the school when the incident occurred. The injured students walked home on their own and their family members subsequently took them to the hospital for treatment.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Udaipur District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the health status of the injured students.

According to the media report carried on 7th October 2026, the school was ordered to close after the incident and alternate arrangements are being made by the authorities for conducting classes. Reportedly, the school building was last repaired in 2020.

2324416.title: NHAI Successfully Defends Arbitration Case in Chittorgarh–Udaipur National Highway Project to Safeguard Public Funds
2324416.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Successfully Defends Arbitration Case in Chittorgarh–Udaipur National Highway Project to Safeguard Public Funds
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

Achieving a significant legal victory, NHAI has successfully defended its contractual position in an arbitration case against concessionaire Uchit Expressway Private Limited, promoted by TRIL Roads Pvt. Ltd. for six-laning of the 93.5 km long Chittorgarh-Udaipur section of NH-76 in Rajasthan. The Arbitral Tribunal substantially upheld the position of NHAI, thereby safeguarding public resources and reaffirming the contractual framework governing National Highway projects.

The three-member Arbitral Tribunal under the Society for Affordable Redressal of Disputes (SAROD), examined claims and counterclaims arising out of the concession agreement for the project. The Tribunal rejected overall concessionaire claims of Rs. 366.53 crores, which included Rs. 238.18 crore of prolongation cost claim tied to COVID-19 by the concessionaire. After detailed consideration, the Tribunal rejected the claim for prolongation cost and allowed claims amounting to only Rs. 14.51 crore along with conditional refund of Rs. 2.82 Crores to the concessionaire. 

In addition, the Tribunal awarded Rs. 33.54 crore (principal) in counter-claims to NHAI. This ruling in favour of NHAI includes Rs. 27 crore for recovery of work dropped from the project scope, Rs. 4.03 crore toward failure to maintain the highway and Rs. 2.51 crore towards unauthorized toll collected after the completion date of the project, in March 2021.

In a series of recent notable legal wins, NHAI has successfully defended various arbitration cases. In July 2026, NHAI successfully defended claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL).Similarly, in June 2026, arbitration case related to Tumkur–Chitradurga 6 laning Project in Karnataka, was awarded in favour of NHAI for Rs. 1,202 crores. Also in April 2026, two arbitration cases in Panipat–Jalandhar Highway Project involving Concessionaire’s claims of around Rs. 8,375 Crores and counterclaims of NHAI for Rs. 2,888.64 Crores were settled for Rs. 819.96 Crores in favour of NHAI. Similarly in May 2026, arbitration case related to 6 laning of Kamrej–Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat in which claims of around Rs. 174.49 crore raised by the contractor, was settled for only Rs. 54 lakhs by the Arbitral Tribunal.

The successful resolution of arbitration cases reflects NHAI’s commitment to sound contractual management and effective legal strategy. It also reaffirms NHAI’s focus on the proper utilization of public funds, while upholding transparency, accountability and contractual discipline in the development and management of National Highway infrastructure.
