"Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is also the success of crores of citizens of the country,” affirmed PM Modi.

Remembering former President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam on his birth anniversary, the Prime Minister paid rich tributes to the late statesman. He highlighted how Dr. Kalam's remarkable life and visionary outlook continue to guide the nation. "His life and his vision are an inspiration for all of us,” remarked Shri Modi.

Recalling the historic milestones achieved at the Asian Games, the Prime Minister celebrated the double Gold victory of the men's and women's hockey teams, with the women ending a 44-year wait, alongside consecutive medals for both cricket teams and dual Golds in Kabaddi. He also lauded the five Golds in archery, stellar displays in shooting, boxing, and wrestling, new athletics records, a weightlifting medal after 28 years, and the first marathon success since 1982. "This time the Asian Games have been memorable for us in many ways,” noted PM Modi.

Applauding the extraordinary contribution of female athletes who secured 38 of India's 85 total medals, including 11 Golds, the Prime Minister stated that their tally represents far more than mere statistics and reflects an empowered New India. He also highlighted how Indian players scripted history by winning maiden Asian Games medals in disciplines like mixed martial arts, soft tennis, and specific sailing events. "Today India is winning medals even in those sports in which we had never won a medal in the history of the Asian Games before,” observed Shri Modi.

Calling upon the athletes to scale even greater heights in the sporting arena, the Prime Minister led an energetic pledge where the contingent chanted "We will Do it!" in unison. He rallied them to uphold the Tricolor's glory on every field, forge a new sporting identity for the nation, and create new champions across every discipline. "More new records in our name, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.

Drawing attention to the venue of the gathering, the Prime Minister reminded the athletes that the stadium is named after the legendary Major Dhyan Chand, who famously practiced hockey for hours into the night. He pointed to the icon's relentless dedication to illustrate that grand resolutions require years of sustained patience and hard work. "This hard work of his reminds us time and again that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day,” remarked Shri Modi.

Contrasting the past dozen years of diligent work on the sports ecosystem with an earlier era when India won only a handful of medals and remained unaware of many disciplines, the Prime Minister recalled how the nation previously had zero representation in over half the Olympic events. He questioned how the country could ever expect to win laurels without first stepping onto the field of competition. "If we do not even compete, how will we bring medals?” remarked PM Modi.

Highlighting a decisive shift in national sporting policy, the Prime Minister emphasized the government's firm determination to eradicate this historic apathy and self-doubt. He celebrated the resulting surge in Indian athletes competing across international arenas today. "We took this resolution that we will remove this pessimistic mindset!” asserted Shri Modi.

Attributing this transformation to a far-reaching vision and sincere effort over the last 10 to 12 years, the Prime Minister detailed the creation of a transparent, modern sports ecosystem anchored by the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and the expanded Khelo India initiative. He pointed out that the government has committed massive financial resources to strengthen sports federations and grassroots programs across the country. "To expand Khelo India and strengthen sports federations, more than 36 thousand crore rupees were allocated,” noted PM Modi.

Detailing the rapid expansion of grassroots infrastructure across over a thousand Khelo India Centers, the Prime Minister listed thousands of new stadiums, multi-purpose halls, athletics tracks, football and hockey grounds, and swimming pools being built across cities of all sizes. He also highlighted direct financial support to athletes, including a 50,000-rupee monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance under TOPS and funding for international coaching stints. "If there is a need to go outside the country for coaching in any sport, the government is facilitating that too and providing financial assistance for it,” observed Shri Modi.

Underscoring the drive to maximize competitive exposure through the Winter Games, Sansad Khel Pratiyogitas, and the new 'Khelo Bharat Niti', the Prime Minister also praised Divyang athletes for bringing laurels to the nation. He noted that the athletes' own triumphs prove what happens when players know the entire nation backs their journey. "Today every player has this confidence that the country stands with them throughout their entire journey,” affirmed PM Modi.

Spotlighting the remarkable performances of 15-to-17-year-old athletes in the contingent as proof that starting young provides an added advantage, the Prime Minister outlined a targeted focus on identifying and training children aged five to fifteen through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India. Looking ahead to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, India's hosting of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, and the aspiration to host the 2036 Olympics, he recalled his Red Fort announcement of a nationwide village-level talent hunt. "These very players will bring medals for India in the times to come,” asserted Shri Modi.

Expressing unwavering confidence in the nation's grand resolutions, the Prime Minister led another spirited "We will Do it!" chant with the athletes. He rallied them around the shared goals of hosting major global sporting events, joining the ranks of top sporting nations, building world-class infrastructure, and becoming a global sports hub. "A champion from every corner of India, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.

Connecting the Asian Games triumph to the broader aspirations of Indian youth, the Prime Minister noted how young innovators have propelled India into the world's third-largest startup ecosystem while pioneering breakthroughs in space, satellite technology, defense, and Artificial Intelligence. He emphasized that just like in sports, youth from small towns and villages are driving this entrepreneurial wave, backed by a decade of systemic reforms that assure them of the nation's full support. "They have the trust that to take their dreams forward, the entire capability of the country stands with them,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Expanding on the broader economic impact of the sporting boom, the Prime Minister pointed out that government initiatives are benefiting far more than just on-field competitors. He highlighted the rapid emergence of diverse professional fields such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. "This has created new avenues of employment and enterprise for the youth,” noted PM Modi.

Urging the internationally experienced medalists to shoulder the responsibility of mentoring the next generation, the Prime Minister asked them to visit schools, return to their original playing grounds, and engage with children in their home villages and cities. He emphasized that sharing their hard-earned experiences could profoundly inspire young aspirants dreaming of following in their footsteps. "Perhaps, a small word from you might give a child the courage to move ahead in sports,” remarked Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the deeper value of athletics beyond the playing field, the Prime Minister stated that sports instill lifelong discipline, adaptability, steadfastness toward long-term goals, and the resilience to rise after a defeat. He noted that these foundational qualities naturally integrate into daily life to guide individuals through every challenge. "This very sportsperson spirit comes in handy throughout life,” observed PM Modi.

Concluding his address with his signature maxim that "one who plays, will flourish," the Prime Minister praised the athletes' enthusiasm as New India's greatest strength and led a final "We will Do it!" chant encompassing the goals of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, a top-three economy, an Aatmanirbhar Bharat, a global manufacturing hub, technology leadership, space exploration, and hosting the Olympics. He extended his best wishes for all their future tournaments and endeavors. "With this very self-confidence, we have to take India to new heights,” asserted Shri Modi.

2324066.title: SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026-Mysuru
2324066.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026-Mysuru
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale Visits SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 in Mysuru
Highlights Government Initiatives for Economic Empowerment
Mela Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
12 States And Union Territories Partcipating in the Mela
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Nine-day SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026, organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is continuing at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, in Karnataka since October 11. The Mela will conclude on October 19 Monday.

A Senior Official in the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) said the Mela provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.

He said the Mela has been jointly organized by three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.

Union Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale during his visit to SHILP SAMAGAM MELA highlighted the Central Government’s commitment to the economic and social empowerment of socially disadvantaged and vulnerable sections.

The Minister was informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.

The Minister visited and inspected stalls with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

Addressing a press conference at the Government Guest House in Mysuru earlier, Shri Athawale said that the Central Government has introduced various welfare and development schemes to promote the economic and social empowerment of Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, sanitation workers, transgender persons and persons with disabilities, including persons with visual impairments. He highlighted the role of the National Development Corporations in extending concessional financial assistance, with loans ranging from ₹1.5 Lakh To ₹35 Lakh under various schemes, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and scheme provisions.

 

Emphasizing the Government’s commitment to social welfare, the Minister stated that ₹1.98 Lakh Crore had been allocated for social welfare schemes in the Union Budget, out of a total budget of ₹ 57 Lakh Crore.

Shri Athawale also referred to the constitutional provisions for reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the provision of 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes following the recommendations of the Mandal Commission, and the subsequent introduction of 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections.

Highlighting the reach of flagship welfare initiatives, Shri Athawale referred to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, under which around four crore beneficiaries have received benefits across the country, including approximately 10 lakh beneficiaries in Karnataka. He also highlighted the contribution of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana in expanding financial inclusion, stating that 2,22,23,000 bank accounts had been opened in Karnataka under the scheme.

Referring to educational assistance in Mysuru district, the Minister stated that approximately 13,000 students studying in Classes I to VIII and 31,000 post-matric students had benefited from educational support. He further noted that nearly 75 per cent of the 7,000 students residing in 84 government hostels in the district belonged to Scheduled Castes. Eligible beneficiaries were also receiving monthly stipends of ₹1,850 for college students and ₹1,750 for high school students, he said.

The Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills.

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.

The Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

In addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.

The Ministry has been organizing SHILP SAMAGAM MELAS since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.

The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first SHILP SAMAGAM MELA of the financial year 2026–27.

The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati, Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 will continue at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans. Through such initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

2324061.title: English rendering of PM’s address during interaction with the participants of Asian Games 2026
2324061.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address during interaction with the participants of Asian Games 2026
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Sports Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji, Minister of State for Sports Sister Raksha Khadse ji, all of you young athletes, coaches, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Coming among all of you fills me with energy as well. So many medal winners gathered together, and meeting all of them at once, is no ordinary thing. It is a very pleasant feeling. All of you young athletes are examples of how, when passion is transformed into victory, it brings not only medals but also a glow on the face. And, of course, it makes the nation shine as well.

Friends,

You have given 1.4 billion countrymen an opportunity to feel proud. Because the greatest achievement, if there is one, is to enhance the honour of the Tiranga. You have enhanced the pride of the Tiranga, you have increased its honour. Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is the success of millions and millions of citizens of this country. On behalf of all the people of India, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you. At the same time, I also wholeheartedly congratulate your coaches, your support staff, and your families.

Friends,

Today is also the birth anniversary of our former President, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. His life and his vision are an inspiration to all of us. I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.

Friends,

In many ways, these Asian Games have been memorable for us. Both our men’s and women’s hockey teams are present here today. Both teams won gold medals this time. And especially our women’s hockey team, you ended a long wait of 44 years by bringing home the gold medal. In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time and, in fact, repeated their own record. In kabaddi too, both our men’s and women’s teams won gold medals. Likewise, five gold medals in archery, and where there are five, there is the grace of the Almighty. Outstanding performances in shooting, major successes in boxing and wrestling, new records in athletics, a medal in weightlifting after twenty-eight years, and India’s success in marathon events for the first time since 1982. All this is truly a matter of great joy.

Friends,

I especially want to appreciate our daughters. Out of the 85 medals won by India, 38 medals were won by our women athletes. Among them were 11 gold medals as well. And these medals are not merely numbers; they represent a powerful image of New India. Today, India is winning medals even in sports where, in the history of the Asian Games, we had never before won a medal. In Mixed Martial Arts, Soft Tennis, and certain sailing events, our players created new history by winning medals for the first time.

Friends,

Now we must reach even greater heights in sports. We have to, don't we? We have to achieve even more, don't we? I want to place a few resolutions before you. And all of you must respond with full enthusiasm: We will Do it! So, repeat after me:

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

A new identity for India in sports, We will Do it!

New champions in every sport, We will Do it!

More records in our name, We will Do it!

Friends,

The stadium in which we are gathered today is named after Major Dhyan Chand ji. His dedication towards hockey was so great that he would practise for hours even at night. His hard work repeatedly reminds us that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day. They require years of patience and sustained effort.

Friends,

Over the past 12 years, India too has worked with great patience and dedication on its sportspersons and its sports ecosystem. There was a time when India could win only a handful of medals in major tournaments. In many sports, people in the country did not even know that such sports existed. There used to be huge events such as the Olympics, yet India had no representation in more than half of the sports. Just think about it. If we do not even compete, then where will the medals come from?

Friends,

We took a pledge that we would remove this pessimistic mindset. And the result is that today, our representation is increasing on every global platform.

Friends,

How did this transformation happen? It happened through the same spirit that helped you achieve success. Over the past 10–12 years, the country worked continuously with dedication and sincerity, pursued a long-term vision, and built a transparent and modern ecosystem for sports. As all of you know, we launched the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). We launched the Khelo India Scheme. Over time, its scope was expanded further. As Mansukh Bhai mentioned earlier, more than ₹36,000 crore has been allocated for expanding Khelo India and strengthening sports federations.

Friends,

Today, more than one thousand Khelo India Centres have been established across the country. Stadiums, mini-stadiums, and multi-purpose sports halls have been created. Athletics tracks, football grounds, hockey grounds, swimming pools, and thousands of such sports infrastructures are being built in both small and large cities. Under this scheme, direct assistance is being provided to athletes as well. They are being given Out-of-Pocket Allowances. Under the TOPS scheme, athletes receive ₹50,000 per month. If any sport requires training abroad, the government is facilitating it and providing financial assistance.

Friends,

To ensure that young people get maximum opportunities to play and compete, events such as Winter Games have been launched, and Members of Parliament Sports Competitions have been started. The country created a new Sports Policy and a new Khelo Bharat Policy. Our para-athletes are also enhancing the nation's pride through their talent and capabilities. For them too, better opportunities and modern facilities in sports are being ensured. And that is why every athlete today feels confident that the nation stands beside them throughout their journey. And when an athlete feels that support, what they can achieve for the nation is something all of you yourselves are excellent examples of.

Friends,

This time, many players in Team India at the Asian Games were only 15 to 17 years old. At such a young age, they enhanced the nation’s pride through their outstanding performances. They won the hearts of the people of the country. This shows that age is no barrier to success. In fact, in sports, starting young is an added advantage. That is why our effort is to identify sporting talent from an early age. We are giving special focus to identifying talent among children aged five to fifteen and training them properly. In the coming years, thousands of new athletes will receive opportunities through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India programmes. We must strengthen our preparations for future sporting events. The Los Angeles Olympics will take place in 2028. India will host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. And hosting the Olympics in 2036 is also India’s aspiration. Keeping this in mind, from the Red Fort I spoke about launching a Talent Hunt campaign. Today, talent is being identified in villages across the country and nurtured. These very athletes will bring medals for India in the years ahead.

Friends,

Our dreams are big. Our resolutions are also big. And today, India has the confidence to achieve them. Every Indian has that confidence. Therefore, with complete conviction, I say: 

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

India among the top sporting nations, We will Do it!

India as a global sports hub, We will Do it!

World-class sports infrastructure in India, We will Do it!

A champion from every corner of India, We will Do it!

Friends,

Our success at the Asian Games is also an example of India’s changing mindset. It shows how today’s youth are impatient to scale every height. There is no summit higher than the determination of India’s youth. There is no goal beyond the capability of our youth power. The limitless sky of possibilities lies before us, and India’s youth are themselves deciding the destination. That is why, in a short span of time, India has become the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Our youth are building companies in the space sector. They are working on satellite technology. The same youth are developing new technologies in the defence sector. They are conducting new experiments in Artificial Intelligence. And this transformation is not limited to big cities. Just as talented individuals from remote areas are now getting opportunities in sports, similarly, in startups, research, and other ventures, young people from small cities and villages are coming forward with new ideas. Behind this confidence lies a deep trust. The systems developed by the country over the past decade have given young people confidence that they can dream big. They know that the full strength of the nation stands behind them to help them realise those dreams.

Friends,

The benefits of our efforts are not limited only to athletes who compete on the field. New career opportunities are being created for youth in areas such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. As sports develop, many related professions are also advancing. This has opened new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for young people.

Friends,

Whatever field we may be in today, we must work hard for our own success. At the same time, we must also take responsibility for shaping the next generation. Now you possess the experience of international tournaments. Therefore, I would request that you devote some time to those children who dream of progressing just as you did. You must water their dreams with the sweat of your own efforts. That is how success comes. Whenever you get an opportunity, meet children in your village and your town. Visit different schools. Be sure to visit the grounds where you first began playing. Your experiences can be extremely valuable to those children. Perhaps a single word from you may give a child the courage to move forward in sports.

Friends,

The youth of the country do not draw inspiration from you only in sports. Because the role of sports extends beyond the playing field. Sports teach us discipline in life. They teach us how to rise again after falling. They teach us how to win after losing. Sports teach us how to stay committed to a goal for a long time and how to adapt ourselves to changing circumstances. These lessons become part of our everyday lives. And this sporting spirit serves us throughout our lives.

Friends,

I always say: The one who plays, blossoms. So keep playing, keep blossoming. Once again, my many best wishes to all of you for the upcoming competitions and for all your future efforts. Your enthusiasm and your confidence are the greatest strengths of New India. With this confidence, we must take India to new heights.

So come, once again, with full energy, say with me:

Viksit Bharat, We will Do it!

Viksit Bharat at Twenty Forty Seven, We will Do it!

We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!

Self-Reliant India, We will Do it!

Self-Reliant India, We will Do it!

Global Manufacturing Hub, We will Do it!

Global Manufacturing Hub, We will Do it!

India’s Leadership in Technology, We will Do it!

Steps into Space, We will Do it!

Hosting the Olympics, We will Do it!

Medals in New Sports, We will Do it!

Yes, We will Do it!

Many, many congratulations.

Thank you very much.

2324046.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulates Assam CM and Assam Police for sustained crackdown against narcotics and a decisive blow to drug networks
2324046.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulates Assam CM and Assam Police for sustained crackdown against narcotics and a decisive blow to drug networks
Crackdown against narcotics in Assam has resulted in 945 arrests, 547 cases and drugs seizures worth over ₹182 crore
Action taken against 703 hotspots and attachment of properties worth nearly ₹31 crore under process
Under the Nasha Mukt Bharat vision of PM Modi, the Vision Document on Narcotics Control 2026-29 reaffirms our resolve to dismantle drug networks
Vision Document on Narcotics Control 2026-29 strike at financial foundations of drug networks and safeguard our youth
The fight against drugs will continue with unwavering resolve
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today congratulated Assam Chief Minister Shri Himanta Biswa Sarma and Assam Police for sustained crackdown against narcotics and a decisive blow to drug networks.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah posted on X, "A decisive blow to drug networks! Congratulations to Assam CM Shri Himanta Biswa Sarma Ji and Assam Police for this sustained crackdown, which has resulted in 945 arrests, 547 cases and narcotics seizures worth over ₹182 crore, alongside action against 703 hotspots and attachment of properties worth nearly ₹31 crore under process. Under the Nasha Mukt Bharat vision of PM Modi, the Vision Document on Narcotics Control 2026-29 reaffirms our resolve to dismantle drug networks, strike at their financial foundations and safeguard our youth. The fight against drugs will continue with unwavering resolve."

A decisive blow to drug networks! Congratulations to Assam CM Shri @himantabiswa Ji and Assam Police for this sustained crackdown, which has resulted in 945 arrests, 547 cases and narcotics seizures worth over ₹182 crore, alongside action against 703 hotspots and attachment of properties worth nearly ₹31 crore under process. Under the Nasha Mukt Bharat vision of PM Modi, the Vision Document on Narcotics Control 2026-29 reaffirms our resolve to dismantle drug networks, strike at their financial foundations and safeguard our youth. The fight against drugs will continue with unwavering resolve.

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) October 15, 2026

As part of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, Assam Police conducted a state-wide anti-drug operation on October 12, 2026, following intensive pre-operation action. The campaign resulted in the registration of 547 drug-related cases and the arrest of 945 accused.

Key achievements include:

* Seizure of narcotics and psychotropic substances worth approximately ₹182 crore.

* Execution of 73 non-bailable warrants (NBWs) and apprehension of 47 absconders, including 10 from other northeastern states.

* Raids at over 703 drug hotspots.

* Processing of properties worth approximately ₹31 crore for seizure, attachment or freezing.

* Processing of 157 proposals under Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (PITNDPS)

* Conduct of 2,229 raids under Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), inspection of 3,662 business establishments and surveys of 2,943 educational institutions.

* 1,34,539 litres of liquor, including IMFL, seized or destroyed.

* Organisation of 633 awareness programmes, reaching 1,12,532 citizens and students.

2324043.title: Customs officers detect 148.67 kg hydroponic weed from Bangkok at air cargo complex at IGI Airport
2324043.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Customs officers detect 148.67 kg hydroponic weed from Bangkok at air cargo complex at IGI Airport
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Customs officers of the SIIB branch, Air Cargo Complex Import, New Customs House, New Delhi, have busted one of the biggest smuggling attempts of narcotic substances. acting on locally developed intelligence, officers intercepted a consignment from Bangkok and uncovered a massive haul of green‑colored NDPS substance, suspected to be ganja/marijuana, concealed inside spools of PU Tubes.

The consignment, declared as PU Tubes packed in 19 cartons, was put on hold due to suspected mis‑declaration. on examination in the presence of the importer’s representative, officers found plastic spools containing PU Tubes. When the spools were broken open, hidden cavities revealed packets of compacted green substance wrapped in polythene. such packets were discovered in 15 cartons. preliminary diagnostic tests indicated the material to be ganja/marijuana.

In total, 120 spools concealed 148.67 kg hydroponic weed. The seized narcotics are valued at approximately Rs. 52 crore, with an estimated street value of Rs. 150 crore in India. The contraband, along with concealment and packaging material, has been seized under the NDPS Act, 1985. Further investigation is in progress.

The operation lasted over 72 hours and culminated in the arrest of one person on 15.10.2026, who was produced before the magistrate the same day. Follow‑up searches at five premises across three states have provided vital leads for ongoing investigation. The entire operation was closely monitored by senior customs officers at the level of chief commissioner and principal commissioner, ACC Imports, and supervised by the additional commissioner of Customs, ACC imports.

Driven by huge profits, smugglers attempt to bring such illicit goods into the country. Customs officers remain vigilant and committed to protecting society from the menace of narcotics.

2324042.title: DRI seizes around 6.2 kg foreign-origin gold; busts sophisticated gold smuggling modus operandi through unaccompanied baggage; three arrested
2324042.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes around 6.2 kg foreign-origin gold; busts sophisticated gold smuggling modus operandi through unaccompanied baggage; three arrested
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), as part of its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling, has uncovered a new and sophisticated modus operandi involving the unaccompanied baggage channel. The network relied on insiders, including warehouse personnel, and intermediaries to retrieve smuggled gold from cargo and pass it to the intended recipient.

Based on specific intelligence, officers of Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted an unaccompanied baggage consignment at Air Cargo Complex, Trivandrum . Detailed examination of the baggage resulted in the recovery and seizure of 6.28 kg foreign origin gold valued at Rs. 9.18 crore, ingeniously concealed inside various hardware items.

The gold was concealed inside various hardware items, including a floor spring, metal locks, a grease gun and a door closer. The modus operandi involved, packing these hardware items along with other articles in a trolley secured with a number lock whose combination had been pre decided among the members of the syndicate. The trolley was shipped as unaccompanied baggage from Dubai to Trivandrum. Upon arrival, the warehouse staff member would open the trolley using the pre decided combination, retrieve the hardware items containing the concealed gold, and hand them over to the mediator, who would, in turn, deliver the same to the receiver.

Simultaneous searches conducted in connection with the operation led to the apprehension of three persons allegedly involved in the smuggling syndicate: a warehouse staff member tasked with retrieving the hardware items containing the concealed gold, a Customs Broker acting as a mediator, and a receiver who had travelled to Trivandrum to take delivery of the gold. All the three were arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.  

DRI remains committed to expose novel sophisticated modus operandi and bust the smuggling networks through intelligence led operations.

2324039.title: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) U.P. Unit holds public hearing to address grievances of opium cultivators
2324039.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) U.P. Unit holds public hearing to address grievances of opium cultivators
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) U.P. Unit held a public hearing to address grievances of opium cultivators on October 12, 2026 in the office premises of the District Opium Officer, Barabanki. The hearing was organised to provide quick and easy solutions to problems issues faced by opium cultivators and receive suggestions on making the opium cultivation farmer friendly.

Deputy Narcotics Commissioner addressing farmers and giving clarifications on opium cultivation procedures.

The public hearing was chaired by Deputy Narcotics Commissioner, Lucknow (U.P.), with Assistant Narcotics Commissioner, Lucknow (U.P.) along with other officers of Barabanki Division also present. The cultivators expressed their apprehensions regarding opium cultivation and were apprised of the legal provisions and administrative remedies available to them.

During a public hearing meeting attended by approximately 150 opium cultivators, participating farmers highlighted several operational challenges and administrative concerns. They primarily raised issues pertaining to irrigation difficulties and climatic vagaries associated with the licensing of a single plot, while also pointing out an anomaly in the current practice of village-wise plot licensing, suggesting instead that allocations be based on the mean distance from a farmer's dwelling. Additionally, the cultivators put forward a formal request for an increase in both the overall number of issued licenses and the permissible size of individual cultivation plots, etc.

The concerns, queries, and doubts presented by the farmers were heard carefully and quick solutions, as far as possible, were provided to them and recorded in case of policy matters.

Farmers discussing their issues before CBN officials at the public hearing

Further, the Deputy Narcotics Commissioner informed cultivators that a helpline number will soon be announced during licensing operation 2026-27 at DNC Office, Lucknow to help opium cultivators.

2324037.title: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) and Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) destroy 2.87 Hectares (7.08 Acres) of illicit cannabis (ganja) cultivation in wildlife sanctuary, District Dhule, Maharashtra
2324037.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) and Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) destroy 2.87 Hectares (7.08 Acres) of illicit cannabis (ganja) cultivation in wildlife sanctuary, District Dhule, Maharashtra
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

Specific intelligence developed by Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), indicated that illicit cultivation of cannabis (ganja) was being carried out over a large area within a wildlife sanctuary near village Jamniapani, Shirpur, District Dhule, Maharashtra. Acting on the intelligence, a joint team officers of DRI, and Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), reached the wildlife sanctuary near village Jamniapani, Shirpur, District Dhule, Maharashtra on 14.10.2026.

The team traced illicit cannabis cultivation across five stretches of land in a remote and densely forested area of the sanctuary, covering a total area of 2.87 hectares (7.08 Acres). The operation posed significant challenges due to the inaccessible terrain, wild animals and lack of mobile network connectivity. The officers proceeded with due diligence and necessary safety precautions and successfully completed the operation. After completing all requisite legal formalities, the cannabis crop was destroyed using a rotavator in the presence of officials from the Police and Forest Department. Further investigation is in progress.

Illicit cannabis in wildlife sanctuary near village Jamniapani, Shirpur, District Dhule, Maharashtra

DRI and CBN will continue such destruction operations of illicit cultivation across India and reaffirm their commitment to combating the illegal narcotics trade and fostering a drug-free and safe environment for the future.

2324032.title: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya asks National Sports Federations to strengthen pipeline of champions at Asian Games review meeting
2324032.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2324032.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya asks National Sports Federations to strengthen pipeline of champions at Asian Games review meeting
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, October 15: Union Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya on Thursday called on National Sports Federations (NSFs) to take greater responsibility for India’s sporting performance, following the nation’s 4th place finish at the 2026 Asian Games. Interacting with a plethora of NSF heads, the Hon’ble Minister reiterated the need to work with further synergy to sustain India’s sporting excellence.

Dr. Mandaviya stressed that India needs a continuous pipeline of champions rather than relying on a handful of medal winners. “How long will Mirabai Chanu alone keep winning medals for us? We need to produce 10 more Mirabai Chanus. Every federation must take this responsibility seriously. We have to identify talent, provide the right training and create an environment in which athletes can progress to the highest level,” the Hon’ble Sports Minister said, underlining the need to identify and develop athletes who can sustain India’s medal-winning ambitions across sporting cycles.

Thursday’s NSFs conclave served as a review of India’s Asian Games 2026 performance and a platform to assess preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, the 2030 Commonwealth Games and the 2030 Asian Games in Doha. It was attended by representatives from all major NSFs, including, shooting, athletics, boxing, archery, squash, wushu, and more.

Dr. Mandaviya also emphasised the need for more sports psychologists, sports science experts and high-performance mental trainers, to mitigate the loss of focus that athletes go through when competing on major international stages. He also urged every NSF to introduce more competitions, strengthen athlete preparation, work with dedicated commitment, as well as carry out honest assessment of gaps in performance and administration.

The conclave saw Shri Vineel Krishna, Joint Secretary (Khelo India), present a discussion on the convergence of Khelo India Scheme with NSFs, while Col. N.S. Johal, CEO (TOPS), gave a performance review of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games and the review of preparations for LA Olympics 2028. The revised Assistance to National Sports Federations (ANSF) guidelines booklet was also inaugurated at the conclave.

Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse called for all federations to align their work with the vision of the Khelo India Mission. “Every NSF must ensure that state and district-level federations are also in place and functioning effectively. This work has to be undertaken wholeheartedly, alongside talent identification. Identifying talent is only one part of the process; athletes must also receive the correct training and support to reach their potential,” Smt. Khadse said.

She stressed that NSFs must ensure that state and district-level federations are functioning effectively, alongside their responsibility for identifying talent. “Only through a collective effort can we strengthen athlete preparation, create a better pathway for talent and increase India’s medal tally,” she added.

Secretary (Sports) Shri Hari Ranjan Rao mentioned that India must aim to finish among the top three at the 2030 Asian Games in Doha, while the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India is scheduled to host, should be treated as a major national challenge. “We have to strive to finish third at the Asian Games in Doha. For the 2030 Commonwealth Games, we must break our own record from the 2010 Commonwealth Games and finish among the top three. Since we are hosting the Games, every NSF must take the competition seriously and prepare accordingly. We must treat this as a challenge and work towards it from now,” he said.

Earlier, Shri Rao had described the sporting ecosystem as a four-tyre vehicle that could move forward only if all its components worked together: athletes, coaches, NSFs, and the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports along with the Sports Authority of India (SAI).

2324013.title: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Launches National Strategic Trade Command Centre at Vanijya Bhawan
2324013.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Launches National Strategic Trade Command Centre at Vanijya Bhawan
NSTCC Aims to Strengthen Data-Driven Monitoring, Trade Intelligence and Evidence-Based Decision-Making
NSTCC to Enable Product-Wise and Market-Wise Trade Analysis, Identify Export Opportunities and Strengthen India's Global Trade Positioning
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, launched the National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of Commerce Secretary, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, and Director General, Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Shri Lav Agarwal.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Piyush Goyal lauded NSTCC for enabling data-driven, evidence-based trade decisions. While reviewing the SCOMET (Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) dashboard, in particular, he called for regular meetings of the Inter-Ministerial Committee, weekly if required, to clear the backlog of pending applications and ensure that all applications are cleared expeditiously.

Developed by the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, NSTCC is a strategic initiative aimed at strengthening the monitoring, analysis and governance of India's international trade ecosystem through integrated data analytics and evidence-based decision-making.

The Command Centre has been conceptualised to provide senior policymakers and government officials with a consolidated view of India's trade performance, export promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators. By bringing together information from multiple trade-related systems, NSTCC seeks to facilitate timely identification of emerging trends, operational bottlenecks and areas requiring policy or administrative intervention.

At the core of NSTCC is an integrated analytics and visualisation platform developed to transform trade-related data into actionable insights. NSTCC provides interactive dashboards covering key trade indicators, scheme performance, application pendency, processing timelines, regional trends and compliance-related parameters.

The platform enables users to analyse information across multiple levels, including national trade performance, Regional Authorities, schemes, products, destination markets and individual applications, subject to role-based access permissions.

In its initial phase, the Command Centre brings together dashboards covering key DGFT functions and trade-related domains, including Importer Exporter Code (IEC), Advance Authorisation, Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG), Certificate of Origin (CoO), SCOMET, restricted imports and exports, and other regulatory and trade facilitation processes. These dashboards will enable monitoring of scheme utilisation, processing efficiency, export obligations, trade patterns and operational performance across Regional Authorities.

The NSTCC is designed to support three key dimensions of trade governance:

• Integrated Monitoring: Providing consolidated visibility into trade trends, application processing, pendency and emerging risks, enabling timely identification and resolution of operational issues.

• Performance Assessment: Facilitating monitoring and benchmarking of schemes, processes and Regional Authorities against defined performance indicators to identify gaps and opportunities for improvement.

• Evidence-Based Policy Inputs: Identifying recurring bottlenecks, procedural complexities and emerging trade patterns to support policy simplification, process improvements and targeted trade facilitation measures.

The initiative also seeks to strengthen India's trade intelligence capabilities by enabling product-wise and market-wise analysis, assessment of trade agreement utilisation, identification of export opportunities and monitoring of India's trade positioning across international markets.

NSTCC has been designed to leverage existing digital infrastructure, including DGFT systems and the Trade Connect ePlatform, while providing a framework for progressive integration of additional datasets from other departments and trade-related agencies.

Going forward, the Command Centre is envisaged to evolve into a broader whole-of-government decision-support mechanism, with phased access for authorised stakeholders, including relevant ministries, states, Export Promotion Councils and other institutions. Its analytical capabilities will also be progressively strengthened through additional data integration, automated alerts and advanced analytics.

The launch of NSTCC marks an important step towards proactive, transparent and responsive trade governance, enabling the Department of Commerce and DGFT to move from periodic reporting towards continuous monitoring, coordinated intervention and evidence-based policy formulation.

The initiative reinforces the Government of India's commitment to leveraging digital technologies and data-driven governance to strengthen trade facilitation, improve administrative efficiency and enhance India's competitiveness in global trade.

2323997.title: Vice-President inaugurates KAUMARACON-2026 and launches digital initiatives of the All India Institute of Ayurveda
2323997.body_html:
AYUSH
Vice-President inaugurates KAUMARACON-2026 and launches digital initiatives of the All India Institute of Ayurveda
“Research Must Establish the Scientific Basis of Traditional Healthcare Practices for Their Global Acceptance”: Vice-President
“Ayurveda Has Great Potential in Preventive Healthcare, Nutrition and Child Development”: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav
“AIIA Has Emerged as a Leader in Ayurvedic Education, Research and Clinical Care”: Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha
Digital Initiatives Launched at KAUMARACON-2026 to Advance Research, Innovation and Clinical Practice
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated KAUMARACON-2026 at the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Ayush. The event is the third international conference on Kaumarabhritya (Ayurvedic paediatrics). It is being held from 15 to 17 October 2026 under the theme “Shaping the Future of Child Health: Global Perspectives, Research Innovations, and Clinical Frontiers in Kaumarabhritya.” The occasion also marked the Institute’s Foundation Day. It celebrated a decade of progress in Ayurvedic education, clinical services, scientific research and innovation.

The Vice-President called for greater scientific research to establish the efficacy of traditional healthcare practices, strengthen patient confidence and enhance the global acceptance of India’s traditional systems of medicine. He noted that India’s traditional systems of medicine represent a valuable legacy rooted in its civilisational wisdom and centuries-old knowledge traditions. He also highlighted the international recognition of Yoga and the establishment of the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in Jamnagar as important milestones in sharing India’s traditional knowledge with the world.

Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of developing AIIA at par with AIIMS, the Vice President said the Institute was progressing towards realising this vision. Congratulating AIIA on its 10th Foundation Day, he emphasised the importance of sustained efforts in research, innovation and academic excellence to further strengthen the Institute’s standing. He called upon researchers and practitioners to preserve traditional wisdom, strengthen it through scientific validation and place child health at the centre of their efforts.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, highlighted the transformative journey of India’s traditional systems of medicine over the past decade under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He also noted that Ayurveda and other traditional healthcare systems, once often regarded as alternative approaches, are increasingly being integrated into the broader healthcare framework through institutional development, scientific research, quality assurance and evidence-based clinical practices.

Referring to the Ministry of Ayush’s 11-year progress, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the growing public trust in Ayush systems, the expansion of healthcare services and India’s increasing international recognition in traditional medicine. The Minister commended AIIA for emerging as a leading institution in this transformation. He noted that since its dedication to the nation by the Prime Minister in 2017, the Institute has strengthened its academic and clinical capabilities, earned NAAC A++ accreditation, expanded its specialised outpatient services and advanced its research infrastructure.

Emphasising the significance of KAUMARACON-2026, Shri Jadhav said that child health must remain a national priority and that India’s classical Ayurvedic knowledge offers valuable perspectives on preventive healthcare, maternal and child nutrition, growth and development. He underscored the importance of combining this traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific methods to establish credible, safe and effective approaches to paediatric healthcare.

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, described the occasion as an opportunity to reflect on the achievements of the Ayush sector and the institutional transformation of traditional medicine in India. He highlighted the Government’s efforts to strengthen Ayush through the National Ayush Mission, expanded healthcare access, research initiatives, quality assurance and international collaboration. He referred to the establishment of the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in Jamnagar and the growing availability of scientific literature through the Ayush Research Portal and Traditional Medicine Global Library.

Highlighting AIIA’s contribution, Vaidya Kotecha noted that the Institute operates more than 45 specialised OPDs, offers postgraduate and doctoral education across 12 specialties, mentors 105 pharmacovigilance centres and maintains more than 97 national and international academic collaborations. He also referred to the establishment of the AIIA satellite campus in Goa and the announcement of three new AIIA institutions in the Union Budget 2026–27.

Referring to the central role of Kaumarabhritya, the Secretary emphasised the importance of research, collaboration and innovation in strengthening paediatric healthcare. He expressed confidence that KAUMARACON-2026 would further advance Ayurveda’s contribution to child health and reinforce its role in India’s healthcare system.

Welcoming the dignitaries, Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, New Delhi described KAUMARACON-2026 as a significant milestone in the Institute’s journey towards completing a decade of service, academic advancement and scientific achievement. He expressed gratitude to the Vice-President for gracing the occasion and reaffirmed AIIA’s commitment to integrating classical Ayurvedic knowledge with contemporary scientific inquiry. He highlighted the Institute’s progress since its dedication to the nation in 2017, noting that AIIA has earned NAAC A++ accreditation and NABH quality recognition and has continued to expand its specialised clinical services, research facilities and academic programmes.

Prof. Prajapati emphasised that child healthcare is fundamental to building a healthy society. He highlighted the establishment of the KINDER Lab, which provides specialised facilities for paediatric electrophysiology and non-invasive diagnostics, and the Ayurinformatics Lab, which supports AI-driven formulation development and dosage design. He noted that the conference provides a valuable platform for sharing clinical insights, discussing translational research and exploring child-friendly therapeutic approaches. He expressed confidence that the scientific deliberations would foster international collaboration and open new avenues for improving child healthcare through research and innovation.

During the inaugural ceremony, the Vice-President inaugurated the Ayush Start-up Portal, the AIIA–iCAINE website and the Ayurveda Digital Innovation and Venture Acceleration Facility (AyuDIVA). He also launched the Vamana App and the Panchakarma Assessment App, marking an important step towards strengthening digital infrastructure, entrepreneurship and technology-enabled clinical practice in Ayurveda.

An international Memorandum of Understanding between Maharishi International University (MIU), USA, and AIIA, New Delhi, was also exchanged in the presence of the Vice-President, reflecting the Institute’s commitment to international academic and research collaboration.

Dr. Maneesha Upendra Kothekar, Chairperson, National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), graced the occasion along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush and heads of various Ayush institutes. The conference also brought together eminent Vaidyas, paediatric healthcare specialists, researchers, academicians and international delegates from across the globe.

KAUMARACON-2026 will continue to deliberate on advances in Ayurvedic paediatric care, with scientific sessions and discussions aimed at strengthening evidence-based approaches to child health.

2323996.title: ‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’
2323996.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’
Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY Undertake Swachhata Drive as Part of Special Campaign 6.0
764 Senior Citizen Homes Supported under IPSrC Directed to Undertake Cleanliness, Decluttering, Waste Management, Greening Activities; Active Participation of Elderly Residents Emphasized
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, is actively participating in Special Campaign 6.0, the Government-wide initiative aimed at institutionalizing Swachhata, promoting efficient management of public spaces and reducing pendency in Government offices and institutions.

In furtherance of the objectives of the Campaign, the Department, under its umbrella scheme Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), has directed all 764 Senior Citizen Homes supported under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) to undertake cleanliness and sanitation activities.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen cleanliness practices in institutions providing care and support to senior citizens and to ensure that these facilities maintain a clean, safe, accessible and dignified living environment for elderly residents.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He said the Campaign, coordinated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), underscores the importance of cleanliness, systematic waste management, environmental sustainability and the development of a culture of continuous improvement across public institutions.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Senior Citizen Homes have been advised to undertake comprehensive cleanliness drives covering their premises, common areas and surrounding spaces, along with decluttering, appropriate waste segregation and disposal, removal of unwanted materials and greening activities. The emphasis is on ensuring that cleanliness becomes an integral part of the daily functioning of these institutions rather than remaining confined to a time-bound campaign.

 

 

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official said that building upon the momentum generated during the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6.0, the Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY across the country have been undertaking a range of activities in accordance with the Campaign's theme, ‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’. He said these activities reflect the importance of maintaining hygienic and orderly institutional environments, particularly in facilities where senior citizens reside and receive care and assistance.

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He said the observance of the Swachhata Drive across the network of 764 IPSrC-supported Senior Citizen Homes also reflects the principle of Jan Bhagidari, recognising that sustainable improvements in cleanliness and public hygiene require the participation and cooperation of all stakeholders. The involvement of residents and caregivers helps strengthen collective responsibility for maintaining clean surroundings and encourages the adoption of good practices in everyday institutional life.

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official elaborated that the cleanliness drives include sweeping and cleaning residential premises, corridors, dining areas, kitchens, recreational spaces and other common facilities; cleaning approach roads and surrounding areas; removing litter, dry leaves, weeds and overgrown vegetation; and ensuring the proper collection, segregation and disposal of waste.

 

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He added these Homes have also been encouraged to remove unnecessary and unused materials, organize storage spaces and maintain clear and accessible pathways to facilitate the safe movement of elderly residents.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official further said the greening and environmental improvement activities form an important component of the initiative adding that plantation of saplings, maintenance of gardens and green spaces, and efforts to improve the overall appearance of institutional campuses contribute to a healthier and more pleasant living environment. Such measures also encourage environmental awareness and promote the responsible use and maintenance of shared spaces, he said.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official said the initiative places particular emphasis on the active participation of senior citizens, staff members and implementing agencies. He added that by involving elderly residents in suitable cleanliness, gardening and campus-improvement activities, the Campaign promotes a sense of ownership, collective responsibility and community participation as the participation is encouraged in a manner appropriate to the health, mobility and individual capacities of residents, ensuring that the activities remain inclusive, safe and meaningful.

 

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

 

The participation of Senior Citizen Homes in Special Campaign 6.0 reinforces the Department's commitment to dignified ageing, improved institutional care and the promotion of active ageing.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The initiative is aligned with the broader objectives of AVYAY, which seeks to create an enabling environment for senior citizens through institutional and community-based support, improved access to services and the promotion of their well-being and dignity. Through the IPSrC component, the Department supports eligible implementing agencies in providing institutional care and essential services to senior citizens, particularly those who require continued care, protection and assistance.

The Senior Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment will continue to encourage Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY to sustain the practices adopted during Special Campaign 6.0 beyond the Campaign period. Regular cleanliness schedules, responsible waste management, periodic decluttering, maintenance of green spaces and active resident participation are expected to remain important elements of institutional management.

Through these efforts, the Department seeks to reinforce a culture of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and dignity in senior citizen care institutions, in keeping with the Government of India's commitment to cleaner, greener and more inclusive public institutions and to ensuring a safe, healthy and dignified living environment for senior citizens across the country.

A clean and well-maintained environment is an important component of the overall well-being of senior citizens, contributing to their comfort, safety, dignity and quality of life. Regular attention to sanitation, waste management and the upkeep of common areas can also help reduce avoidable environmental hazards and support the maintenance of healthier residential facilities.

2323959.title: Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
2323959.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
Event highlights the pivotal role of women farmers  in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat
Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra  highlights  invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors; emphasises  the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, celebrated Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 today (15 October 2026 ) at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The programme was organised to recognise the invaluable contribution of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their pivotal role in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.

 

Sh. Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in his address, highlighted the invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors, particularly in ensuring food security, sustaining rural livelihoods, managing natural resources and driving agricultural development. He emphasised the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture through various initiatives, including direct income support, affordable institutional credit, technology transfer, skill development, farm mechanisation and improved access to agricultural marketing infrastructure.

महिला किसान दिवस के अवसर पर अपनी सभी किसान बहनों को प्रणाम करता हूं। भारत गांव के बिना अधूरा है और गांव खेती के बिना और खेती महिलाओं के बिना नहीं हो सकती। अनादि काल से हमारी बहनें खेती में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका का निर्वहन करती आ रही हैं। महिला किसान हमारी कृषि व्यवस्था की रीढ़ हैं और देश की खाद्य सुरक्षा एवं ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूती प्रदान कर रही हैं। बदलते युग और खेती के तरीकों में आज बहनों की भूमिका खेती में बहुत महत्वपूर्ण हो गई है। अब ड्रोन दीदी है जो दवाओं का छिड़काव करती हैं, कृषि सखी हैं जो किसानों को कृषि पद्धतियों की ट्रेनिंग देती हैं, बैंक सखी हैं जो बैंक से टाई-अप करती हैं, पशु सखी हैं जो पशुपालन और दूध उत्पादन के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है। किसान के कच्चे उत्पाद के प्रोसेसिंग का काम हमारी बहनें कर रही हैं और इन उत्पादों को लोगों तक पहुँचाने में हमारी बहनें किसान दीदियाँ FPOs के माध्यम से बहुत महत्वपूर्ण काम कर रही हैं। आइए, मेरी बहनों, महिला किसान दिवस पर हम यह संकल्प लें कि कृषि के हर आयाम पर हम काम करेंगे। हम खुद भी आगे बढ़ेंगे, खेती आगे बढ़ाएँगे, देश आगे बढ़ाएँगे। मुझे विश्वास है कि देश की नारी शक्ति आत्मनिर्भर कृषि, समृद्ध ग्रामीण भारत और विकसित भारत @2047 के संकल्प को साकार करने में निर्णायक भूमिका निभाएँगी। महिला किसान सशक्त होंगी, तो कृषि समृद्ध होगी; कृषि समृद्ध होगी, तो भारत विकसित होगा। सभी को महिला किसान दिवस पर हार्दिक बधाई एवं शुभकामनाएं!

— Shivraj Singh Chouhan (@ChouhanShivraj) October 15, 2026

The programme witnessed the participation of progressive women farmers, women agricultural extension workers and functionaries from various States/UTs, along with senior officers of DA&FW. The theme for Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 was “Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India.” The theme underscores the vital role of women in strengthening agricultural productivity, promoting sustainable farming practices, conserving natural resources and contributing to rural prosperity.

 

As part of the programme, outstanding women farmers were felicitated in recognition of their achievements and contributions to agriculture and allied sectors. The felicitation acknowledged their dedication, resilience, innovation and leadership in agricultural activities and rural entrepreneurship. A book titled “Women Farmers of India: Journey from Challenges to Success” was also released during the event. This book is a compilation of inspiring success stories of women farmers, highlighting their remarkable contributions, achievements, innovations, and journeys from struggle to success in agriculture and allied sectors. It proudly showcases the vital role of women in agriculture, recognising their potential, leadership, and entrepreneurial spirit.

 

The programme also provided a platform for women farmers and extension functionaries to share their experiences and journeys. A few participants addressed the gathering and spoke about their personal experiences, challenges, achievements and contributions to agriculture. Their accounts highlighted the important role of women in adopting improved agricultural practices, strengthening rural livelihoods and inspiring other women to participate in agricultural development.

 

Women farmers make significant contributions across the agricultural value chain, including crop cultivation, livestock management, seed conservation, natural resource management, post-harvest activities and value addition. Their traditional knowledge, entrepreneurial initiatives and adoption of innovative and climate-resilient practices are essential to making Indian agriculture more productive, sustainable and inclusive.

Women agricultural officers and extension functionaries also play a crucial role in bridging the gap between agricultural research and farming communities. Through training, technology dissemination, awareness generation and guidance on government schemes, they facilitate the adoption of scientific agricultural practices and empower women farmers with knowledge and institutional support.

The celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to recognising women as key stakeholders in agricultural transformation. It highlighted the importance of strengthening women's access to technology, resources, capacity-building opportunities and institutional support, while encouraging their greater participation in decision-making and leadership across agriculture and allied sectors.

Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 is also being observed across States and Union Territories, Extension Education Institutes (EEIs), State Agricultural Management and Extension Training Institutes (SAMETIs) and MANAGE, with participation from women farmers and other agricultural stakeholders. Special emphasis has been placed on the participation of women farmers from tribal regions.

The celebration reinforced the message that empowering women farmers and recognising their contributions are essential to building developed agriculture, strengthening rural livelihoods and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.

2323953.title: TDB-DST supports Development and Commercialisation of Indigenous 32-Slice CT Scanner by Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
2323953.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST supports Development and Commercialisation of Indigenous 32-Slice CT Scanner by Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

Strengthening India’s indigenous medical device manufacturing capabilities under the Government of India’s Make in India initiative, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd., Malur, Karnataka, to support the development and commercialisation of an indigenous 32-slice Computed Tomography (CT) Scanner.

Panacea Medical Technologies, an Indian medical device manufacturer specialising in radiotherapy and radiology, has established capabilities in developing advanced technologies, processes, modules and products for medical imaging and cancer treatment. Building on its expertise in high-precision imaging, the company has undertaken the development of a diagnostic CT scanner to expand its portfolio into advanced diagnostic imaging.

The project envisages the design, development and deployment of a 32-slice CT scanner for diagnostic imaging across various clinical disciplines. CT scanners use rotating X-ray systems and digital detectors to capture cross-sectional images, which are reconstructed through computer algorithms to generate detailed images of internal body structures. Their development requires precise engineering, integration of imaging components and rigorous calibration to ensure imaging accuracy and patient safety.

India’s diagnostic imaging sector is witnessing growing demand for advanced technologies, driven by expanding healthcare infrastructure, the rising burden of chronic diseases and the need for timely and accurate diagnosis. Indigenous development of high-end medical equipment can contribute to strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and reducing dependence on imported technologies.

The Government of India has identified medical devices as a priority sector under the Make in India initiative. Through its support for indigenous technology development, TDB seeks to enable Indian enterprises to develop advanced medical technologies, strengthen domestic manufacturing and improve access to healthcare equipment.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The development of an indigenous CT scanner aligns with the Government of India’s vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing of high-end medical devices under the Make in India initiative. TDB’s support aims to encourage medical technology companies to develop innovative indigenous solutions that can address the country’s healthcare requirements while creating opportunities for wider adoption in global markets. Such initiatives can contribute to building India’s capabilities as a manufacturer of advanced medical equipment.”

Promoter of Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd., said, “We express our sincere gratitude to the Technology Development Board for its pivotal support. This collaboration will accelerate our efforts to develop indigenous diagnostic imaging technology and contribute to making advanced CT imaging more accessible across India.”

2323918.title: Raksha Rajya Mantri Chairs Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference of NCC in Guwahati, Assam
2323918.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Rajya Mantri Chairs Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference of NCC in Guwahati, Assam
Ministers from 7 NER states, Sikkim and West Bengal participated in the conference
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri (RRM) Shri Sanjay Seth attended the Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference 2026 in Guwahati, Assam, organised by the National Cadet Corps (NCC) on October 15, 2026. The conference deliberated on the expansion, strengthening and effective functioning of the NCC in the North Eastern Region (NER), West Bengal and Sikkim.

Addressing the conference, RRM appreciated the participation of cadets from the North Eastern States in the Republic Day Camp (RDC) and the increasing enrolment of girl cadets, reflecting the NCC’s contribution to women’s empowerment. He emphasised the need to work towards the Prime Minister’s vision of expanding the NCC from its present strength of approximately 17 lakh cadets to 20 lakh. RRM stressed the importance of motivating and guiding the youth to imbibe the spirit of ‘Nation First’. He called upon all nine participating States to formulate and implement practical, actionable plans for NCC expansion, with particular emphasis on strengthening infrastructure and enhancing training facilities for cadets and reaffirmed the Government’s commitment towards it.

 

Quoting the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi "The NCC is a movement that empowers India's Yuva Shakti, making our youth confident, disciplined, and dedicated to the nation," RRM emphasised on ensuring effective training, adequate institutional support and improved coordination among stakeholders to strengthen the organisation’s outreach and functioning.

The conference provided a platform for strengthening coordination between the NCC and the State Governments, with deliberations focusing on expanding NCC coverage, cadet welfare, training infrastructure, institutional strengthening and addressing administrative challenges. It also emphasised the contribution of NCC towards social service and community development, character-building, leadership, national integration and the development of a spirit of service among young people.

The North Eastern Region NCC Directorate provides coverage across the seven States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura through nine Group Headquarters and 50 units. NCC is present in 1,645 educational institutions in the region, with a strength of approximately 1.25 lakh cadets. Similarly, the West Bengal & Sikkim NCC Directorate provides coverage through six Group Headquarters and 56 units, with NCC activities extending to 1,326 educational institutions and approximately 1.25 lakh cadets.

The conference, led by Director General NCC, Lt Gen Virendra Vats, was attended by Additional Secretary, Mrs Dipti Mohil Chawla, Ministers and senior officials from the participating States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, West Bengal and Sikkim and Senior officials from Ministry of Defence & NCC.
