2323670.title: Lucknow to Host Third Regional Workshop on Training Institute Transformation on 23 and 24 October 2026
2323670.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2323670.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Lucknow to Host Third Regional Workshop on Training Institute Transformation on 23 and 24 October 2026
Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, to inaugurate the workshop in the presence of Dr Jitendra Singh; eight States and four Union Territories of the Northern Region to participate
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 10:56AM by PIB Delhi

The Capacity Building Commission (CBC) will hold the third regional workshop of Sādhana Śhrinkhla 2026 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on 23 and 24 October 2026. The two-day consultation will bring together States and Union Territories of the Northern Region to deliberate on how Government Training Institutes can grow into modern, competency-driven capacity building institutions under Mission Karmayogi.

The workshop will be inaugurated by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, in the august presence of Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

A Regional Series with a National Purpose

Sādhana Śhrinkhla, short for Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement, is a series of four regional consultative workshops. It carries forward the conversation on institutional reform that the Commission has led over the past year through Regional Task Force meetings, Sādhana Saptah from 2 to 8 April 2026, and the National Departmental Summit on Institutionalising Capacity Building in May 2026.

The series opened at Vijayawada on 29 and 30 September 2026, followed by the North Eastern Region workshop at Guwahati on 9 October 2026. Lucknow now takes the dialogue to the Northern Region.

Participating States and Union Territories

Hosted by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the workshop will see participation from the States of Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, and the Union Territories of Chandigarh, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh. Senior State officials will be joined by heads and faculty of Training Institutes, subject experts and industry partners.

With eight States and four Union Territories spanning the Himalayan region, the Indo-Gangetic plains and the desert State of Rajasthan, the Lucknow workshop brings together the widest range of administrative contexts in the series so far.

What the Workshop Will Address

Civil servants today are expected to keep pace with new technologies, changing citizen expectations and complex development priorities. Training Institutes are central to preparing them for this, and the workshop will focus on how they can respond more closely to what officials actually need in their roles.

Deliberations will cover four broad areas: institutional governance and leadership; operational effectiveness and collaboration between institutes; faculty and institutional competencies; and digital transformation, including the use of Artificial Intelligence in training. Each participating State and Union Territory will be supported in identifying its own priorities and drawing up a practical roadmap for reform.

UNNATI as the Common Platform

These reforms will be taken forward through the Unified New-Age National Training Initiatives (UNNATI) portal, launched during Sādhana Saptah 2026. UNNATI connects more than 700 Training Institutes on a single platform and links them to the competency needs identified in Capacity Building Plans, helping institutes share resources, collaborate and improve on the basis of data.

Shaping the Training Institute Transformation Framework

The outcomes of the Lucknow workshop, together with those from Vijayawada, Guwahati and the final regional workshop, will feed into the Training Institute Transformation Framework being developed by the Commission. The Framework will offer a common direction for reform while leaving room for each State's institutional realities.

Through Sādhana Śhrinkhla, the Commission aims to build a connected and responsive network of Training Institutes that equips civil servants to serve citizens better, in keeping with the vision of Mission Karmayogi and Viksit Bharat 2047.

2323665.title: Digital India BHASHINI Division and Government of Manipur Sign MoU to Advance Multilingual AI and Language Technology at BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop
2323665.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Digital India BHASHINI Division and Government of Manipur Sign MoU to Advance Multilingual AI and Language Technology at BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop
BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop - Manipur Chapter explores language technology, local language data and citizen-centric digital services
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Information Technology, Government of Manipur, organised the BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop, Manipur Chapter, in Imphal on 14 October 2026. The workshop explored opportunities to advance multilingual artificial intelligence, strengthen language technology and integrate Indian language solutions into government and citizen-facing digital services.

The programme was graced by Shri Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Manipur, and brought together government representatives and other stakeholders to discuss the role of language technology in making digital services more accessible and inclusive.

A key outcome of the workshop was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between DIBD and the Government of Manipur, represented by Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, DIBD, and Shri Somorjit Salam, IAS, Secretary, Information Technology, Government of Manipur. The MoU aims to strengthen cooperation in language technology, improve language resources and explore solutions for multilingual digital services across the state.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Manipur, highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence and language technology to promote India’s linguistic diversity and expand opportunities for the state’s communities. “Through artificial intelligence and language technology, we are promoting India’s diverse languages and exploring opportunities to bring more of Manipur’s languages into the digital space. Our linguistic diversity is a valuable strength as we move forward,” he said.

Shri Somorjit Salam, IAS, Secretary, Information Technology, Government of Manipur, emphasised that digital services must be accessible and meaningful to the people they are intended to serve. “Digital services are effective only when people can understand and use them confidently. Through BHASHINI, we can address language barriers with carefully tested solutions that respond to Manipur’s needs and deliver lasting public benefit,” he said.

The workshop provided an overview of BHASHINI’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and its multilingual AI ecosystem, highlighting the role of language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications in enabling digital services across languages. Discussions explored how these capabilities could be integrated into government platforms and citizen-facing applications to support more accessible service delivery.

A live demonstration of real-time English-to-Manipuri translation showcased the potential of language technology to bridge communication gaps. The session also highlighted the importance of building digital language resources and validating language models using relevant data, with inputs from language experts and local communities, to improve their usefulness in real-world settings.

Speaking on the need to build language technologies that reflect India’s diversity, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, DIBD, said: “AI must understand India in all its linguistic diversity. Through our partnership with Manipur, we aim to strengthen language technologies, expand practical applications and ensure that language is not a barrier to accessing digital services or pursuing opportunities,” he said.

The workshop highlighted the linguistic diversity of Manipur, including Manipuri, Tangkhul, Thadou, Paite, Hmar, Liangmai and other languages spoken across the state. The state’s linguistic knowledge, local expertise and community participation can contribute to developing language technologies that better reflect regional needs and communication practices.

Sessions explored applications of multilingual AI in governance and citizen services, including education, healthcare, legal services and grievance redressal. BHASHINI शिल्पी, an interactive platform for developers, students and innovators, provided an opportunity to learn, experiment, solve problems and build with Language AI. Going beyond a conventional technology session, it encouraged participants to explore real-world challenges, exchange ideas and discover possibilities for developing, scaling and innovating with BHASHINI’s language technologies, services and APIs. The interactive Q&A further enabled participants to discuss potential applications and seek clarity on implementation. The BHASHINI Mitra initiative was also highlighted as an avenue for state institutions and language communities to contribute language data and strengthen multilingual AI resources.

As a next step, DIBD and the Government of Manipur will identify priority use cases, assess language-data requirements and explore the integration of BHASHINI’s language technologies into relevant government platforms. The collaboration will also focus on strengthening language resources and working with language experts and local communities to develop and validate solutions that reflect the state’s linguistic diversity and public service needs.

The BHASHINI Rajyam initiative aims to strengthen collaboration between BHASHINI and state governments, helping translate language technology capabilities into practical solutions that improve access to digital services and enable wider participation in India’s digital ecosystem.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is advancing India’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure to enable multilingual access to digital services. BHASHINI brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support government departments, developers, researchers and other stakeholders in building multilingual AI solutions. It powers more than 800 government websites, has enabled over 9 billion cumulative AI inferences and processes more than 24 million AI inferences daily. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages, advancing the adoption of language technology across India’s digital ecosystem.

****

2323590.title: Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies Included under Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme
2323590.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
2323590.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies Included under Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme
Government of India approves the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) proposal to include the Chemicals and Petrochemicals under RDI Scheme
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has included Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies as an additional technology area eligible for funding under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, with effect from 8 October 2026.

The decision has been taken by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, following a proposal by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

DCPC had proposed the inclusion of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector as a priority area under the RDI Scheme. The decision is expected to strengthen research, development and innovation in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector and facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for advanced industrial applications.

Under the visionary leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India launched the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme in November 2025, with a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore to catalyse private-sector investment in research, development and innovation. The scheme seeks to provide long-term financing and refinancing on favourable terms for transformative projects, accelerate the adoption of advanced technologies, strengthen India’s industrial competitiveness and foster self-reliance in critical and emerging technology areas.

At the launch of the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme last year, the Prime Minister said, “India is rapidly building a vibrant ecosystem for research and development. We are focusing on Ease of Doing Research so that a modern ecosystem of innovation can flourish in India.”

Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers & Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, has welcomed the inclusion of the sector under the RDI Scheme and described it as an important development for the chemicals and petrochemicals industry.

Shri Nadda said the decision would provide a much-needed impetus to research and innovation, supporting the development of advanced, efficient and cost-effective technologies for manufacturing chemicals, petrochemical products, polymers and their derivatives in India.

The inclusion of Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies is aligned with the broader objective of strengthening India's domestic manufacturing ecosystem, promoting technology-led industrial growth and reducing dependence on imported technologies and high-value materials.

2323586.title: NCISM Chairperson launches CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 to strengthen Ayurveda research and innovation
2323586.body_html:
AYUSH
NCISM Chairperson launches CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 to strengthen Ayurveda research and innovation
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Chairperson of National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), Prof. Maneesha Kothekar, today launched CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 (2nd circular) of the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS). The initiatives aim to strengthen the research ecosystem in Ayurveda by encouraging research among undergraduate students and recognising scholarly excellence, research communication and innovation.

CCRAS SPARK 5.0

The Studentship Program for Ayurveda Research Ken (SPARK) 5.0 for 2026-27 is the fifth edition of the programme. It seeks to introduce undergraduate Ayurveda students to research methodology and techniques through short-term independent research projects, and to foster research aptitude, analytical thinking and early interest in research as a career among BAMS students.

  • A total of 300 studentships are being offered, with a studentship amount of ₹50,000.
  • BAMS students in their third/fourth/professional years studying in NCISM/Government of India-recognised colleges or universities are eligible.
  • Registration opens on 15 October 2026. The last date for submission of applications is 15 November 2026.

CCRAS Ayurshodh – National Research Recognitions

CCRAS Ayurshodh provides a platform to recognise and encourage research contributions in Ayurveda across three categories:

  • CCRAS-Prabodh 3MT: Communication of research through three-minute thesis presentations.
  • CCRAS-Prakash: Recognition of scholarly achievements through publications based on original research.
  • CCRAS-Navonmesha: Recognition of innovative prototypes, novel solutions, process innovations and transformative research methodologies.

The second circular details the awards, including prize money sponsored by Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited. The finals of CCRAS Ayurshodh are scheduled for 11 December 2026.

Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS; Dr. Ranjit Puranik, MD and CEO, Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited; Presidents of various NCISM boards and heads of CCRAS institutes across the country were present on the occasion.

The initiatives are intended to nurture emerging research talent, promote effective research communication, encourage quality scholarly publications and foster innovative approaches to advancing Ayurveda research.

Further information is available at the following links:

  • CCRAS SPARK 5.0: https://spark.ccras.org.in/
  • CCRAS Ayurshodh: https://ayurshodh.ccras.org.in/

2323573.title: Government mobilizes National Law Universities to target Criminal Case Backlogs across 100 Hotspot Districts
2323573.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government mobilizes National Law Universities to target Criminal Case Backlogs across 100 Hotspot Districts
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant move to address the issue of pendency of cases at the District and Subordinate Judiciary, the Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, has decided to take action in a focused manner by identifying hotspot districts where such cases are in large number. Accordingly, under the guidance of Union Law Minister Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, the department has initiated a nationwide, research-based mission targeting the top 100 judicial districts with high litigation pendency. Over 5.8 crore cases are pending across courts in the country, of which the majority are in district and subordinate courts. Further, those identified  100 districts account for over half of all district-court pendency.

Accordingly, under this initiative, a meeting was convened with Vice Chancellors of nineteen National Law Universities of sixteen states. The meeting was convened through video conferencing. It was  chaired by the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal.

Secretary, Department of Justice, the Director General (Awards), the Director General, Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D), the Director General, National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), and other officials attended the meeting physically. 

During the discussions, various alternatives like identifying infructuous cases, case profiling, alternative dispute resolution, management of adjournments, plea bargaining, mediation assisted settlements, bringing summary trial process etc. were deliberated upon. It was also highlighted to the NLUs that they may effectively utilize their pro bono clubs, researchers and students to carry out the ground level analysis  of case pendency in the selected districts and suggest possible strategies to address the issue. As the way forward, NLUs were requested to develop focused approach for the 100 districts, based on district-specific diagnosis and identify the main causes of delay. They were also requested to suggest feasible mechanism to reduce litigation pendency. All the Vice Chancellors of NLUs have assured their active participation and their willingness to serve the Nation.

Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal summed up by reiterating the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji for Viksit Bharat @2047, for which an accessible, efficient, cost effective, fair, speedy and responsive justice delivery system is essential.

2323572.title: INDIAN NAVY COMPLETES MAIDEN COMMAND OF COMBINED TASK FORCE 154
2323572.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY COMPLETES MAIDEN COMMAND OF COMBINED TASK FORCE 154
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy successfully completed its maiden Command of a Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) Task Force, with the relinquishment of Command of Combined Task Force 154 (CTF 154) at a ceremony held in Manama, Bahrain, on 14 Oct 2026. The eight-month tenure marked a significant milestone in India's growing contribution to multinational maritime training, capacity building and collaborative maritime security.

The ceremony was attended by VAdm Curt A Renshaw, Commander Combined Maritime Forces; HE Dr Pradeep Singh Rajpurohit, Ambassador of India to the Kingdom of Bahrain; Cmde Khalid Jasim Althawadi, Naval Sector Commander, Royal Bahrain Naval Force; Cmde Dan Thomas, Deputy Commander Combined Maritime Forces; and senior representatives of CMF Headquarters and Partner Nations. VAdm Manish Chadha, Director General Naval Operations, Indian Navy, participated through video teleconferencing. During the ceremony, Cmde Milind M Mokashi, formally relinquished Command of CTF 154 and handed over responsibilities to Commander Melissa Desjardins, Deputy Commander CTF 154, who received Command on behalf of CMF Headquarters.

Established in May 2023, CTF 154 is CMF's dedicated multinational maritime training Task Force, mandated to enhance professional competencies, interoperability and capacity development among Partner Nations. The Indian Navy assumed Command of CTF 154 on 11 February 2026, becoming the first Indian Navy contingent to lead a CMF Task Force.(https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2226776)

During its tenure, the Indian Navy-led CTF 154 conducted 20 Staff Enhancement Training engagements, two major multinational training exercises and the inaugural Subject Matter Expert Exchange on Piracy and Armed Robbery (SPAR 2026). These initiatives collectively generated over 7,800 training hours, with personnel from 39 countries participating in CTF 154 activities. The Staff Enhancement Training and SPAR engagements alone recorded over 1,100 participant attendances, reflecting the scale and reach of the training initiatives undertaken during the Command.

A major highlight was Operation Compass Rose 26-1, conducted from 20 to 22 Apr 2026. Adapted to a fully virtual format in view of the prevailing regional security environment, the exercise brought together 137 participants, 11 observers and 21 facilitators from 25 Partner Nations and 13 organisations. The exercise demonstrated the ability of CMF partners to sustain multinational training and operational coordination despite regional constraints.

Operation Southern Readiness 26-2, conducted at the Southern Naval Command, Kochi, from 20 to 23 Jul 2026, marked the first major CMF training exercise hosted by India. The exercise witnessed participation of 276 personnel from 27 countries and generated approximately 3,800 training hours, making it the largest Maritime Domain Enhancement Training engagement undertaken by CTF 154 since its establishment. The exercise provided participating nations an opportunity to train at the Indian Navy's specialist training establishments and gain exposure to advanced simulators and operational platforms, highlighting India's established naval training infrastructure and capacity to support multinational training requirements.

(https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2288511)

The 20 Staff Enhancement Training engagements addressed a broad spectrum of contemporary maritime security challenges, including Maritime Domain Awareness, Maritime Law and Law Enforcement, Information Sharing, Counter-Piracy, Maritime Crime Investigation, Cyber Resilience, Emerging Technologies, Multinational Operational Planning, Leadership and Personnel Resilience. Drawing upon expertise from the Indian Navy, CMF Task Forces, Partner Nations, regional maritime agencies and specialist institutions, the programme facilitated the exchange of operational experience and specialised knowledge. Notably, the tenure witnessed the first dedicated 'Training of Trainers' engagement within the CMF training framework and CMF's first professional engagement with a Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea.

The concluding major training engagement was SPAR 2026, conducted on 05 and 06 Oct 2026. The inaugural exchange brought together 135 participants, including facilitators, from 25 countries, with contributions from 19 organisations and specialist teams. The initiative provided a common platform for operational counter-piracy forces, maritime law enforcement agencies, Information Sharing organisations, legal specialists, technology providers and the maritime industry to deliberate upon evolving piracy threats and contemporary challenges in maritime security.

During the Command tenure, CTF 154 also expanded its engagement with regional partners and specialised institutions. Participation in the Fifth Regional Maritime Law Enforcement Dialogue at Nairobi and interactions with the Royal Bahrain Naval Force facilitated discussions on maritime law enforcement, emerging training requirements and avenues for future cooperation.

India joined the Combined Maritime Forces as an Associate Partner in 2022 and became a full member in 2023. The successful completion of its maiden Command of CTF 154 represents an important progression in India's engagement with the multinational maritime partnership. The tenure demonstrated the Indian Navy's ability to plan, coordinate and deliver multinational training initiatives, bringing together diverse nations, institutions and operational expertise in support of shared maritime security objectives.

The successful tenure reinforces India's growing contribution to regional maritime security and underscores the Indian Navy's role as a Preferred Security and Training Partner, committed to strengthening maritime capacities and promoting a secure, stable and rules-based maritime environment.

2323570.title: Bharat’s civilisational journey had, for centuries, been a story of cultural exchange: Hon’ble Prime Minister
2323570.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Bharat’s civilisational journey had, for centuries, been a story of cultural exchange: Hon’ble Prime Minister
Brihattar Bharat to Strengthen Global Cultural Connections through Joint Research and International Collaboration:  Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi

 The three-day international conference on ‘Bharat’s Cultural Connections across the Globe’ by the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India Government of India, was inaugurated by the Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. The conference is being held from 14 to 16 October 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi conveyed his best wishes for the conference through a message, which was read out by Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture. Shri Vivek Aggarwal also delivered the introductory address.

Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi, Member Secretary, IGNCA, delivered the welcome address, while Dr. Arvind Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, proposed the vote of thanks. Prof. Dharm Chand Choubey, Head of the Brihattar Bharat Division at IGNCA, was also present on the occasion. An exhibition titled ‘Asia’s Shared Cultural Heritage’ was organised during the conference. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Shri Vivek Aggarwal and other distinguished guests visited the exhibition, which showcases the shared heritage and historical cultural connections between India and other Asian countries.

On this occasion, Shri Vivek Aggarwal read out the message of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Extending his best wishes to the Ministry of Culture and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, the Prime Minister warmly welcomed the scholars, researchers, diplomats and other distinguished participants from India and abroad attending the conference.

In his message, the Prime Minister said that India’s civilisational journey had, for centuries, been a story of cultural exchange. Centres of learning such as Nalanda strengthened the exchange of knowledge between India and other parts of Asia, while Buddhist monks, scholars, traders and travellers carried Indian ideas to different parts of the world through land and maritime routes.

He observed that this cultural dialogue continued to flourish, with Indian philosophy, music, dance, literature, cinema and culinary traditions connecting societies across the world with India. The celebration of Indian festivals and traditions in many countries, along with the global spread of yoga, exemplified how India’s ancient knowledge traditions continued to connect people across countries and cultures.

The Prime Minister noted that India’s cultural heritage was receiving increasing global recognition. He highlighted the significance of the conference in marking the centenary of the Greater India Society, which had played an important role in promoting the study and understanding of India’s cultural and intellectual relations with Asia and other parts of the world. He expressed the hope that the deliberations would further strengthen understanding of the historical and cultural ties between India and the world and advance international cultural cooperation.

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the Brihattar Bharat Conference provides an opportunity to explore how the wisdom of the past can guide our future and how cultural exchanges enable civilisations to share ideas, knowledge and artistic traditions. Marking the centenary of the Greater India Society, established in Calcutta on 14 October 1926, the conference reaffirms the importance of studying India’s historical and cultural connections with the world. Brihattar Bharat should be understood not as a political or territorial claim, but as a broad sphere of cultural and historical connections. He reiterated that India’s civilisational outlook, expressed through the principle that the entire world is one family, offers a lasting message of mutual respect and shared responsibility. Culture should connect the world, not divide it. Even when political relations become difficult or languages create barriers, cultural exchanges and evidence-based research can foster understanding and sustain dialogue.

He emphasised that the study of India’s global cultural connections should develop into a dynamic, evidence-based field grounded in international collaboration. Brihattar Bharat should become a platform where shared heritage inspires joint research, strengthens mutual understanding and builds enduring international partnerships. The conference should not merely commemorate a significant scholarly endeavour, but also mark the beginning of a renewed international movement to study, preserve and exchange the cultural connections that unite humanity.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal highlighted that the Brihattar Bharat Project seeks to bring India’s ancient cultural connections with the world to international recognition through collaborative, evidence-based research involving scholars from around 51 countries. Marking the centenary of the Greater India Society, the project aims to explore India’s contributions to global knowledge systems, languages, sciences, art and cultural traditions through joint research, seminars and workshops. It also envisages a structured five-year agenda for international academic exchange and seeks to explore multinational nominations of shared intangible cultural heritage to UNESCO’s Representative List. Brihattar Bharat is a joint scholarly endeavour to deepen understanding of our shared heritage and strengthen international relations. By fostering academic collaboration and cultural dialogue, the initiative seeks to carry forward a message of peace, unity and shared prosperity, rooted in the timeless Indian principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’- the world is one family.

 In his welcome address, Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi said that the identity of civilisations is shaped not only by geographical boundaries, but also by the journeys of ideas, the movement of people and the memories they leave behind. Throughout history, merchants crossed mountains and seas, Buddhist monks and pilgrims travelled between sacred sites, scholars exchanged ideas and translated texts, while artisans carried their skills and artistic traditions across regions. These encounters enabled cultures to engage in dialogue, learn from one another and evolve, creating connections that continue to shape the world. The concept of Brihattar Bharat is rooted in this rich history of cultural exchange.

He explained that Brihattar Bharat is an initiative of the ICR Division of the Ministry of Culture, implemented by IGNCA, to identify, document, preserve and make accessible the shared cultural heritage of Indian civilisation and selected countries. The initiative seeks to look beyond geographical and political boundaries to explore the historical connections and cultural exchanges between people across nations.

Prior to the inaugural session, a plenary session was held under the chairmanship of Ambassador Shashank (IFS, Retd.), Former Foreign Secretary, Ministry of External Affairs and Former President of Antar Rashtriya Sahayog Parishad (ARSP). The session featured Diana Mickevičienė, Ambassador of Lithuania to India; Ambassador Jagnnath Sami, High Commissioner of Fiji to India; Ms. Lily Pandeya, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture; and Shri T.C.A. Raghavan, former diplomat and author, as speakers. Ms. Priyanka Chandra, Director, ICR(International Cultural Relations)  Division, Ministry of Culture, moderated the session. Ambassadors and delegates participating in the conference were also present.

The conference seeks to renew the scholarly legacy of the Greater India Society through interdisciplinary research and international collaboration, exploring historical cultural exchanges between India and the world. The deliberations cover ten themes, examining shared traditions in philosophy, religion, languages, arts, textiles, cuisine, performing arts, trade and diaspora communities across regions. Organised under the Brihattar Bharat Scheme (2026–2031), the initiative aims to advance collaborative research, documentation, digitisation and preservation of shared cultural heritage. It also seeks to strengthen international academic partnerships and promote the global dissemination of research on India’s cultural connections with the world.

  ***

2323568.title: ITRA, Jamnagar to Organise National Symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on Artificial Intelligence in Ayurveda
2323568.body_html:
AYUSH
ITRA, Jamnagar to Organise National Symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on Artificial Intelligence in Ayurveda
Two-day event on October 15–16 to explore the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies on the occasion of the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, under the Ministry of Ayush, will organise the Dr. P. M. Mehta Oration and the two-day national symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on October 15 and 16, 2026, to mark the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day. The central theme of the symposium is ‘Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Ayurveda’. The event aims to explore opportunities for advancing research, innovation and healthcare services through the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies.

The programme will be held under the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA. Hon’ble Member of Parliament Smt. Poonamben Madam will attend as the Chief Guest. Mr. Sameer Pujari, Head of Data, Digital Health, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence in the Division of Health Systems at the World Health Organization (WHO), Switzerland, and Dr. Shyama Kuruvilla, Director of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, will also participate in the event. Distinguished guests will include Prof. Shailendra Saraf, Director, National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER), Gandhinagar; Dr. Mansi Deshpande, Vice-Chancellor, Gujarat Ayurved University; and Dr. Manoj Nesari, former Adviser (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush.

The participation of these eminent experts is expected to facilitate meaningful deliberations on the convergence of Ayurveda and modern digital technologies, with a focus on research and innovation. National and international experts will discuss the potential applications of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in Ayurvedic research, drug development, education and healthcare delivery.

The symposium will feature expert lectures, academic discussions, deliberations on research and technological collaboration, institutional recognitions and cultural programmes. Special emphasis will be placed on the ethical, scientific and practical applications of AI in Ayurvedic research, drug development, quality assurance, medical education and healthcare services.

Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, said that the integration of Ayurveda and artificial intelligence could open up new avenues for research and innovation. She emphasised that connecting traditional knowledge with modern scientific and data-driven approaches could contribute meaningfully to the advancement of Ayurveda, knowledge exchange and the strengthening of public healthcare services.

Through this initiative, ITRA, Jamnagar, aims to provide a common platform for Ayurveda scholars, researchers, practitioners and technology experts, while promoting responsible technological innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration in traditional medicine.

About ITRA, Jamnagar

Dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on October 15, 2020, ITRA is the first institution in the country to receive the status of an Institution of National Importance in the field of Ayurveda. Located in Jamnagar, a city renowned for its historical and academic traditions in Ayurveda, the Institute promotes education and research through programmes ranging from undergraduate to doctoral levels, along with courses related to Ayurveda pharmacy, yoga and naturopathy.

The Institute operates a 300-bed hospital accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH), where an average of approximately 1,000 patients receive treatment daily through the Outpatient Department (OPD). Since its establishment, the Institute has provided consultation and treatment to a total of 18,47,807 patients through its OPD, while 27,520 patients have received inpatient care. Currently, 20 OPDs are functioning across various departments of the Institute. In addition, weekly OPD services are provided at eight locations across Jamnagar city and district.

The Institute also houses six laboratories accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), equipped with modern scientific instruments, along with dedicated facilities for yoga and naturopathy.

In the fields of education and research, ITRA has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 27 institutions, including 18 national and nine international institutions. Its Ayurveda library houses more than 30,000 books and over 5,000 manuscripts. The Institute also maintains an animal house facility for medical and pharmaceutical research in accordance with prescribed standards.

2323564.title: KAUMARACON 2026 to Begin at AIIA, New Delhi, on October 15; Vice-President to Address International Ayurveda Paediatrics Conference
2323564.body_html:
AYUSH
KAUMARACON 2026 to Begin at AIIA, New Delhi, on October 15; Vice-President to Address International Ayurveda Paediatrics Conference
Three-Day Conference from October 15–17 to Bring Together National and International Experts in Child Healthcare
AIIA to Celebrate Foundation Day on October 17
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, will organise KAUMARACON 2026, the International Conference on Kaumarabhritya (Ayurveda Paediatrics), from October 15 to 17, 2026, at its Sarita Vihar campus in New Delhi.

The three-day conference will bring together experts, academicians, researchers, practitioners and students from India and abroad to deliberate on advancements in Ayurveda-based child healthcare, research and clinical practice.

The inaugural session on October 15 will be attended by the Hon’ble Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, as the Chief Guest. Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, will attend as the Guest of Honour. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Maneesha Upendra Kothekar, Chairperson, National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), will also be present.

Highlighting the Institute’s journey and achievements, Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said that the Institute, conceptualised in 2002 and dedicated to the nation by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in 2017, is entering its tenth year. He noted that AIIA has made significant progress in Ayurveda education, patient care and research. AIIA, New Delhi, has more than 200 inpatient beds and advanced diagnostic facilities, while the establishment of AIIA Goa in 2022 has further expanded its institutional reach. He added that KAUMARACON 2026 reflects the Institute’s commitment to advancing specialised Ayurveda healthcare, particularly in the field of child health.

AIIA is affiliated with the University of Delhi for postgraduate education and PhD research programmes and has received NAAC A++ accreditation. Its hospital is accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH). The Institute undertakes academic, intramural, extramural and industry-sponsored research projects and publishes three research journals.

Kaumarabhritya: Advancing Comprehensive Child Healthcare

Kaumarabhritya is a specialised branch of Ayurveda that focuses on child health and well-being, including growth and development, nutrition, immunity, mental health and the management of childhood diseases.

The Department of Kaumarabhritya at AIIA provides outpatient and inpatient services, newborn care through a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), vaccination, mental healthcare and skin care. The department also operates a specialised outpatient service for cancer care in children and attends to approximately 120–150 children daily in its outpatient section.

The department has established the KINDER Lab (Kaumarabhritya Initiative for Neurology, Dermatology, Respiratory and related areas), a specialised diagnostic facility supporting clinical assessment and research in paediatric healthcare.

Prof. Dr. Rajagopala S., Head of the Department of Kaumarabhritya, AIIA, and Organising Chairman of KAUMARACON 2026, said that children’s health and well-being are fundamental to building a healthy society. He emphasised that Kaumarabhritya addresses the comprehensive healthcare needs of children, from nutrition and immunity to physical growth, mental well-being and disease management. He added that the conference would facilitate scientific exchange, dissemination of research findings and collaboration among professionals working in Ayurveda paediatrics.

The third edition of KAUMARACON follows the conferences held in 2019 and 2023 at Ayurveda University, Jodhpur, Rajasthan. The 2026 edition is expected to attract more than 500 participants, including experts, teachers, practitioners, postgraduate scholars and students from across the country. International experts from Brazil, the United States, Germany, Sri Lanka and Nepal are also expected to participate online.

The scientific programme will include a pre-conference workshop on computer-aided drug designing (Ayurinformatics) and diagnostics in paediatrics, an oration lecture, six scientific sessions, including a session with international experts, and 12 parallel sessions.

More than 175 scientific papers are scheduled to be presented during the conference. The deliberations will provide a platform for sharing research outcomes, clinical experiences and innovative approaches in Ayurveda paediatrics. The conference aims to promote evidence-based scientific dialogue, encourage interdisciplinary collaboration and strengthen the role of Ayurveda in comprehensive child healthcare.

The three-day programme will culminate on October 17 with the Foundation Day celebrations of the All India Institute of Ayurveda, commemorating the Institute’s establishment, institutional growth and contributions to Ayurveda education, healthcare and research.

The Foundation Day programme will highlight the Institute’s achievements in academic excellence, patient care, research and the development of specialised healthcare services. Faculty members, students, researchers, practitioners and invited guests are expected to participate in the celebrations.

Through KAUMARACON 2026 and its Foundation Day celebrations, AIIA seeks to promote specialised paediatric healthcare, strengthen scientific research and foster knowledge exchange, while advancing Ayurveda’s contribution to the country’s healthcare system.

2323562.title: India and Brunei Darussalam Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at Third Joint Trade Committee Meeting
2323562.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and Brunei Darussalam Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at Third Joint Trade Committee Meeting
Discussions Focus on Expanding Bilateral Trade, Improving Market Access and Facilitating Business-to-Business Exchanges
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi

The third meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was convened to review bilateral trade and economic cooperation and identify avenues for strengthening commercial ties between the two countries. The meeting was co-chaired by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, Shri Amit Verma, and Permanent Secretary (Economy & Trade), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Brunei Darussalam, Dr. May Fa'ezah Ahmad Ariffin. Representatives from relevant Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries participated in the deliberations.

The discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, addressing market access priorities and identifying institutional mechanisms to facilitate business-to-business exchanges. Both sides also deliberated on facilitating exports of agricultural and animal products from India to Brunei Darussalam, with a view to supporting food security and diversifying trade.

Pharmaceuticals, healthcare and energy were identified as key areas for further cooperation. Both sides explored opportunities for regulatory collaboration, procurement and healthcare services, recognising the potential for greater engagement in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors. Discussions on energy covered traditional and emerging energy partnerships to support sustained industrial growth.

The two sides also emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties and commercial outreach through cooperation in tourism and participation in trade fairs and exhibitions. They noted that targeted trade promotion events and reciprocal business delegations could help identify investment opportunities in manufacturing, infrastructure and services.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining regular communication between relevant nodal agencies and working groups to monitor follow-up actions and advance the trade and investment objectives discussed during the meeting.

The next meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee will be held in Brunei Darussalam.

***

2323554.title: Close defence-academia-industry collaboration key to accelerating development & adoption of indigenous tech amid evolving nature of warfare: Raksha Mantri
2323554.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Close defence-academia-industry collaboration key to accelerating development & adoption of indigenous tech amid evolving nature of warfare: Raksha Mantri
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for close collaboration among the Defence Forces, DRDO, academic institutions, defence public sector undertakings and private industry, including start-ups, to accelerate the development, adoption & continuous upgradation of indigenous technologies amidst the rapidly evolving nature of warfare. Speaking at the launch of IIT Kanpur’s ‘Greater Than Us’ fundraising campaign in New Delhi on October 14, 2026, he emphasised that strengthening indigenous technological capabilities is strategically crucial as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, advanced sensors, cybersecurity and space-based technologies are reshaping military dynamics.

Raksha Mantri underscored the growing interlinkage between national security and technological capability, stressing that IITs can make a significant contribution by aligning academic research with operational defence requirements and industry needs. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ commitment lies at the centre of its ‘Viksit Bharat’ vision as it aims to create a technologically capable, economically competitive, innovative and confident nation, which is not just a consumer of knowledge & technology but an active contributor to their creation, he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the importance of strong institutions of higher education and research in realising this vision, noting that the Government has made sustained efforts to strengthen the ecosystem, whose growing contribution to innovation and entrepreneurship is reflected in the IIT ecosystem’s support for over 6,000 start-ups, 56 unicorns and nearly 5,000 patents. “These achievements demonstrate that IITs are not merely institutions that impart knowledge, but are increasingly becoming engines of innovation, enterprise and technological capability. Institutions such as IIT Kanpur play a significant role in advancing India’s development by expanding scientific capabilities, strengthening the innovation ecosystem and creating solutions that benefit society,” he added.

Acknowledging the initiatives undertaken in this direction, Raksha Mantri made special mention of IIT Kanpur’s DRDO-Industry-Academia Centre of Excellence and welcomed the proposal to establish a School of Defence Technologies at the Institute. He added that the proposal to set up a National Military Drone Technology Hub at IIT Kanpur, in collaboration with the Ministry of Defence to fast-track indigenisation and innovation to gain combat edge, has made significant progress and its approval process is nearing completion. 

Shri Rajnath Singh exuded confidence that such partnerships would bring scientific talent, institutional expertise and the operational experience of the Defence Forces under one umbrella to develop indigenous technologies of strategic importance. Credible academic institutions can play a crucial role in translating research into practical defence applications and addressing the evolving technological requirements of the military, he said.

On IIT Kanpur’s role in strengthening Uttar Pradesh’s industrial ecosystem, Raksha Mantri said that the institute can serve as a bridge between scientific research and industrial application, emerging technologies and enterprise. He noted that Kanpur’s rich industrial legacy, coupled with IIT Kanpur’s technological expertise can generate new opportunities for entrepreneurship, employment, investment and economic growth, contributing to the state’s vision of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy.

Shri Rajnath Singh referred to the C3i Cybersecurity Technology Innovation Hub at IIT Kanpur and the institute’s medical school, terming them as significant initiatives in cybersecurity, healthcare and medical technology innovation. He stated that research in emerging areas such as advanced materials, semiconductors, quantum technology and environmental sustainability would be critical to addressing national priorities and developing future technologies.

Stressing the need for sustained investment in research and innovation, Raksha Mantri referred to the Government’s approval of Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Scheme to catalyse private-sector investment in research & advanced technologies. “While public policy can create an enabling environment, institutions must nurture talent and generate ideas, and industry must help translate innovations into practical applications and scale them up,” he said.

Through the ‘Greater Than Us’ campaign, IIT Kanpur aims to raise US$1 billion by March 2029, which is the largest fundraising campaign ever undertaken by any IIT. Rs 4,155 crore, nearly half of the goal, has already been committed by alumni, donors, corporate partners, and the government. The objective is to strengthen IIT Kanpur’s research infrastructure, nurture talent, and accelerate the development and commercialisation of indigenous technologies & innovations to support India’s vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Shri Rajnath Singh expressed confidence that the campaign would support stronger research capabilities, advanced facilities, opportunities for talented students and solutions to national & global challenges. He called upon the institute’s alumni, industry, philanthropic supporters and institutional partners to contribute through financial support, mentorship, research partnerships and professional networks. 

Prof Manindra Agrawal, Director, IIT Kanpur; Shri Awanish Kumar Awasthi, Advisor to the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and faculty, students & alumni of the institute were present on the occasion.

2323546.title: India Strengthens Science and Technology Partnerships with Global South through Inaugural Ministry of External Affairs–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme
2323546.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India Strengthens Science and Technology Partnerships with Global South through Inaugural Ministry of External Affairs–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme
33 Ambassadors and Embassy Officials from 29 Countries Explore CSIR's Innovations in Sustainable Infrastructure, Genomics and Healthcare
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative to strengthen India's science and technology partnerships with countries of the Global South, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), in collaboration with the New, Emerging and Strategic Technologies (NEST) Division of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India, launched the inaugural edition of the MEA–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme on 14 October 2026.

The programme brought together 33 Ambassadors and senior embassy officials representing 29 countries, providing them with first-hand exposure to CSIR's scientific capabilities, indigenous technologies and advanced research infrastructure. The inaugural edition featured visits to two premier CSIR laboratories in New Delhi—the CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) and the CSIR-Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (CSIR-IGIB).

Jointly conceptualised by CSIR and MEA, the initiative seeks to build stronger scientific and technological linkages with partner countries, particularly across the Global South, by showcasing India's research capabilities and identifying opportunities for collaborative research, technology transfer, capacity building and deployment of innovative solutions addressing shared developmental challenges.

During the inaugural session, Dr. Rama Swami Bansal, Head, International S&T Affairs Directorate, CSIR, presented an overview of CSIR's scientific and technological capabilities, its international engagements and potential models for collaboration with countries of the Global South. Dr. Sadre Alam, Joint Secretary, MEA, outlined the genesis, objectives and expectations of the programme, highlighting its role in fostering international partnerships through science and technology.

Dr. Chalumuri Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, and Dr. Souvik Maiti, Director, CSIR-IGIB, introduced the visiting delegation to their respective institutes' research strengths, technological achievements and contributions in the areas of sustainable infrastructure and healthcare.

At CSIR-CRRI, the delegation witnessed several advanced research facilities and technologies, including the Driving Simulator, Cyclic Load Test Facility, Steel Slag Laboratory, a 3D model of bio-binder technology and drone models. A major highlight was the live demonstration of Ecofix, a steel slag-based instant pothole repair mix developed for rapid road maintenance. The demonstration showcased how indigenous technologies can transform industrial waste into valuable resources while offering practical, sustainable and cost-effective solutions for infrastructure development.

The delegation subsequently visited CSIR-IGIB, where participants were introduced to advanced facilities in genome sequencing, biosafety, zebrafish research, biobanking and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). The visit offered insights into India's growing capabilities in genomics, biomedical research, precision healthcare and biotechnology, highlighting opportunities for scientific cooperation and capacity building in the healthcare sector.

The programme concluded with an interactive session during which the visiting Ambassadors and embassy officials shared their perspectives, priorities and expectations for future engagement with CSIR. Discussions explored opportunities for joint research, technology partnerships, knowledge exchange, capacity building and adaptation of Indian technologies to address the specific developmental needs of partner countries.

The inaugural MEA–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme represents an important step towards translating India's scientific and technological strengths into meaningful international partnerships. By bringing foreign diplomatic representatives directly into CSIR laboratories and facilitating interactions with scientists and technology developers, the initiative provides a platform for identifying practical areas of cooperation and accelerating the adoption of innovative solutions.

The programme is expected to open new avenues for sustained engagement between CSIR and countries of the Global South, reinforcing India's commitment to sharing scientific knowledge, technological expertise and indigenous innovations for inclusive and sustainable development.

2323543.title: Defence Accounts Department Organises Shramdaan under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ Campaign
2323543.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Defence Accounts Department Organises Shramdaan under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ Campaign
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Defence Accounts Department organised a nationwide Shramdaan under the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign, with field offices participating in the two-week-long Swachhata Pakhwada and planting over 25,000 trees under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative.

The campaign concluded with a cleanliness drive at MCD Primary School, Bagdola, Dwarka, New Delhi, led by Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) Smt Alka Nangia Arora, in association with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. Officers and staff of the CGDA office and MCD officials participated in the drive, which also included sapling plantation.

2323545.title: CEA Brainstorming Event: Making Indian Power Sector AI Enabled (International Conference cum Exhibition)
2323545.body_html:
Ministry of Power
CEA Brainstorming Event: Making Indian Power Sector AI Enabled (International Conference cum Exhibition)
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

Under the theme “Making Indian Power Sector AI Enabled”, the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) held the first day of its two-day international conference-cum-exhibition at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi, on 14 October 2026.

Shri Manohar Lal, Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs and Shri Prahlad Joshi, Union Minister of Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy Government of India, conveyed their messages on the occasion. Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy; Shri Jitin Prasada, Union Minister of State for Commerce & Industry and Electronics & Information Technology; Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power; Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA ; Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy; were also present during inauguration.

The inaugural session featured addresses by senior government dignitaries and the leadership of CEA. Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power and Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, addressed the gathering, highlighting the importance of advancing India’s power sector in response to emerging challenges and technological developments. Further, Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA, set the context for the conference. It was highlighted that CEA has already formed a team of 54 artificial intelligence (AI) enthusiast/ brand ambassador. They will take it forward in all areas of power sector. All power utilities may also have dedicated AI team.

The session also saw the launch of CEA’s Vidhyut Dwar Portal and the release of the CEA Manual on Transmission Planning Criteria, 2026. The CEA Employee Awards were also distributed during the session, recognising outstanding performance and exceptional contributions by CEA employees.

The event brought together stakeholders from the power sector to deliberate on practical applications of AI across generation, regulation, renewable energy integration, transmission and distribution systems. The technical programme on Day 1 featured six parallel thematic discussions: Optimizing Generation through AI for Conventional Sources; Regulatory Reforms using AI; AI-Enabled Renewable Energy Integration for a Flexible Grid; Modernising Distribution through AI; Transmission Modernization, Grid Stability and System Restoration through AI; and AI-Enabled Rooftop Solar, Microgrids and Mini-Grids.

The session on conventional generation examined how AI may support heat-rate and combustion optimisation, flexible plant operation, predictive maintenance, digital twins, auxiliary-power optimisation and emissions monitoring. These applications may help improve plant availability and operational efficiency while enabling conventional stations to respond more flexibly to changing system requirements as renewable energy expands.

Discussions on regulatory reforms considered the use of AI, advanced analytics and digital tools for reviewing aggregate revenue requirement and tariff filings, validating submissions, organising regulatory knowledge, monitoring compliance and supporting market surveillance. The discussions also highlighted that AI may function as a human-supervised decision-support tool and may not replace statutory judgment, procedural fairness or regulatory accountability.

The session on renewable energy integration explored AI-based forecasting of variable renewable generation and demand, improved visibility of distributed energy resources, storage optimisation, congestion management and coordination of renewable assets through virtual power plants. The focus was on enabling a flexible and reliable grid through better data, forecasting and coordination of resources.

Modernisation of distribution systems was discussed with reference to the growing availability of smart-meter, network and asset data. Potential applications included demand forecasting, power-procurement optimisation, predictive maintenance of distribution transformers, outage detection and fault localisation, energy auditing, loss analytics, billing and revenue assurance, consumer services and regulatory reporting. These applications may support more reliable supply, lower losses and more responsive consumer services.

The discussion on transmission modernisation and grid stability examined AI-enabled network planning, corridor and right-of-way optimisation, drone-based inspection and computer vision, predictive maintenance, digital twins, dynamic line rating, congestion and contingency analysis, inertia forecasting, and decision support for system restoration and black-start preparedness. Participants considered the data, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, governance and capacity-building requirements that would support adoption at scale.

The session on AI-enabled rooftop solar, microgrids and mini-grids focused on intelligent planning and operation of decentralised energy resources. Topics included rooftop solar identification and sizing, feeder-level forecasting, autonomous microgrid operation, storage optimisation, agriculture-feeder analytics, demand response and aggregation of rooftop solar, batteries, electric vehicles and flexible loads.

Across the discussions, a common theme was the need to move from isolated technology demonstrations towards prioritised, implementable use cases supported by reliable data, interoperability, appropriate safeguards, institutional capability and measurable performance indicators. The deliberations are intended to inform practical pathways for responsible adoption and scaling of AI applications in the Indian power sector.

The two-day brainstorming event is being organised as part of overall initiative aims to develop a coordinated and outcome-oriented approach to AI adoption across the electricity value chain, supporting efficient and flexible power supply, reliable and intelligent networks, responsive institutions, secure digitalisation and resilient domestic industrial capability.

2323532.title: MCL commits ₹22.64 Crore for Five CSR projects in Sundargarh District
2323532.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
MCL commits ₹22.64 Crore for Five CSR projects in Sundargarh District
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), under its CSR initiative has signed MoUs with the District Administration of Sundargarh on tuesday for five developmental projects worth ₹22.64 crore. The projects include the rejuvenation and beautification of Kata Bandha (₹4.32 crore), Brahamani Bandha (₹3.98 crore) and Abdul Hussain Bandha (₹2.69 crore); freshwater inland aquaculture in mining-affected areas of Hemgir Block (₹3.81 crore); and renovation, improvement and construction of tanks under Talsara Assembly Constituency (₹7.84 crore) in Sundargarh district.

The General Manager (CSR), MCL, and the District Collector, Sundargarh, signed the MoUs for project implementation by the District Administration.

Aligned with the “Amrit Sarovar” mission, the rejuvenation of water bodies will promote water conservation, groundwater replenishment and environmental improvement while developing leisure destinations, supporting small-scale tourism and generating local economic activity. The works include embankment protection, construction of pathways, bathing steps, stone packing, railings, seating spaces, electrical works and horticulture, aligning with Mission Amrit Sarovar.

The aquaculture project will be implemented in-line with the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana which will benefit over 700 small-scale farmers and FPO members through the development of 50 new ponds and renovation of 20 existing ponds. Besides this, it also includes formation of women-led fish seed production units and Custom Hiring Centres, an Aqua Business School and a Fish Farmers Producers' Organisation (FFPO).

Through these initiatives, MCL aims to strengthen water resource management, promote sustainable livelihoods, support women-led enterprises and contribute to the socio-economic development of communities across Sundargarh district of Odisha.

2323502.title: Release of 121st Issue of Sarvekshana, Journal of Official Statistics
2323502.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Release of 121st Issue of Sarvekshana, Journal of Official Statistics
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

The 121st Issue of Sarvekshana, the premier bi-annual Journal of Official Statistics was released by National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

Sarvekshana serves as a prominent platform for disseminating research based on data from National Sample Survey (NSS) and other Official Statistics. Recognised for its academic rigour and policy relevance, the journal contributes to the advancement of statistical research and promotes the wider use of official statistical data. It is circulated among researchers, data users, Ministries/Departments, and reputed national and international institutions.

  The 121st Issue features three technical papers, addressing diverse and significant aspects of Official Statistics, namely :-

  1. Impact of In-kind Social Transfer on Level of Living of Indian Households.
  2. Role of Size of Factories in Efficiency – A Study Based on Data from Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2022–23.
  3. Effect of Adopting PPS Circular Systematic Sampling in Annual Survey of Industries: A Simulation Study.

  Each paper has undergone a rigorous peer-review and editorial process to ensure its quality, accuracy, and relevance. The studies contribute to a deeper understanding of statistical methodologies, industrial efficiency and the role of social transfers in shaping household living standards.

  In addition to the technical papers, the Issue presents highlights of two Surveys conducted by the NSS, viz. the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) 2025 (January–December 2025) and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025 (January–December 2025). The inclusion of these highlights provides readers with key insights into the unincorporated sector and labour market trends, further enhancing the issue's relevance for researchers, policymakers, and other users of official statistics.

  Through the continued publication of Sarvekshana, NSSTA reaffirms its commitment to fostering research in Official Statistics, encouraging the wider application of statistical data, and strengthening the analytical foundations of evidence-based policymaking. The Journal remains an important medium for sharing statistical knowledge, promoting methodological innovation, and supporting informed decision-making.

The Issue can be readily accessed on the websites (www.mospi.gov.in) and NSSTA (www.nssta.gov.in).
