2322664.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum
2322664.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum
The vision I have come with is power to empower; Beyond the power to control, power to enable; Beyond the power to compete, power to collaborate; Beyond the power to succeed, power to help others succeed: PM
Our constant endeavour is to ensure that India's capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well: PM
India's progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities: PM
We do not grow at anyone's cost; We grow with the world and for the world: PM
In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability: PM
For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction: PM
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today addressed the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. Acknowledging Mr. Michael Bloomberg’s earlier remarks, the Prime Minister celebrated the forum's unprecedented debut in India. He praised the platform's ability to unite the world’s brightest minds to deliberate on key global themes, including the economy, technology, energy, and international affairs. "I congratulate Mr. Bloomberg and his entire team; you have chosen the right place at the right time,” remarked Shri Modi.

Addressing the summit's core focus on emerging global powers, the Prime Minister highlighted a monumental paradigm shift in the 21st century's third decade, where technology, data, knowledge, and innovation have become the ultimate metrics of power. He challenged the audience to reconsider the fundamental purpose of this power, questioning whether it should elevate a select few or actively democratize opportunities for millions, emphasizing a shift from controlling to enabling and from competing to collaborating. '“Moving beyond the power to succeed to the power to help others succeed, the vision with which I have come here today is Power to Empower,” asserted Shri Modi.

Grounding this philosophy in ancient cultural wisdom, the Prime Minister quoted traditional Sanskrit texts emphasizing that the true value of knowledge, wealth, and power is determined entirely by how ethically they are utilized. He stressed that understanding this profound purpose of power is absolutely essential for navigating today’s complex global dynamics. "Meaning, the true value of Power lies in its Purpose,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Translating these ancient ideals into modern administration, the Prime Minister stated that the concept of 'Power to Empower' is not a mere global sermon but a deeply ingrained cultural tradition actively applied to the nation’s governance and work culture. He announced his intention to illustrate this transformative philosophy using concrete examples of the nation's progress. "Therefore, I will take my point forward using examples from India itself,” noted Shri Modi.

Showcasing the vibrant dynamism of the 'Mother of Democracy', the Prime Minister proudly listed the nation's massive linguistic diversity, its 80,000 publications, and over a thousand television channels. He emphasized that in the modern social media era, the nation's half-a-billion YouTube and Instagram users engage in robust, open debates, proving that digital power is actively fueling democratic discourse. "In present times, what has played a major role in this is digital power,” observed Shri Modi.

Recounting the aggressive battle against digital exclusion, the Prime Minister noted that just over a decade ago, mere access to mobile phones and the internet was considered an elite privilege. He explained that since 2014, the government deliberately slashed data prices down to ensure that everyone from small-town students to village shopkeepers could instantly access knowledge and markets. "Meaning, Connectivity in India has not just connected people; it has also connected opportunities,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the extraordinary scale of financial inclusion, the Prime Minister invited international guests to witness a seamless digital payments ecosystem where a humble street vendor and a massive car showroom utilize the exact same technological platform. He framed this radical financial democratization as the ultimate proof of inclusive technology at work. "This is the strength of Inclusive Technology,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing the nation's commitment to international technological solidarity, the Prime Minister declared that domestic digital capabilities are continuously shared with the Global South and other partner countries to help them build their own Digital Public Infrastructure. He cited the open-source CoWIN platform, deployed during the pandemic, as a prime example of domestic innovation actively unlocking global possibilities. "Meaning, our capability should empower humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.

Championing the massive democratization of innovation, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's explosive startup growth, which skyrocketed from a few hundred in 2014 to over 2.5 lakh today. He proudly pointed out that nearly half of these startups originate from smaller cities and that over 45 percent feature female leadership, proving that the power to solve problems is reaching all segments of society. "Meaning, opportunities for Innovation are reaching more people,” noted Shri Modi.

Pivoting to the core philosophy of public administration, the Prime Minister stated that governmental authority must never aim to create systemic dependency, but must instead focus on rendering citizens entirely capable and empowered. He credited this exact empowerment-driven governance model for successfully lifting 25 crore people out of poverty over the last decade. "And India is walking on this very path,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing the systemic eradication of corruption, the Prime Minister highlighted the deployment of the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer systems to deliver government assistance directly into citizens' bank accounts. "This has reduced corruption, increased the convenience of the country's citizens, and established a direct relationship between Government and Citizen,” observed Shri Modi.

Illustrating this empowerment philosophy on the global stage, the Prime Minister recalled the critical vaccine shortages during the COVID-19 pandemic and questioned whether life-saving manufacturing power should have been hoarded by a few nations. He expressed immense pride that the nation chose a humanitarian path by supplying vaccines to over 100 countries. "Our Manufacturing Capability became a medium of assistance for other countries as well,” asserted Shri Modi.

Presenting a unique example of inclusive foresight, the Prime Minister mentioned a recent domestic AI Impact summit that expanded the dialogue beyond human applications to actively discuss how artificial intelligence could benefit animal welfare. He used this anecdote to prove that an increasingly capable nation will continually generate broader benefits for the entire world. "The more capable India becomes, the more beneficial it will be for humanity, for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Calling for a balanced global order, the Prime Minister argued that while competition, innovation, and national strength are vital, they must be fundamentally paired with compassion and a commitment to solving global challenges like climate change, water governance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies. He insisted that the world desperately needs powers that actively create new, shared opportunities. "Power is not just the ability to move ahead; it is also the ability to empower others to move ahead,” asserted Shri Modi.

Demonstrating the nation's fierce commitment to climate action, the Prime Minister recalled the bold 2015 Paris Agreement pledge to achieve 40 percent installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030. He proudly announced that the nation surpassed this target in November 2021, nine years ahead of schedule, becoming the very first G20 country to do so. "This was not just about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a sign of India's changing Energy Journey,” noted Shri Modi.

Quantifying this massive green energy pivot, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's renewable energy capacity has skyrocketed from a mere 75 gigawatts in 2014 to approximately 300 gigawatts today. He highlighted this four-fold expansion as a monumental achievement in the country's sustainable development.

Explaining the grassroots economic benefits of this energy transition, the Prime Minister detailed how the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM schemes are actively empowering households and farmers to generate their own solar power and slash input costs. He noted that these initiatives have added over 30 gigawatts of capacity, reducing carbon emissions by over 30 million tonnes annually while simultaneously protecting nature and enriching citizens. "And it is also empowering people,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Contrasting the nation's cooperative ethos with global power struggles, the Prime Minister stated that amidst international races for dominance, the country is intentionally forging a distinct, stabilizing path. He noted that the current decade serves as an undeniable witness to this unique national temperament. "In this race for Power in the world, India is moving ahead with a different temperament,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the cascading shocks defining the 21st century's third decade, the Prime Minister listed the rapid succession of global pandemics, regional wars, and severe supply chain disruptions affecting critical minerals, energy, and trade. He painted a stark picture of a world where one crisis barely recedes before another emerges. "The world searches for a way out of one crisis; by then, a new crisis emerges,” observed Shri Modi.

Condemning the weaponization of global interconnectedness, the Prime Minister lamented that essential elements like supply chains, energy, minerals, technology, and payment systems are being actively exploited as instruments of pressure and dominance. He warned that the integration achieved by decades of globalization is rapidly fracturing into dangerous geopolitical chokepoints. "The roots that globalization created in past decades, when and where they turned into chokepoints, we all are seeing this,” noted Shri Modi.

Addressing the resulting global crisis of confidence amidst rapid technological disruption and demographic challenges, the Prime Minister stated that the world is desperately searching for reliable partners who will maintain supply lines and honor commitments during crises. He positioned the nation as the ultimate dependable ally offering a radically different, cooperative approach to global relations. "And it is right here, India stands before you with a different temperament, a different thought,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Defining the nation's global operating model, the Prime Minister declared that the country's 21st-century progress is fundamentally defined by collaborative, inclusive advancement. He cited the nation's role as the provider of one-fifth of the world's generic medicines, a pioneer of digital identity models, and a trusted talent hub hosting over 2,000 Global Capability Centres servicing the globe. "India's progress is the story of moving forward by collaborating with everyone, by taking everyone along,” asserted Shri Modi.

Reiterating the nation's role as a stabilizing global force, the Prime Minister emphasized that whenever the world requires a steady pillar, the country responsibly extends its hand to support the international community. He outlined a fundamental philosophy of equitable advancement on the global stage. “We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world, and for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Drawing upon profound historical legacy, the Prime Minister pointed out that the nation historically gifted the concept of 'Zero' to humanity without ever demanding royalties, and continues to operate with that exact same selfless spirit today. He contrasted this with historical global organizations that operated strictly on self-interest. "And even today India is working with this same spirit,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the nation's track record of building inclusive global platforms, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Big Cat Alliance, the Global Biofuel Alliance, IMEC, and Mission LiFE. He stressed that these platforms were intentionally designed to generate universal benefits for all forms of life rather than serving narrow geopolitical interests. "Meaning those which benefit everyone, which benefit every life, India has taken such initiatives,” asserted Shri Modi.

Summarizing the overarching philosophical framework driving the nation's foreign policy, the Prime Minister invoked the visions of 'One Sun, One World, One Grid', 'One Earth, One Family, One Future', and 'One Earth, One Health'. He emphasized that the country exclusively utilizes its power to connect, unite, and elevate others. "And even in this, the use of Power is only to Empower others,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Showcasing the nation's macroeconomic resilience amidst global uncertainty, the Prime Minister proudly cited a 7.8 percent growth rate for the April-June quarter, a current account deficit slashed to a mere 0.61 percent, and foreign exchange reserves exceeding 700 billion dollars. He declared that the domestic banking system is currently enjoying its strongest position in decades. "In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability,” asserted Shri Modi.

Attributing recent sovereign rating upgrades to this immense structural strength, the Prime Minister highlighted the relentless execution of systemic reforms, including the implementation of GST to create a unified national market, the drafting of Insolvency Laws, the consolidation of 29 labor codes into four, and the decriminalization of hundreds of minor business offenses. He assured global investors that this unstoppable momentum is a deliberate, proactive choice driving the nation forward. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address by invoking the ancient Vedic mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the global community to walk, speak, and understand one another together to multiply collective strength and solve major global challenges. He expressed profound confidence that the Bloomberg New Economy Forum would serve as a massive platform to propagate this exact spirit of creating shared global opportunities.

2322663.title: DARPG releases the 50th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for September, 2026
2322663.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2322663.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DARPG releases the 50th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for September, 2026
A total of 99,134 PG cases received for the States/UTs & 1,15,168 PG cases redressed in September, 2026,
Under the Sevottam Scheme, 1,312 training courses completed, in which ~43,738 officers have been trained in the last five Financial Years
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) 50th monthly report for States/UTs for September, 2026. The said report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal by the States/UTs.

In September, 2026, 99,134 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 1,15,168 PG cases were redressed. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in September, 2026 with 45,970 PG cases, followed by Andhra Pradesh with 8,340 PG cases. As of 30th September, 2026, the total pendency of PG cases on the CPGRAMS portal stands at 2,37,128 across all States and UTs. Moreover, 23 States/UTs have more than 1,000 pending PG cases each.

The report provides the data for new users registered on CPGRAMS through CPGRAMS Portal during September, 2026. A total of 92,822 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in September, 2026, through various channels, out of which, the highest registrations are from Uttar Pradesh (15,742). The Feedback collected through Call Centre and Online are a total of 1,87,362 feedbacks in September, 2026, where, 75,568 feedbacks were collected from States/UTs.

The report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in September, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 12,996 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of September, 2026.

The report also provides the total number of training programmes conducted and officers trained over the last five financial years under the Sevottam Scheme. Between FY 2022–23 and FY 2026–27, a total of 1,312 training courses were conducted, training ~43,738 officers.

Key Highlights for the month of September, 2026, are as follows:

General Highlights

  • A Review Meeting was conducted with States/UTs on 24th September, 2026 to review the grievance redressal performance against service delivery benchmarks and identify measures to strengthen grievance redressal.
  • West Bengal completed its full integration with CPGRAMS Portal on 22nd September, 2026.
  • Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27), 1,312 training courses have been completed, in which ~43,738 officers have been trained.
  • In September 2026, Karnataka received the highest number of grievances through CSCs, constituting 54% of the total 12,996 grievances received via CSCs.

Status of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • In September, 2026, 99,134 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 1,15,168 PG cases were redressed, representing the highest disposal of the year.
  • Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in September, 2026 with 45,970 PG cases, followed by Andhra Pradesh and Haryana with 8,340 and 6,437 PG cases respectively.

Status of Pendency of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • 23 States/UTs have more than 1000 pending grievances as on 30th September, 2026.
  • For States/UTs, as on 30th September, 2026, there exists a pendency of 2,37,128 PG cases which represents an approximate 6.3% decrease over the pendency recorded in August 2026.

2322662.title: Strong Statistical Systems Key to Achieving Viksit Bharat @ 2047: Dr. P. K. Mishra
2322662.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Strong Statistical Systems Key to Achieving Viksit Bharat @ 2047: Dr. P. K. Mishra
"Our Statistical Architecture Must Be as Modern and Ambitious as Our National Aspirations”: Dr. P. K. Mishra
"The Quality of Our Data Influences the Quality of Our Decisions and Development Outcomes”: Principal Secretary to PM
"Statistics Are Not Merely an Administrative Requirement, but a Strategic National Asset”: Dr. P. K. Mishra
AI and Advanced Analytics Can Strengthen Official Statistics, but Cannot Substitute for Quality of Statistics: Dr. P. K. Mishra
Dr. P. K. Mishra Delivers Keynote Address at Conference of State Planning, Finance and IT Secretaries Organised by MoSPI
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:40PM by PIB Delhi

Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, Dr. P. K. Mishra, today delivered the keynote address at the inaugural session of the Conference of State Planning, Finance and IT Secretaries, organised by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in New Delhi. Emphasising the importance of credible statistics, data harmonisation and technology-enabled governance, he said a strong statistical system is essential for evidence-based policymaking and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

Dr. Mishra said statistics, data, technology, planning and governance are increasingly interconnected elements of India’s development journey. A robust statistical system, he noted, must enable governments to measure development progress across States and districts, assess policy outcomes, identify gaps and ensure that public resources deliver the intended results. “What cannot be measured cannot be managed effectively. And what cannot be managed effectively cannot be transformed sustainably,” he observed.

Highlighting the need to modernise economic measurement, Dr. Mishra said India’s statistical systems must evolve alongside an economy that is increasingly digital, formalised and interconnected. He noted that the introduction of the new National Accounts Series, with 2022-23 as the base year, alongside updated Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) series, represents an important step towards keeping statistical methodologies aligned with changing economic realities.

Underscoring the importance of State Statistical Systems, Dr. Mishra said India’s development story is fundamentally a story of its States, where policies are implemented, economic activity takes place and citizens experience development outcomes. He called for stronger institutional capacity and closer Centre–State coordination to improve the quality of official statistics.

Dr. Mishra said artificial intelligence, machine learning, geospatial systems, satellite imagery and advanced analytics offer significant opportunities to improve the timeliness, accuracy and usefulness of official statistics. However, he cautioned that technological advancement must remain guided by statistical quality, transparency, privacy, security and accountability. “Speed cannot come at the cost of accuracy. Greater use of data cannot come at the cost of confidentiality,” he said.

Dr. Mishra described statistics as an important instrument of cooperative federalism, enabling States and the Centre to compare outcomes, identify best practices and learn from regional differences. As India progresses towards 2047, he said, national averages alone would not suffice; granular data at State, district and local levels would be increasingly necessary to identify development gaps and guide interventions.

Concluding, Dr. Mishra called for a collective national effort involving MoSPI, State Statistical Offices, Finance, Planning and IT Departments, NITI Aayog, academic institutions and other stakeholders. He said India needs a statistical architecture that is trusted, transparent, technology-enabled, interoperable and policy-relevant. Such a system, he added, would not merely measure India’s transformation but also help guide and accelerate it towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

2322625.title: Khadi & Village Industries: From Tradition to Enterprise
2322625.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Khadi & Village Industries: From Tradition to Enterprise
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 11:12AM by PIB Delhi

A charkha spinning in a village once spoke of nationalism. Today, that spirit is taking new shape through a growing ecosystem of rural enterprises. Honey, herbal products, banana fibre, textiles and other village industries are creating new possibilities for traditional skills.

The spirit of self-reliance continues to resonate with the vision of Vocal for Local and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Traditional skills and local resources are finding new markets through access to finance, technology and training.

This growing connection between local enterprise and consumers is also reflected in the Khadi Mahotsav. The Khadi Mahotsav takes place annually from 2 October to 31 October. With a particular focus on youth, the campaign sensitises them towards Khadi and “Vocal for Local” and encourages the public to buy Khadi and local products.

At the centre of this transformation is the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). It is a statutory body established under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956. The Act mandates KVIC to plan, promote, facilitate, organise and assist village industries. It covers measures related to training, raw materials, marketing, research, and quality improvement. It also supports skill development and research, while providing technical information and facilities related to Khadi and village industries.

In 2025–26, sales of Khadi and Village Industries products reached a historic ₹1.87lakh crore, the highest level recorded (as of May 2026). Compared with 2013–14, sales grew by 501%, while production increased by 380% to ₹1,25,296 crore. Employment in the sector increased by 56% to 2.04 crore. The remuneration paid to artisans has also increased. It rose from ₹4 per hank in 2013–14 to ₹15 per hank currently, an increase of approximately 275%.

One hank is equivalent to 840 yards of yarn in length and one pound by weight.

Building Rural Businesses, One Artisan at a Time

From acquiring skills to accessing markets, a range of interventions is supporting artisans and village industries.

KVIC has a network of 35 departmental and non-departmental training centres. Training covers food products, bakery, beekeeping, agarbatti, candles, motor repairing and several other activities. During FY 2025-26, 79,682 trainees received training under various KVIC training programs.

Women constitute more than 80% of approximately five lakh artisans in the Khadi sector. In 2025–26, 47,382 women received training under various KVIC programmes, accounting for approximately 59% of all trainees.

Training is complemented by interventions including toolkit and equipment distribution, marketing support and other measures.

Since March 2008, the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) has provided employment opportunities to nearly 97.95 lakh people through KVIC.

One such beneficiary is Shri Jitendra Baitha, who established a bakery products manufacturing unit in Bihar in 2020. His venture has an annual turnover of ₹72 lakh and currently provides employment to 20 people, in the local community.

Support also includes enterprise finance and the tools and technology needed for production.

The Gramodyog Vikas Yojana empowers artisans by providing modern machines, toolkits and equipment. During 2025–26, 37,769 such machines, toolkits and equipment were distributed. KVIC, under the scheme, has distributed more than 3.23 lakh machines, toolkits and equipment (May 2026).

These efforts are complemented by measures that strengthen the wider ecosystem in which Khadi institutions and artisans operate.

The Khadi Vikas Yojana helps Khadi institutions improve products, add value and respond to changing market demand. Its Modified Market Development Assistance provides greater flexibility for value addition and market-oriented pricing. During 2024–25, ₹245 crore was disbursed to 1,097 Khadi Institutions, benefiting 1,45,484 artisans.

Access to affordable credit adds another layer of support. Under the Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate Scheme, eligible Khadi institutions can access credit at a concessional interest rate of 4% per annum.

For artisans, the workplace itself also matters. The Workshed Scheme provides improved production spaces and a more congenial working environment. During 2025–26, up to December 2025, 1,309 artisans benefited under the scheme.

These measures support artisans with improved working conditions and access to resources for production.

From Village Enterprises to Wider Markets

Across village industries, traditional skills and local resources are being developed into new businesses and products, supported by technology, training and market linkages. Research and development efforts are strengthening productivity, quality and competitiveness.

Shri S.P. Singh built his enterprise around honey and cookies, with support under the PMEGP scheme through KVIC. Based in Punjab, his business now provides employment to around 200 workers and exports its products to international markets. Honey and cookies are among its key products, with the United States accounting for a major share of exports.

After receiving support in 2010, the enterprise gradually expanded its export presence through participation in international exhibitions. KVIC facilitated participation in exhibitions across Dubai, the United States and the Middle East, helping the enterprise connect with overseas buyers. Today, the business exports to 36 countries and is developing a second unit in Rajpura, Punjab, to expand honey exports to European markets.

For Shri B. Sundaraj, a naturally fragrant plant became the foundation for a village enterprise. Through his Agarbathi Unit, he produces agarbatti, herbal products, Vetiver Agarbathi and Vetiver Samburani. With support under the Gramodyog Vikas Yojana (GVY) during 2024-25, he strengthened his manufacturing capabilities and diversified his product range. This enables him to develop multiple value-added products from a locally available resource. His enterprise illustrates how KVIC support can help translate traditional knowledge and local resources into marketable village industry products.

In Jatti Majra village of Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, Shri Sahil Chaudhary runs a mono-carton manufacturing unit. The enterprise caters to construction and packaging requirements in the region. Established with a project cost of ₹25 lakh, the unit operates under KVIC-supported PMEGP.

The enterprise now records an annual turnover of around ₹45 lakh and provides employment to 23 people. The financial assistance helped translate Chaudhary’s entrepreneurial idea into a functioning manufacturing enterprise. His journey illustrates how local entrepreneurship can contribute to self-reliance, employment and the broader vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat.

Opening New Markets for Village Enterprises

KVIC has expanded both digital and physical channels for reaching consumers. It has an online Khadi India store (www.khadiindia.gov.in) offering a range of products, including clothing and fabrics, grocery, beauty products, essential oils, perfumes and incense sticks.

The Khadi India brand is supported through dedicated publicity and marketing initiatives. These efforts connect traditional products with contemporary consumers. The marketing network extends across the country. It includes 8 departmental Khadi India sales outlets and 15 KVIC branches. Khadi Institutions operate another 8,035 sales outlets nationwide.

National, zonal, state and district exhibitions provide additional market opportunities. KVIC also promotes participation in domestic and international trade fairs.

Khadi: Weaving a Global Story

Khadi is finding new expressions in fashion, with its distinctive craftsmanship showcased at platforms such as New Zealand Fashion Week 2026 and Lakmé Fashion Week 2025. In these events, the heritage techniques were brought together with contemporary designs to create a distinctly modern identity.

From Heritage to Opportunity

The growth of Khadi and Village Industries is reflected in higher production and sales, expanding employment, increased artisan remuneration and new rural businesses. As traditional skills connect with technology, finance and markets, the sector continues to open new avenues for enterprise across rural India.

2322621.title: Taking Voice-First Multilingual AI Beyond Borders: BHASHINI at NCGG Mussoorie
2322621.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Taking Voice-First Multilingual AI Beyond Borders: BHASHINI at NCGG Mussoorie
Shrutlekh and the BHASHINI Mobile App Enable Multilingual Engagement; Shrutlekh to Support Communication Throughout the Programme
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 11:08AM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), facilitated real-time multilingual communication at the National Centre for Good Governance’s (NCGG) Capacity Building Programme on Urban Service Delivery for Civil Servants of Multiple Countries, being held in Mussoorie from 12 to 23 October 2026. Sponsored by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India, the programme is organised by NCGG under the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, as part of India’s international capacity-building efforts through the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme.

The programme brings together civil servants and public-sector representatives from countries including Peru, Cambodia, Nigeria, Kenya, Palestine, Lebanon, The Gambia, Ecuador and Spain, providing a platform for international exchange of experiences and best practices in governance and urban service delivery.

As part of the programme, BHASHINI deployed its Shrutlekh platform to facilitate real-time translation between English and Spanish during the ice-breaking session. The platform supported translation in both directions - English to Spanish and Spanish to English - helping international delegates communicate and participate more effectively despite language barriers.

   

The deployment reflects BHASHINI’s Voice-First Multilingual AI approach, which seeks to make communication and digital services more accessible through speech-based, multilingual technology. By enabling participants to engage across languages, BHASHINI demonstrated how AI-powered language solutions can support inclusive international collaboration and public-sector capacity building.

The BHASHINI team supported participants in using the Shrutlekh platform and introduced them to the BHASHINI ecosystem, its multilingual AI capabilities and potential applications across sectors such as healthcare, finance, agriculture and public service delivery. Participants were also encouraged to explore the BHASHINI mobile application and its features for overcoming language barriers in everyday communication and digital interactions.

Shrutlekh is intended to remain available for use throughout the programme, which concludes on 23 October 2026, subject to operational requirements. The engagement highlights the potential of Voice-First Multilingual AI to strengthen cross-cultural interaction, facilitate knowledge exchange and enable more inclusive participation in international capacity-building initiatives.

Through this initiative, BHASHINI continues to showcase India’s capabilities in AI-powered language technology and its potential to support accessible, multilingual digital experiences across diverse public-sector contexts.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is advancing India’s language AI ecosystem through datasets, AI models, APIs and multilingual applications. As India’s Language Digital Public Infrastructure, BHASHINI supports the integration of language technologies into digital platforms and services.

BHASHINI-enabled language technologies have been integrated across 2,353 government platforms, including over 800 government websites. The platform supports 36 Indian languages in text, 23 Indian languages in voice and 35 international languages. It has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, with over 24 million AI inferences daily, helping make digital services more accessible through language technology.

2322510.title: Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates and Lays Foundation Stones for Development Projects of ₹331 Crore in Mizoram
2322510.ministry: Ministry of Development of North-East Region
2322510.body_html:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region
Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates and Lays Foundation Stones for Development Projects of ₹331 Crore in Mizoram
Union Minister Dedicates Five Projects Worth ₹102 Crore and Lays Foundation Stones for Five Projects of ₹228.54 Crore, Strengthening Connectivity, Power, Water Supply, Healthcare, Education, Sports and Culture
Northeast Is Emerging as an Engine of India's Growth; Development Must Preserve Mizoram's Unique Identity and Natural Heritage
Mizoram Records Over 5 Lakh Tourist Visits in First Half of 2026: Scindia
Union Minister Scindia Announces ₹6,812.30 Crore investment by MDoNER for Northeast in FY 2026–27
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, today inaugurated development projects and laid foundation stones of new initiatives worth ₹331 crore, in Mizoram.Shri Scindia is on  two-day visit of Mizoram.

Upon his arrival in Aizwal, the Union Minister proceeded to Tuivamit and  inaugurated five project worth ₹102 Crore. Union Minister also laid foundation stone of five projects of ₹228.54 crore. Projects cover critical sectors including road connectivity, power transmission, water supply, healthcare, education, sports and cultural infrastructure.

Addressing the gathering in the presence of Mizoram Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma and other dignitaries, Union Minister Scindia said that the development initiatives reflected the Government of India's commitment to transforming connectivity into economic opportunities and improving the quality of life across Mizoram.

Describing Mizoram as a land of majestic mountains and even greater aspirations, the Union Minister said, "Geography may shape the landscape. It must never shape the limits of the  people."

He emphasised that the occasion was not merely about inaugurating infrastructure or laying foundation stones, but about creating opportunities for farmers, entrepreneurs, young people and communities across the state.

Northeast Emerging as an Engine of India's Growth---

Highlighting the growing economic significance of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said that while India is recording economic growth of around 7–7.5%, the Northeast is increasingly emerging as a major contributor to the country's growth trajectory.

He observed that it would not be an exaggeration to describe the North Eastern Region as an engine driving India's development forward.

The Union Minister noted that this was his 35th visit to the North Eastern Region and said that every visit strengthened his commitment to the development of the eight Ashtalakshmi states.

"Every time I come here, I go back recharged and with a renewed commitment towards the Ashtalakshmi states," he said.

Referring to his longstanding association with Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma, Shri Scindia fondly recalled the close relationship between the Chief Minister and his late father. In a lighter moment, he remarked that he represented the second generation of that relationship and appreciated the Chief Minister's youthful energy and enthusiasm.

Shri Scindia also highlighted the region's extraordinary natural beauty and ecological wealth, stressing that development must proceed alongside environmental conservation.

Connectivity Transforming Mizoram's Development Landscape ---

The Union Minister highlighted the significant improvements in Mizoram's connectivity through roads, railways and air transport, observing that the state was becoming increasingly connected not only through infrastructure but also through stronger bonds between people.

He described the 51.38-kilometre Bairabi–Sairang railway line as a historic milestone that brought Mizoram onto India's railway map and transformed access to major economic centers.

The railway connectivity has facilitated the movement of more than 15 lakh passengers through over 1,100 train trips, linking Aizawl with Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The introduction of the Sairang–Silchar service has further strengthened connectivity with the Barak Valley.

Highlighting another landmark achievement, Shri Scindia referred to the arrival of the first Food Corporation of India food-grain rake at Sairang in March 2026, carrying approximately 26,000 quintals of rice from Punjab in 42 wagons.

He said that the direct movement of food grains from Punjab to Mizoram by rail would have been difficult to imagine a decade ago and demonstrated how improved connectivity was bringing distant regions of the country closer together.

Referring to tourism, Shri Scindia noted that Mizoram had recorded 4,94,362 domestic tourist visits and 7,389 foreign tourist visits during the first six months of 2026, reflecting the state's growing appeal as a tourism destination.

Mizoram Ginger Mission to Strengthen Farmers' Livelihoods --

Highlighting the state's agricultural potential, Shri Scindia described Mizo ginger as a unique strength and economic identity of Mizoram.

He said that the ₹189.79 crore Mizoram Ginger Mission would bring nearly 20,000 farming households into an integrated value chain encompassing cultivation, processing, branding, connectivity and access to national and international markets.

The Union Minister emphasised that the objective was not merely to increase ginger production but to ensure that farmers and local communities received a greater share of the economic value generated.

"Mizo ginger is Mizoram's USP; our mission is to make sure the value stays where the ginger grows," he said.

₹331 Crore Development Push Across Key Sectors -

Detailing the Ministry of DoNER's continued investments in the state, Shri Scindia informed the gathering that the Ministry has been allocated ₹6,812.30 crore for the North Eastern Region in the current financial year.

He stated that 375 projects worth ₹4,617.70 crore have been taken up in Mizoram, of which 295 projects, involving an investment of ₹2,692.31 crore, have already been completed.

Congratulating the Government of Mizoram for its cooperation and efforts in implementing development projects, the Union Minister said that the completion of nearly four out of every five projects demonstrated the progress achieved through coordinated efforts between the Centre and the State.

The Union Minister highlighted ten development projects worth approximately ₹331 crore, comprising five projects worth around ₹102 crore dedicated to the people and five projects worth ₹228.54 crore for which foundation stones were laid.

He described these initiatives as investments in both "Routes and Roots" — routes representing the physical infrastructure required to connect people and markets, and roots representing institutions that nurture health, education, culture and talent.

"Routes take Mizoram to the world. Roots keep Mizoram Mizo," he said.

Five Development Projects Worth ₹102 Crore Dedicated to the People

The projects inaugurated and dedicated to the people include:

  1. Daido–Vangkawt Road, Champhai (₹17.24 crore): A 3.33-kilometre road developed under NESIDS-Roads to improve connectivity in the Mizo Ginger pilot region and facilitate the movement of agricultural produce to markets.
  2. 132 kV Bairabi–West Phaileng Transmission Line via Mamit (₹54.95 crore): A 74-circuit-kilometre power transmission line aimed at strengthening the state's electricity transmission network and improving power infrastructure.
  3. Augmentation of North Vanlaiphai Water Supply Scheme (₹20.50 crore): A project designed to improve access to water supply and strengthen essential public infrastructure.
  4. AYUSH Development Centre (₹2.64 crore): An initiative to strengthen institutional capacity and healthcare infrastructure in the AYUSH sector.
  5. Aizawl Institute of Arts & Music for the North Eastern Region, Tuivamit Tlang (₹6.90 crore): Developed under the Schemes of the North Eastern Council, the institute aims to promote artistic talent, preserve cultural traditions and create professional opportunities in music and the arts.

Speaking about the Aizawl Institute of Arts & Music, Shri Scindia praised the exceptional musical talent of Mizoram and expressed his admiration for the musicians who performed during the programme.

He appreciated the energy, enthusiasm and skill displayed by the performers, particularly the drummers, and said that their performances reflected the artistic excellence and vibrant cultural spirit of Mizoram.

Foundation Stones Laid for Five Projects Worth ₹228.54 Crore --

The Union Minister also laid foundation stones for five development projects aimed at expanding connectivity and strengthening social infrastructure across the state.

These include:

  1. Pukzing–Silsuri Road, Mamit (₹100.24 crore): A 21-kilometre road project under NESIDS-Roads aimed at improving all-weather connectivity. Shri Scindia highlighted that Silsuri is among the villages identified for a new bank branch, where inadequate road connectivity has remained a constraint.
  2. Tualpui–Champhai Road (₹57.01 crore): A 21-kilometre road project covering Khawzawl and Champhai districts to strengthen regional connectivity and improve access to markets and essential services.
  3. Oil Palm Link Road (₹26.49 crore): A 32.70-kilometre road project under NESIDS-Roads connecting areas across Kolasib, Mamit, Lunglei and Lawngtlai, expected to benefit nearly 60,000 people across 19 villages by improving agricultural transportation and access to essential services.
  4. 40-Bed Hostel for ANM School, Zemabawk, Aizawl (₹10 crore): A project under NESIDS-OTRI aimed at strengthening nursing education and supporting the training of healthcare professionals.
  5. Sports Infrastructure Development in Mizoram (₹34.80 crore): An initiative to create improved sporting facilities and opportunities for young athletes, building on Mizoram's strong sporting culture and contributions to Indian football and other disciplines.

Development Must Reflect the Spirit of Hnatlang

Concluding his address, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia invoked Mizoram's traditional spirit of Hnatlang, a community practice in which people voluntarily come together to undertake collective work for the welfare of their village and neighbours.

He described the development initiatives as an expression of Hnatlang on a larger scale, bringing together the Central Government, the State Government and the people in a shared mission of progress.

The Union Minister emphasised that the success of development projects should ultimately be measured not by their financial outlay but by their impact on people's lives — whether through better market access for farmers, improved healthcare, greater opportunities for young musicians or enhanced sporting facilities for aspiring athletes.

Reaffirming the Government of India's commitment to the inclusive and sustainable development of Mizoram, Shri Scindia said that the objective was to create new economic opportunities while preserving the state's unique cultural identity and natural heritage.

The Union Minister's two-day visit to Mizoram on October 12–13, 2026, also includes engagements with students, civil society representatives and stakeholders from the banking sector, reflecting the Ministry of DoNER's continued focus on infrastructure development, youth empowerment and economic inclusion across the North Eastern Region.

2322497.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of MSME Concludes ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ Campaign with Nationwide Cleanliness and Awareness Initiatives
Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi Leads Cleanliness Drive as Ministry of MSME Promotes Jan Bhagidari and Environmental Sustainability under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 8:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) observed Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 from 17th September to 2nd October 2026, culminating in Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026. Guided by the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, the campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and Jan Bhagidari across the Ministry, its attached offices and autonomous bodies.

As part of the campaign, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME; Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME; and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME), participated in a cleanliness drive at MSME-DFO, Bal Sahyog, Connaught Place, under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative on 1st  October 2026. More than 150 participants participated in the cleanliness drive, underscoring the importance of collective action in maintaining clean public spaces. Tree plantation activities were also undertaken under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, reinforcing the Ministry’s commitment to environmental conservation and sustainable development.

.  

The campaign commenced with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME). Approximately 250 officials of the Ministry of MSME and its field offices participated in the pledge and reaffirmed their commitment to cleanliness and the vision of Swachh Bharat.

 

As part of awareness and sensitisation activities, the Ministry sensitised officers and representatives of its attached offices, autonomous bodies and field formations on the objectives and significance of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026. The campaign encouraged participating organisations to undertake meaningful cleanliness drives, awareness programmes and sustainable initiatives in their offices and surrounding areas.

  

During the campaign period, the Ministry and its field formations across the country undertook activities under key components including CTU (Cleanliness Target Unit) Transformation & Clean Public Places, Swachh Paathshala, SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir, Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata, and Swachhata se Samriddhi. These initiatives helped strengthen public participation, promote awareness on cleanliness and reinforce the importance of sustainable and collective efforts towards a Swachh Bharat.

2322494.title: INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INDIGENOUS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT INS MANGROL
2322494.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INDIGENOUS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT INS MANGROL
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy commissioned INS Mangrol (P82), the third Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), at the Naval Dockyard, Mumbai, on 12 Oct 2026.  The commissioning ceremony was presided over by VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command.

The commissioning ceremony was attended by senior officers of the Defence Forces, representatives of the Ministry of Defence, Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), industry partners and other distinguished dignitaries.

Indigenously designed and constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi, INS Mangrol represents India's growing capabilities in warship design, construction and systems integration. With over 80 percent indigenous content, the ship reflects the nation's commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, while highlighting the contribution of Indian defence industries and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) towards strengthening indigenous naval capabilities.

Designed for operations in coastal and shallow waters, INS Mangrol is equipped to undertake Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), underwater surveillance and Low-Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), along with mine warfare-related tasks. Its advanced sensors, sonar and weapon systems enhance its capability to detect, track and counter underwater threats in the challenging littoral environment. Powered by three diesel engine-driven waterjet propulsion units, the ship offers high manoeuvrability and rapid response, essential for operations in shallow and confined waters.

VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, in his address, congratulated the Indian Navy and CSL on the commissioning of INS Mangrol. He highlighted the importance of indigenous warships in strengthening India's maritime surveillance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in the evolving maritime security environment. He also emphasised the growing capabilities of India's indigenous shipbuilding industry and the Indian Navy's continued commitment to technological advancement, operational preparedness and self-reliance in defence manufacturing.

INS Mangrol derives its name from the coastal town and prominent fishing harbour of Mangrol in Junagadh district of Gujarat. The ship also carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until April 2004, continuing the naval tradition of preserving the names of distinguished warships.

The commissioning of INS Mangrol marks another significant milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities and coastal defence preparedness. The ship will contribute to safeguarding India's coastal approaches and maritime interests, enhancing maritime domain awareness and countering underwater threats. Its induction further reinforces the Indian Navy's commitment to maritime security, regional stability and self-reliance in warship construction, in furtherance of India's maritime interests in the Indian Ocean Region.

2322461.title: 9 Days SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 Underway In Mysuru Since October 11
2322461.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
9 Days SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 Underway In Mysuru Since October 11
MELA Showcases Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products of Artisans from 12 States
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 is underway at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds at Mysuru in Karnataka, being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, since October 11.

The 9 Days Mela upto October 19, aims to provide a marketing platform for products made by beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis, including artisans supported by the three National Corporations functioning under the Ministry, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

A senior official in the Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the target groups.

He said the Ministry has been organising SHILP SAMAGAM MELAS since 2022, and 975 artisans have been benefited through 13 such fairs organised so far.

The Mysuru edition is the first SHILP SAMAGAM MELA of the financial year 2026–27.

The official said a total of 83 stalls have been put up at the Mela, out of which 80 have been allotted to artisans, including 37 women artisans. Food stalls serving traditional delicacies have also been set up for visitors.

The Mela features artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, he added.

The Official informed that the exhibition showcases a wide range of traditional products, including handicraft items, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed products, Kanjivaram sarees, leather goods, wooden toys, bags and purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. The platform enables artisans to display their products to a wider audience and connect with prospective customers, while promoting India's diverse cultural heritage and traditional skills.

The official further said that SHILP SAMAGAM MELA also serves as a platform to disseminate information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and its three national corporations—NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC. The initiative seeks to enhance awareness about available assistance and development opportunities for eligible beneficiaries, while encouraging entrepreneurship and economic empowerment.

The Ministry has also introduced BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) to expand market access for products made by the target groups through various digital platforms in India and abroad. Under this initiative, products are branded as BHARAT TULIP to enhance their visibility and facilitate online sales. The programme aims to strengthen artisans' livelihoods while preserving traditional art forms and promoting India's rich craftsmanship to a wider audience.

The Official said the Ministry facilitates the participation of artisans by providing free stalls and support covering travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods, and meals, including lunch and dinner. This assistance helps artisans participate in the mela and showcase their products without bearing stall rental costs and specified participation-related expenses.

It is pertinent to mention that during the Financial Year 2026–27, the Ministry proposes to organise additional SHILP SAMAGAM FAIRS At Guwahati, Dilli Haat In New Delhi, Jodhpur And Lucknow.

The Ministry and its three National Corporations will also participate in major exhibitions, including the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in Faridabad in February 2027.

Through initiatives such as SHILP SAMAGAM MELA and BHARAT TULIP, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote market access, entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities for artisans from the target groups, while supporting the preservation and wider recognition of India's traditional arts and crafts.

2322460.title: CAQM reviews Zone-wise Preparedness of all 12 MCD Zones for Road Dust Mitigation and Deep Cleaning of Roads in Delhi
2322460.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2322460.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM reviews Zone-wise Preparedness of all 12 MCD Zones for Road Dust Mitigation and Deep Cleaning of Roads in Delhi
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

As part of its continued efforts to strengthen dust mitigation measures and improve road cleanliness for effective air pollution control in Delhi, the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, today held a hearing to review the actions taken and preparedness of all 12 zones of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The review focused on the removal of accumulated and legacy dust, garbage and Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste from roads, roadsides, medians, footpaths and other open areas.

 

The Hearing was held pursuant to the Commission’s notice dated 7th October 2026, issued following an inspection conducted on 3rd October 2026, during which instances of high visible road dust and accumulation of C&D waste were observed on road stretches maintained by the Public Works Department (PWD) and cleaned by MCD, indicating the need for further strengthening of dust mitigation and cleaning measures on the ground. The Commissioner, MCD and concerned Deputy Commissioners (DCs) of the 12 zones of MCD were called upon to explain the actions taken and preparedness for addressing the identified gaps. During the hearing, the Deputy Commissioners, MCD made zone-wise presentations detailing the cleaning and sweeping operations undertaken, dust mitigation measures implemented, enforcement actions taken and preparedness for further improving road cleanliness and abating road dust emissions.

 

The presentations highlighted sustained efforts towards mechanized road sweeping, water sprinkling, road washing and intensive deep cleaning of major roads and identified air pollution hotspots. Measures for the removal and scientific disposal of accumulated legacy dust, silt, malba, garbage and C&D waste were also presented, along with cleaning of footpaths, road edges, medians, kerb stones and other areas prone to dust accumulation. The deployment of mechanical road sweeping machines (MRSMs), water sprinklers, water tankers, anti-smog guns, jetting machines and dedicated sanitation teams form part of the ongoing dust suppression and cleaning operations by the 12 zones of MCD in Delhi.

The zones also presented measures for repairing potholes and damaged road stretches, paving unpaved areas, greening dust-prone patches and improving sanitation at vulnerable locations. Preparedness for the winter season includes special deep-cleaning drives, hotspot-specific interventions, improved management of designated C&D waste collection points, regular field inspections and enforcement against open burning, improper waste disposal and other polluting activities. The need for coordinated action(s) with PWD, DDA, DJB, Railways and other concerned agencies to address dust-generating activities and resolve pending infrastructure-related issues was also highlighted.

The review covered the Outer North Zone (Narela), City SP Zone (Old Delhi), Civil Line Zone (North), Rohini Zone (North West), Central North Zone (Keshavpuram), Central Zone (Karol Bagh), South Zone, Central Zone (South East), Najafgarh Zone (South West), West Zone, Shahdara South Zone (East) and Shahdara North Zone (North East).

The Commission emphasized the need for effective implementation of the measures presented to ensure improved road cleanliness and sustained reduction in road dust emissions. Further, continued gaps in the implementation of prescribed dust mitigation measures would be viewed seriously and that appropriate action(s) including prosecution, may be initiated against the responsible agencies or officials for non-compliance.

The Deputy Commissioners, MCD were directed to ensure effective utilization of deployed machinery and sanitation manpower thus augmenting the machinery as per the quantum of work to be done and actual requirement. Further, regular cleaning of identified road stretches, prompt removal and scientific disposal of accumulated dust and C&D waste and priority attention to damaged roads and other dust-generating locations, should be focused. Close field-level supervision, regular monitoring of progress and accountability for gaps in implementation were also reviewed.

The Commission noted the actions taken by MCD and reiterated that the removal of accumulated dust and garbage from roads and open areas must be ensured within the stipulated timeline of 31st October 2026. All concerned zones and agencies were directed to ensure strict compliance with the Commission’s Statutory Directions and strengthen dust mitigation measures for effective control and mitigation of road dust pollution and improvement of air quality in Delhi-NCR.

2322456.title: Secretary (Power) holds Bilateral Meeting with the European Commission's Director General for Taxation and Customs Union- Mr. Gerassimos Thomas
2322456.body_html:
Ministry of Power
Secretary (Power) holds Bilateral Meeting with the European Commission's Director General for Taxation and Customs Union- Mr. Gerassimos Thomas
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, held a bilateral meeting with Mr. Gerassimos Thomas, Director-General for Taxation and Customs Union, European Commission, today in New Delhi. Discussions focused on India's carbon market development, the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and opportunities for enhanced technical cooperation.

Secretary (Power) highlighted India's progress under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), including the notification of emission intensity reduction targets for 490 industrial units and the development of the domestic carbon market. He also highlighted India's progress in increasing the share of non-fossil sources in its electricity generation capacity, noting that non-fossil sources account for 308 GW of the country's total installed capacity of 558 GW.

The EU side appreciated India's progress in developing its carbon market and shared developments relating to CBAM implementation. Both sides expressed willingness to continue technical engagement on recognition of carbon pricing mechanisms, monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) systems, and capacity building.

Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation and facilitate continued dialogue on carbon markets, CBAM-related methodologies and other areas of mutual interest.

2322458.title: Ministry of Rural Development Brings National SARAS Mela 2026 to Vijayawada for the First Time outside Delhi-NCR, in Collaboration with Andhra Pradesh Government
2322458.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Rural Development Brings National SARAS Mela 2026 to Vijayawada for the First Time outside Delhi-NCR, in Collaboration with Andhra Pradesh Government
National SARAS Mela 2026 to Bring 1,500+ Women Entrepreneurs from 30+ States and UTs to Vijayawada
Hon’ble President of India H.E. Smt. Droupadi Murmu to Inaugurate National SARAS Mela 2026 in Vijayawada on 15 October
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

Vijayawada, 12 October 2026: Vijayawada is set to become a vibrant showcase of India’s rural enterprise and women-led entrepreneurship as the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, in collaboration with the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP), Andhra Pradesh, brings the first National SARAS Mela 2026 to the city.

Scheduled from 13 to 31 October 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, the Mela will bring together 1500+ women from Self-Help Groups across 30+ States and Union Territories, creating a platform where rural enterprises, traditional crafts, regional cuisines and entrepreneurial stories come together. The event will be inaugurated by the Hon’ble President of India, H.E Smt. Droupadi Murmu.


विजयवाड़ा, बस 1 दिन का इंतजार और! 🛍️✨ हस्तशिल्प व हथकरघा उत्पादों, स्वादिष्ट व्यंजनों और सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमों का महासंगम सरस आजीविका मेला होने वाला है शुरू आइए #Swadeshi और आत्मनिर्भरता के इस उत्सव का मिलकर मनाएं जश्न #MoRD #DAYNRLM #SarasMeinHum #SarasAajeevikaMela #SarasAajeevikaMela2026 #SarasVijayawada #WomenEmpowerment #LakhpatiDidi

— Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India (@MoRD_GoI) October 12, 2026

The inauguration ceremony will be attended by Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Hon’ble Governor of Andhra Pradesh, and Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Hon’ble Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, and Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan, Hon’ble Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Union Minister of Civil Aviation, joins them, along with Union Ministers of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani (Rural Development and Communications), Shri Kamlesh Paswan (Rural Development) and Shri Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma (Heavy Industries and Steel). The Government of Andhra Pradesh is further represented by Shri Kondapalli Srinivas, Minister of MSME, SERP, NRI Empowerment and Relations, and Shri Satya Kumar Yadav, Minister of Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education, with Shri Kesineni Sivanadh, Member of Parliament, including Shri Rohit Kansal, IAS, Secretary, Department of Rural Development. Their presence underlines the importance of strengthening rural livelihoods, promoting women-led entrepreneurship and creating sustainable market opportunities for Self-Help Group (SHG) women.

Aligned with the Government of India’s Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) and the Prime Minister’s vision of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis by 2029, the Mela, along with SARAS Aajeevika Gallery and the eSARAS digital platform, provides women entrepreneurs with opportunities to showcase their traditional crafts, access wider markets and connect with consumers across India and beyond. These initiatives help women from rural areas to transform their skills into sustainable enterprises, strengthen their incomes and achieve financial independence.

The National SARAS Mela begins on 13th October with a formal inauguration on 15th October at 11:30 AM and takes place alongside the Dasara Sharannavaratri Utsavams and Vijayawada Utsav 2.0.

Visitors can look forward to regional artistry including Phulkari from Punjab, Pashmina from Jammu & Kashmir, Ikat and Telia textiles from Telangana, and Paunchei from Mizoram, alongside intricate handicrafts such as Meenakari, Dokra, brasswork, woodcraft, traditional paintings, alongside regional delicacies and home-style cuisines from across the country. The Mela works as a marketplace where women from Self-Help groups sell directly to customers, build buyer connections and take their products to wider markets, including through the eSARAS platform.

A significant focus of the Mela will be the Lakhpati Didi Pavilion, which will bring alive the journey of women moving from skills and collective participation towards enterprise, market access, sustainable income supported by institutions  to enable socio-economic empowerment. The pavilion will also allow visitors to hear directly from the women behind these journeys.

The collaboration also extends beyond showcasing products. Through the Knowledge Pavilion, participating women will interact with corporates, industry experts and organisations in areas including branding, marketing, packaging, business development and market expansion. The Convergence Pavilion will further connect women with relevant government departments, ministries and institutions supporting the growth of their enterprises.

Visitors can experience live craft demonstrations at the Demo Pavilion, watching handlooms being woven and handicrafts taking shape before their eyes, discover regional cuisines and enjoy cultural programmes celebrating the strength and entrepreneurial spirit of rural India.  Standing tall at National SARAS Mela 2026, will be a 16-foot signature installation, called “SHAKTI - The Spirit of Lakhpati Didi” symbolising the collective power of millions of women who are preserving India's rich craftsmanship while transforming their skills into livelihoods, independence and prosperity. This first National SARAS Mela is supported by various government partners including NABARD and NIRDPR. The food court will bring together delicacies across the country through 50 food stalls.

At its heart, the National SARAS Mela is about the women behind every product, craft and enterprise, and the journey from skill to enterprise, enterprise to market, and market to sustainable livelihood.

*****

2322448.title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Launches Commercialisation Catalogue of Technologies Developed under Various Sponsored Programmes
2322448.body_html:
Ministry of Mines
Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Launches Commercialisation Catalogue of Technologies Developed under Various Sponsored Programmes
Connecting Research with Industry – From Technology Development to Commercialisation
Posted On: 12 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy today launched the Commercialisation Catalogue of Technologies developed under the Science & Technology (S&T) Programme of the Ministry of Mines, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Department of Science and Technology (DST), and industry-sponsored programmes. This is an important step towards bridging the gap between research and industries showcasing indigenous technologies and facilitating their transfer, adoption, and commercialisation by industry.

The initiative aims to systematically document, showcase and promote technologies developed through publicly funded research and industry-supported projects, facilitating their adoption by industries, technology transfer, licensing and commercialisation. The Catalogue will serve as a common platform connecting technology developers, research institutions, laboratories, start-ups, MSMEs and industries, enabling promising indigenous technologies to progress from research and development to industrial application

A significant number of R&D projects have resulted in valuable technological outcomes, including innovative processes, prototypes, pilot-scale technologies, patents and other commercially relevant solutions. However, these outcomes are often dispersed across individual project reports and institutions. The proposed Catalogue seeks to address this gap by bringing verified technical information on such technologies together in a single, accessible repository for industries and prospective technology adopters.

To facilitate participation in this initiative, the Ministry is seeking standardised and verified technical inputs from Principal Investigators (PIs), Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs), implementing institutions and technology developers through the SATYABHAMA Portal (https://research.mines.gov.in/). The information submitted will support the assessment of technology outcomes, validation of technical details, preparation of technology profiles and identification of technologies with potential for commercialisation.

The Commercialisation Catalogue represents a significant step towards building a technology-driven and industry-oriented innovation ecosystem in India, ensuring that promising research outcomes translate into practical industrial solutions, economic value and wider technological impact.
