2321828.title: Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) with the theme ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’ concludes successfully in New Delhi
2321828.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) with the theme ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’ concludes successfully in New Delhi
Three-day Conclave brings together policymakers, economists, academics, business leaders and international thought leaders to deliberate on resilience, global fragmentation, technology, trade and India’s economic priorities
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 9:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Economic Growth (IEG), in partnership with the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, successfully concluded the Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026), held from 3–5 October 2026 in New Delhi under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux.” The three-day Conclave brought together more than 200 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries, for high-level discussions on contemporary economic and policy challenges.

The Conclave was inaugurated on 3rd October 2026 by the Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, who delivered the inaugural address. In his address, the Vice-President emphasised that economic resilience cannot be separated from social resilience, highlighting inclusion as a foundation of resilience in a rapidly changing world. He also underlined the importance of policymaking that remains grounded in ground realities and responsive to changing circumstances.

Over three days, the Conclave featured plenary sessions, interactive discussions and focused roundtables examining the challenges and opportunities arising from global economic and geopolitical shifts. Discussions centred on building resilience while sustaining growth, openness and institutional credibility amid recurrent global shocks and uncertainty.

A key highlight of KEC 2026 was the Special Plenary on “Resilience in an Age of Flux: India’s Economic Priorities,” addressed by Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, with Ms. Amélie de Montchalin, President of the Cour des Comptes, France, as discussant. The session examined how India can sustain growth, preserve macroeconomic stability and expand investment amid global fragmentation, technological disruption and recurrent shocks, while strengthening the foundations of long-term economic resilience.

The Conclave also brought together significant perspectives on central banking, financial stability and macroeconomic resilience. Discussions examined how monetary authorities can navigate inflation, financial fragility, capital flows and institutional credibility in an environment characterised by recurrent global shocks.

Technology and the digital economy formed another important strand of KEC 2026. Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Minister for Development of North Eastern Region, delivered the keynote address on “Connected India, Empowered Finance: Building Trusted Digital Infrastructure for the AI Economy.” The session examined how digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and new communication networks can contribute to productivity and economic transformation while maintaining trust and competition.

The Conclave also explored the intersection of culture, heritage and economic development. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, delivered the keynote address on “Culture as Capital: From Heritage to Horizons,” examining the role of cultural capital and heritage in the broader architecture of economic development.

The global dimension of the Conclave was further strengthened through discussions on India's evolving position in a changing international order. The special concluding session, “India and the World: Adaptive by Design,” was moderated by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Board of Trustees, IEG. Dr. S. Jaishankar, Union Minister for External Affairs, delivered the special concluding address, with Mr. George Yeo, former Foreign Minister of Singapore, as discussant. The session examined India's strategic autonomy, partnerships and ability to respond flexibly to an increasingly contested and uncertain global environment.

The Conclave's deliberations extended across a broad range of contemporary economic issues, including global fragmentation, trade and supply chains, fiscal and structural reforms, financial markets, development finance, investment, technology and artificial intelligence, employment and skills, demographic change, food systems, sustainability and climate finance. These discussions brought together perspectives from India and across the world, reflecting the Conclave's objective of connecting economic scholarship with policy and global experience.

The Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave also featured the participation of senior policymakers and leading economic thinkers, including Dr. P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister; Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India; Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India; Smt. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser; Lord Nicholas Stern; Professor Michael Greenstone; Jean-Claude Trichet, former President of the European Central Bank; and other eminent Indian and international economists, policymakers and business leaders.

Since its inception in 2022, the Kautilya Economic Conclave has grown into a significant platform for dialogue on contemporary economic and policy challenges. Jointly convened by the Institute of Economic Growth and the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, the Conclave serves as a bridge between scholarship, policymaking and global perspectives. The earlier editions were held under the themes “Redefining the Future” (2022), “Navigating a World on Fire” (2023), “The Indian Era” (2024) and “Seeking Prosperity in Turbulent Times” (2025).  Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra, Chairman, Board of Governors, IEG, and Professor Sabyasachi Kar, Director, IEG, played key roles in guiding and organising the Conclave.

The Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave reaffirmed the importance of sustained dialogue and evidence-based policymaking in navigating an increasingly complex global environment. Under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux,” the Conclave highlighted the need for India and the wider global community to build institutions, policies and partnerships capable of responding to uncertainty while sustaining inclusive growth, investment, innovation and long-term development.

2321818.title: PSA Prof. Sood Chairs Fourth All S&T Clusters’ Meet in Chandigarh, Calls for Stronger Collaboration and Technology Deployment
2321818.ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
2321818.body_html:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
PSA Prof. Sood Chairs Fourth All S&T Clusters’ Meet in Chandigarh, Calls for Stronger Collaboration and Technology Deployment
संहतिः कार्यसाधिका - Fourth All S&T Clusters’ Meet Reaffirms the Power of Collaboration in Driving Innovation
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 8:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, chaired the Fourth All S&T Clusters’ Meet held on 9–10 October 2026 at Panjab University, Chandigarh, hosted by PU-IIT Ropar Regional Accelerator for Holistic Innovations Foundation (PI-RAHI). He was joined  by Dr (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary and Dr Vishal Choudhary, Scientist-F, Office of the PSA. Prof. Meenakshi Goyal, Vice-Chancellor, Panjab University; Prof. Rajeev Ahuja, Director, IIT Ropar; Prof. Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Director, IIT Jodhpur; Prof. Rajat Sandhir, and Dr Pushpendra P. Singh, Director, PI-RAHI; and representatives of the eight S&T Clusters participated in the deliberations.

In his opening remarks, Prof. Sood noted that the Clusters have evolved into integrated ecosystems addressing regional, industrial, and societal challenges and increasingly functioning as “National Technology Accelerators.” He emphasised the need to strengthen inter-Cluster collaboration, stakeholder participation, coordination with RuTAG and RSVCs, and technology visibility. He also highlighted the growing global engagement of the Clusters, including the 12 international MoUs emerging from the First International Conference on S&T Clusters and subsequent partnerships with the University of Western Australia, India–Australia Smart Farm Network and UK Catapult Network.

During the inaugural session, Prof. Sood launched an Automatic Weather Station, highlighting the role of technology-enabled solutions in strengthening climate-smart and data-driven agriculture. The Meet also highlighted key inter-Cluster initiatives in sustainable mobility and clean technologies, including the inauguration of an EV Charging Station in Himachal Pradesh and the EVChargex Battery Swapping Station in Panchkula. The Himachal Pradesh initiative brings together charging infrastructure, EV users, and digital services, leveraging collaboration between DRIIV and PI-RAHI to support the State’s transition to electric mobility. The Panchkula facility demonstrates the transition of indigenous battery-swapping technology from pilot to commercial deployment, integrating EVs, batteries, rider onboarding, and digital management on a common platform. Prof. Sood also launched the report on Phycotree – Microalgal Photobioreactor, highlighting DRIIV’s efforts to facilitate the transition of indigenous technology from identification to field validation and potential deployment, including its engagement with GMR for applications at New Delhi IGI Airport; Kalaanubhav portal for PI-RAHI, featuring traditional crafts and products of artisans from Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir, along with an exhibition showcasing the work of artisans from Northern India; SPARKS 2.0; IGNITE 2.0; GINI 2.0; the STI Ecosystem of Northern India Reports; and an MoU signing ceremony. The Meet further marked the announcement of the UK Catapults–S&T Clusters collaboration in Healthcare, Emerging Technologies, and Net Zero Technologies, strengthening opportunities for technology development and international collaboration.

Scientific Secretary Dr Maini emphasised the need to build a connected National Cluster Network through sharing of technologies, infrastructure, expertise and industry partnerships. She highlighted inter-Cluster replication through D-PoC, Kalaanubhav and i-Passport, and called for stronger industry participation from R&D to validation, commercialisation, and scale. She urged the Clusters to focus on replication, collaboration and scale, translating successful regional solutions into larger national and global programmes.

 

A dedicated Stakeholders Meet on Strengthening S&T Clusters was also organised in Chandigarh, bringing together industry partners, CSR partners, academic institutions, and government representatives for interaction with the leadership of the S&T Clusters. The interaction provided an opportunity to discuss greater stakeholder participation and strengthen partnerships for technology development, validation, and deployment.

On the second day, Prof. Sood inaugurated a Digital Podiatric Clinic at the Panjab University Health Centre, Chandigarh, established by PI-RAHI under a CSR partnership from HL Klemove. The clinic is described as Northern India’s first Digital Podiatric Clinic and deploys AI-powered foot-screening technology for early detection and preventive care of diabetic foot conditions, bringing advanced medical technology closer to community healthcare. The delegates also visited the facility following its inauguration.

 

Prof. Sood also announced the 2nd International Conference on S&T Clusters, marking the next phase of the international outreach of the Cluster initiative. The announcement was followed by further deliberations on the present and future plans of the Clusters and discussions led by the Chair.

The two-day Meet provided a platform to review the progress of the eight S&T Clusters, assess their ongoing initiatives and discuss their present and future plans, with emphasis on technology translation, inter-cluster collaboration, industry engagement and strengthening regional innovation ecosystems. Cluster presentations and follow-up discussions were held across the two days covering the Pune Knowledge Cluster Foundation (PKCF), Jodhpur City Knowledge and Innovation Foundation (JCKIF), Bhubaneswar City Knowledge and Innovation Cluster (BCKIC), Delhi Research Implementation and Innovation (DRIIV), AMTZ-Vizag Cluster, Bengaluru Science and Technology Cluster (BeST), Research and Innovation Circle of Hyderabad (RICH), and PI-RAHI.

The Fourth All S&T Clusters’ Meet reaffirmed the importance of strengthening collaboration among the eight Clusters and building stronger linkages with industry, academia, government, and other stakeholders. The deliberations focused on taking forward Cluster-led initiatives, promoting technology deployment and creating greater opportunities for replication and scale-up of solutions across regions.

Conceived in 2020 following recommendations of the Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC), the Science and Technology (S&T) Clusters program of OPSA brings together academia, research institutions, industry, startups, government, and other stakeholders to address regional challenges through science, technology, and innovation. Over the years, the Clusters have evolved as regional innovation ecosystems focused on translating research and technology into solutions with societal and economic impact.

2321808.title: Youth Must Become Ambassadors of Viksit Bharat and Place Nation-Building at the Centre of Every Action: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
2321808.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2321808.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Youth Must Become Ambassadors of Viksit Bharat and Place Nation-Building at the Centre of Every Action: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
MY Bharat Youth Convention in Varanasi brings together youth achievers from sports, academics and digital media to inspire leadership and nation-building
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), organised the Youth for Viksit Bharat: MY Bharat Youth Convention at Swatantrata Bhavan, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, on October 10, 2026. The Convention brought together youth achievers, sportspersons, digital content creators and young leaders to celebrate youth excellence and encourage greater participation in nation-building.

The programme was attended by Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Shri Girish Chandra Yadav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Youth Welfare and Sports, Government of Uttar Pradesh, and Shri Sunil Paliwal, Secretary, Department of Youth Affairs, Government of India. Indian cricketer Shri Dhruv Jurel and Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi also interacted with participants.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya called upon young people to see themselves not merely as beneficiaries of India's development journey but as active partners and ambassadors of Viksit Bharat. Referring to the Prime Minister's vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, he emphasised that today's youth would be the generation that lives in and leads India in 2047. “Viksit Bharat must be shaped by the youth, for the youth and through the youth,” he said, urging young citizens to look beyond individual aspirations and contribute meaningfully to their communities and the nation.

Highlighting the importance of India's cultural values, the Minister underscored the role of discipline, service, responsibility and respect in nation-building. He observed that meaningful transformation does not always require large interventions, as small and sustained efforts can produce significant results when undertaken with purpose. He encouraged young people to make themselves socially relevant by addressing community needs and translating their aspirations into constructive action.

Dr. Mandaviya highlighted the opportunities available to young citizens through MY Bharat for volunteering, leadership, community service and experiential engagement. He emphasised that India's demographic strength can become a major developmental advantage when young people are connected with a larger national purpose. “Viksit Bharat is not only a destination for India's youth; it is a national mission that has to be realised through the energy, ideas, discipline and participation of young Indians,” he said, urging youth to consider both the future they wish to build and the legacy they will leave for generations to come.

The Minister also highlighted the importance of youth participation in the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan, noting that substance abuse poses a challenge to young people's potential, family well-being and national progress. He called upon young citizens to promote awareness, encourage positive choices and mobilise communities towards a drug-free society. He further urged them to use their creativity and digital influence responsibly in support of positive social change.

A key highlight of the Convention was the felicitation of achievers across diverse fields. Asian Games medallists Rohit Yadav, Prachi Choudhary, Parul Choudhary, Jay Kumar and Raj Kumar Pal were recognised for their sporting achievements. Arpit Giri, Aditya Upadhyay and Avantika, who cleared JEE and secured admission to IIT (BHU), were also felicitated for their academic accomplishments.

The Convention also honoured content creators Prajwal Prajapati, Abhishek Chaurasiya, Amit Kumar Gautam, Harsh Gupta, Shivam Pandey, Suryanshu Shukla, Saurabh Chandra, Bhim Yadav, Shivaditya, Dishu Khanna and Aditya Maurya, recognising the role of digital platforms in youth engagement, creative expression and positive social impact.

Indian cricketer Shri Dhruv Jurel shared his experiences with participants, highlighting the importance of discipline, commitment and perseverance in pursuing excellence in sports. Shri Vishal Chaturvedi, Director of Hanuman Ansh, also interacted with the participants, sharing insights on creative expression and the role of music and cultural storytelling in engaging young audiences. The programme featured a musical performance by Shri Sadhu Tiwari, associated with Hanuman Ansh, along with folk music, a nukkad natak and a folk dance presented by MY Bharat volunteers. These performances celebrated India's rich cultural heritage and highlighted the role of art and culture in youth engagement.

The Convention highlighted MY Bharat's role in connecting young citizens with opportunities for volunteering, leadership, experiential learning and community participation. By bringing together achievers and aspiring young people, it sought to amplify inspiring success stories, promote peer learning and encourage wider participation in youth-led initiatives.

The MY Bharat Youth Convention reaffirmed the importance of recognising young achievers, nurturing talent and enabling youth to contribute meaningfully to India's development journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

*****

2321793.title: Telangana Delegation Explores Assam’s Rich Cultural Heritage and Traditions Under Yuva Sangam Phase VII
2321793.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Telangana Delegation Explores Assam’s Rich Cultural Heritage and Traditions Under Yuva Sangam Phase VII
Delegates Interact with Governor of Assam Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, has organised Yuva Sangam Phase VII programme under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat initiative to strengthen cultural and emotional bonds among the youth of India.

The programme enables young participants to explore the cultural heritage, traditions, educational landscape and developmental achievements of different States and Union Territories, fostering mutual understanding and national integration through 20 paired States and higher education institutions.

The Telangana delegation, led by Central University of Karnataka, received a warm welcome from Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati upon its arrival in Guwahati on 4 October 2026.

The Telangana delegation began its day in Assam on 5 October 2026 with a refreshing yoga session. The session offered the young delegates with an opportunity to begin their day with wellness, mindfulness and positive energy while experiencing an important aspect of India’s traditional knowledge and cultural heritage.

The delegation interacted with the Governor of Assam, Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya, on 5 October 2026. The interaction offered the young delegates an opportunity to gain insights into Assam’s rich heritage, traditions and cultural significance. The interaction further enriched their understanding of India’s diverse cultural landscape and the importance of strengthening connections among young people across the country.

The Telangana-Assam exchange under Yuva Sangam Phase VII reflects the programme’s core objective of encouraging young Indians to explore the diversity of the country, engage with communities beyond their home States and develop a deeper appreciation of India’s shared cultural heritage. Such exchanges provide young people with meaningful opportunities to explore, connect and create lasting memories, while contributing to the larger vision of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat and strengthening the bonds of unity in diversity.

2321795.title: LAUNCH OF NEXT GENERATION OFFSHORE PATROL VESSEL (YARD 3040, SHREYAS) AT M/s GRSE, KOLKATA
2321795.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
LAUNCH OF NEXT GENERATION OFFSHORE PATROL VESSEL (YARD 3040, SHREYAS) AT M/s GRSE, KOLKATA
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

Yard 3040 (Shreyas), Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (NGOPV), was launched at M/s GRSE, Kolkata, on 10 Oct 2026 by Mrs Reyman Kochhar, in the presence of VAdm Ajay Kochhar, Vice Chief of the Naval Staff. The event reflected the rich traditions and ethos of the Indian Navy. Senior dignitaries from the Indian Navy, Ministry of Defence, GRSE and Industry Partners attended the occasion.

The construction of NGOPVs is concurrently being undertaken at two shipyards (GSL, Goa & GRSE, Kolkata). These indigenously designed and built ships will augment the existing OPVs/ NOPVs for multi-domain operations, such as maritime surveillance, search & rescue, protection of offshore assets, HADR and anti-piracy missions. These ships derive their names from India’s rich heritage, with this ship being named as ‘Shreyas’, meaning ‘Best’ or ‘Most Excellent’ in Sanskrit.

The launch marks yet another significant milestone in Indian Navy’s pursuit towards indigenous shipbuilding and is in consonance with Government of India’s vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Make in India’ initiatives.

2321791.title: NBA Disburses Rs 2.02 Crore of ABS Funds from Seed Sector to Support Biodiversity Conservation and Community Well-Being at Grassroots Level
2321791.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2321791.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA Disburses Rs 2.02 Crore of ABS Funds from Seed Sector to Support Biodiversity Conservation and Community Well-Being at Grassroots Level
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority has disbursed Rs 2.02 crore among 27 States and 3 Union Territories, representing their respective shares of Access and Benefit-Sharing contributions received from seed-sector companies for the utilisation of biological resources, to support biodiversity conservation, sustainable use of biological resources and strengthening the livelihood of local communities.

The ABS contributions from the utilisation of agricultural biological resources, including rice, eggplant, cauliflower, cucumber, hot pepper, bottle gourd, bitter gourd, tomato and okra, cover multiple varieties and hybrids. The contributions were received from East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd., Syngenta India Ltd., Devgen Seeds and Crop Technology Pvt. Ltd., Limagrain India Pvt. Ltd., Bayer Science & Innovation Pvt. Ltd., Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. and Enza Zaden India Pvt. Ltd.

Where biological resources procured through markets or traders, and individual benefit claimers could not be identified, the NBA applied the distribution modalities recommended by an expert committee and approved by the Authority. Accordingly, the beneficiary share was apportioned among the concerned State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) based on the cultivation area of the respective biological resources, as reflected in the agricultural statistics published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Of the total ABS amount of Rs 2.02 crore disbursed to 27 SBBs and 3 UTBCs, the top 10 States accounted for Rs 1.43 crore of the total ABS amount.

With this release, the cumulative ABS disbursement by the NBA has reached Rs 202.00 crore, demonstrating India’s commitment to equitable benefit-sharing arising from the utilisation of biological resources and the reinvestment of such benefits in conservation and community welfare.

The ABS mechanism provides an important avenue for mobilising financial resources and channelling them towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and local development. Disbursements to State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support initiatives, including strengthening Biodiversity Management Committees, updating People’s Biodiversity Registers, conserving traditional crop varieties and medicinal plants, restoring habitats, and promoting the sustainable management of biological resources at grassroot level. These measures can further strengthen institutional capacities and enhance the participation of farmers, local communities and other stakeholders in biodiversity governance.

ABS-funded activities can complement relevant Government schemes and programmes, particularly those promoting tribal welfare, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource-based enterprises, such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana. Such convergence can strengthen community-led conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood opportunities, while leveraging existing institutional mechanisms

India’s Access and Benefit-Sharing framework contributes to the implementation of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2024–2030. It supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as well as Target 19 on resource mobilisation. The framework also contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), through biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource use, livelihood support and institutional collaboration.

As India prepares to participate in the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), commencing on 19 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, its ABS framework demonstrates the country’s continued commitment to biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of biological resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation.

2321784.title: Second Meeting of Global Initiative on AI for Agri-Food Systems (GI-AI4FS) held at IMC 2026 in New Delhi
2321784.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Second Meeting of Global Initiative on AI for Agri-Food Systems (GI-AI4FS) held at IMC 2026 in New Delhi
Meeting focuses on responsible and effective application of AI and IoT to transform agri-food systems
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India hosted the Second meeting of the UN Global Initiative on AI for Agri-Food Systems (GI-AI4FS) alongside India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The meeting was jointly hosted with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. The GI-AI4FS is a UN Global Initiative, coordinated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), in close collaboration with Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and World Food Programme (WFP).

The meeting witnessed active participation from around 70 delegates in-person and 25 participants online, bringing together representatives of international organisations, government departments, agricultural research institutions, academia, industry and standards development organisations to advance global cooperation on the application of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in agriculture and food systems.

The inaugural session commenced with opening remarks by Dr. Sebastian Bosse, Chair of GI-AI4FS, followed by keynote addresses by Mr. Krishnan Pallassana, Senior Specialist – Strategy, Innovation & Partnerships, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau (TSB), ITU; Dr. A. K. Nayak, Deputy Director General (Natural Resource Management), ICAR, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare; Mr. Syed Tausif Abbas, Senior Deputy Director General & Head, TEC, DoT, India.

The meeting highlighted the growing role of AI, the Internet of Things (IoT) and digital connectivity in transforming agricultural practices and strengthening agri-food systems. The integration of connected sensors, weather stations, drones, satellite-based systems and AI-enabled analytics can support precision agriculture, improve resource utilisation, enable early detection of crop diseases and help farmers make informed decisions. Digital technologies also offer opportunities to improve traceability, reduce post-harvest losses and enhance efficiency across agricultural supply chains.

This meeting was preceded by a 2-day International Hackathon on ‘AI for Agri-Food Systems’, held on 8–9 October 2026, also jointly hosted by TEC, DoT and ICAR at the ICAR campus, New Delhi. The hackathon provided a collaborative platform for students, researchers, developers and innovators to develop practical technology solutions addressing real-world challenges in agriculture and food systems.

The GI-AI4FS meeting further featured a showcase of outcomes from this International Hackathon on AI Innovation for Resilient Agri-Food Systems. Shortlisted teams presented their solutions and demonstrated innovative AI applications developed during the hackathon. The programme also included the presentation of winning solutions and recognition of outstanding innovations, along with an award ceremony acknowledging the contributions of participating teams, partners, mentors and other contributors.

The meeting also addressed the governance architecture and organisational development of GI-AI4FS. The agenda included deliberations on the proposed governance and coordination structure, the nomination and confirmation of Working Group (WG) Chairs and Co-Chairs and members, the Terms of Reference of the Working Groups and the identification of priority areas and initial work streams.

Overall, the second meeting of GI-AI4FS provided a platform for advancing dialogue on the responsible use of AI in agriculture and food systems by promoting trustworthy and interoperable farmer-centric AI solutions, strengthening international cooperation on governance and standards and identifying opportunities to translate innovation into practical applications.

2321780.title: CAQM Reviews Stubble Burning Prevention Measures with District Administrations of Amritsar and Tarn Taran; Conducts Field Visits to Hotspot Villages
2321780.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2321780.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
 CAQM Reviews Stubble Burning Prevention Measures with District Administrations of Amritsar and Tarn Taran; Conducts Field Visits to Hotspot Villages
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level team of Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the chairmanship of Dr. S.D. Attri, Member (Technical), CAQM, visited Amritsar and Tarn Taran Districts of Punjab, during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.  These districts have been identified as hotspots for paddy stubble burning. Apart from field visits, the visiting team held a review meeting in Amritsar today (10.10.2026) with Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and other district-level officials of Amritsar and Tarn Taran district. This visit, apart from deployment of Flying Squads, is in line with high priority attached by the Commission towards achieving the objective of reduction and elimination of paddy stubble burning, a major cause of winter air pollution in NCR and adjoining areas.

The deliberations focused on reviewing preparedness and coordination among the concerned departments and district administration for effective in-situ and ex-situ utilisation of paddy stubble. The Commission stressed upon the importance of facilitating the farmers in terms of timely availability of CRM Machines, sensitizing, conducting Information, Education and Communication (IEC) Activities and providing necessary support.

Along with the review meeting, CAQM undertook field visits on 09.10.2026 and 10.10.2026 to the selected hotspot villages and facilities in districts of Amritsar and Tarn Taran to assess the prevailing ground-level situation and review the implementation of measures aimed at preventing stubble burning.

Regarding the district of Amritsar, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status, along with the availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery. It was informed that balers from Amritsar and adjoining districts were operating for collection and management of paddy straw. A supply chain has been established with industries having boilers for utilisation of paddy straw bales, with farmers and aggregators linked to these industries to facilitate ex-situ management. The district has also established a Control Room and Help Desk at the District Administrative Complex to identify farmers requiring CRM machinery and facilitate its availability. A district-level helpline has been circulated for reporting fire and stubble burning incidents to enable prompt action.

Regarding the district of Tarn Taran, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status and the availability and deployment of CRM machinery in the district. It was informed that balers from Tarn Taran and adjoining districts were operating for effective ex-situ management of paddy straw and that the district had substantially achieved its targets regarding procurement and availability of CRM machinery for farmers. Extensive field patrolling and surveillance through Nodal/ Cluster Officers and other field functionaries, along with IEC Activsties and enforcement measures to promote in-situ and ex-situ utilistion of paddy straw were also highlighted.

The officers of both districts assured their utmost commitment towards implementation of the CAQM’S Statutory Direction(s), strengthening preventive measures and making concerted efforts to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning incidents in their respective districts.

Additionally, as part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads deputed by the Commission have been deployed in 18 districts across Punjab, namely Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Firozpur, Muktsar, Bathinda, Amritsar, Moga, Mansa, Fazilka, Patiala, Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot, Barnala, Malerkotla, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Fatehgarh Sahib, for the period from 01.10.2026 to 30.11.2026.

CAQM has emphasised the need for continuous and effective field surveillance by District, Nodal and Cluster Officers, particularly in hotspots viz. low-cost sensors and other monitoring mechanisms and enforcement activities must continue without any lapse. Further, it was directed to ensure close coordination among farmers, aggregators, industries and other stakeholders to strengthen the ex-situ management supply chain and optimal utilisation of CRM machinery, balers, field staff, surveillance systems and control rooms.

CAQM has been continuously monitoring, coordinating and reviewing the measures being undertaken by the concerned State Governments, State Pollution Control Boards and District Administrations for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning. The Commission has reiterated the need for concerted and coordinated efforts by all concerned agencies, along with active facilitation and cooperation of farmers and other stakeholders, to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.

2321754.title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Visits Sainya Sampark Mela in Deoghar, Jharkhand
2321754.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Visits Sainya Sampark Mela in Deoghar, Jharkhand
“Our Soldiers Have Always Stood with the Nation, and We Must Always Stand with Them and Their Families”: Vice-President
Vice-President Calls for Continued National Commitment to Welfare of Veterans and Veer Naris
Jharkhand Has a Proud Tradition of Military Service and Sacrifice: Vice-President
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited the Sainya Sampark Mela – Sadaiv Aapke Saath in Deoghar, Jharkhand, today. The Mela was organised by the Indian Army in collaboration with the Deoghar District Administration to provide welfare services and grievance redressal facilities to ex-servicemen, Veer Naris and their dependents across the Santhal Pargana region.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited the Sainya Sampark Mela – Sadaiv Aapke Saath in Deoghar, Jharkhand, organised by the Indian Army to support veterans, Veer Naris and their families. He emphasised that while our soldiers have always stood with the Nation, the Nation must always stand with them and their families. He called for a lasting national commitment to their welfare, ensuring that their sacrifices are honoured and they receive the respect, support and care they deserve.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 10, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President paid tribute to the veterans and Veer Naris for their invaluable sacrifices and contributions to the Nation. Describing veterans as an important national resource, he said that their experience could guide the youth and their leadership could contribute significantly to nation-building. Saluting the Veer Naris, he observed that behind every soldier serving at the border stands a family that shares the sacrifices and responsibilities of military service. He emphasised that the Nation could never forget the sacrifices made by soldiers and their families.

Recalling his tenure as Governor of Jharkhand, the Vice-President highlighted the State’s proud tradition of service to the Nation. He paid tribute to Param Vir Chakra awardee Lance Naik Albert Ekka and recalled the contributions of tribal freedom fighters, including Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Tilka Manjhi, Sidhu and Kanhu, and Nilambar and Pitambar. He said that the spirit of patriotism and national service continued to inspire the people of Jharkhand.

The Vice-President highlighted the fulfilment of the long-standing demand for One Rank, One Pension under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and referred to various welfare initiatives undertaken for veterans and Veer Naris. Appreciating the single-window mechanism at the Mela, he said that bringing pension-related assistance, medical facilities, documentation services and grievance redressal under one platform was a meaningful example of last-mile delivery.

Emphasising the importance of coordinated public service, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the participation of the Armed Forces, civil administration, financial institutions, healthcare providers and welfare agencies reflected a shared commitment to serving those who had served the Nation. He called for the theme “Sadaiv Aapke Saath” (Always with You) to become a continuing national commitment, ensuring that veterans and their families always felt respected, supported and cared for.

During the visit, the Vice-President toured various stalls at the Sainya Sampark Mela, including displays of weapons and military equipment, disaster relief facilities, Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) services, medical screening and blood donation camps, women’s health awareness initiatives, NCC activities and pension-related services. He also interacted with veterans, beneficiaries and other people attending the Mela.

The Vice-President congratulated the Indian Army and the Deoghar District Administration for organising the initiative and appreciated the efforts of Member of Parliament Dr. Nishikant Dubey. He also thanked the participating institutions and agencies for their contributions towards the welfare of the Armed Forces community.

The event was attended by the Governor of Jharkhand, Shri Santosh Kumar Gangwar; Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav; Members of Parliament Dr. Nishikant Dubey and Shri Aditya Sahu; General Officer Commanding, 111 Area, Lt. Gen. Pawan Chadha; Chairperson of Baba Baidyanath Medical Trust, Ms. Anamika Gautam; senior officers of the Indian Army, officials of the civil administration, veterans, Veer Naris and their families.

2321739.title: MY Bharat–NSS Concludes First Month of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan with Nationwide ‘Yuva Sanwad Mela’; Engages Over 1.06 Lakh Participants
2321739.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2321739.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat–NSS Concludes First Month of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan with Nationwide ‘Yuva Sanwad Mela’; Engages Over 1.06 Lakh Participants
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through MY Bharat and the National Service Scheme (NSS), successfully organised the nationwide ‘Yuva Sanwad Mela’ on October 9, 2026, marking the conclusion of Month 1 of the 100-Week Sankalp Abhiyan under the theme ‘My Health, My Pride’. Conducted across 200 designated institutions and their adopted villages, the initiative recorded a consolidated outreach of 1,06,855 participants, bringing together young people and community members to strengthen awareness about substance abuse prevention and promote a healthier, addiction-free society.

Implemented across 15 NSS Regional Directorates, the Week 4 intervention achieved 100 per cent execution against the target of 200 institutions. The initiative engaged 93,662 youth participants and reached an additional 13,193 citizens through dedicated outreach activities in villages and slum communities. Moving beyond conventional pledge-taking activities, the Yuva Sanwad Mela emphasised interactive dialogue, public awareness and cultural expression to encourage informed conversations on the harmful effects of substance abuse.

The nationwide initiative featured three major components: youth dialogue, awareness stalls and cultural performances. Under the Youth Dialogue (Sanwad) component, 509 interactive seminars and open forums were organised, engaging 36,086 youth in discussions on the root causes of substance abuse, peer pressure and community-led prevention strategies, with participation from faculty members and local leaders.

Under the awareness component, NSS volunteers established 396 informational stalls and kiosks to disseminate information on the physical and psychological consequences of addiction and familiarise participants with available counselling resources. These activities engaged 32,909 participants. Complementing these efforts, 587 cultural performances, including street plays (Nukkad Nataks), skits and musical presentations, reached 24,944 individuals, using creative and locally relevant formats to communicate the message of an addiction-free India.

The campaign also demonstrated strong participation across genders. The reported youth participation figures recorded 48,269 female participants and 45,618 male participants, reflecting the active involvement of young women in the nationwide awareness drive. Through their participation, NSS volunteers and young people helped carry the message of health, well-being and collective responsibility into educational institutions and surrounding communities.

The grassroots mobilisation was further amplified through digital platforms, with young ambassadors generating 935 social media posts using the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva. These digital efforts extended the visibility of local activities and helped reinforce the campaign’s message among wider audiences.

The successful conclusion of Month 1 establishes a foundation for the next phase of the 100-Week Sankalp Abhiyan. Month 2 will focus on physical fitness and sports under the theme ‘Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth’, encouraging young people to adopt healthy lifestyles and recognise physical activity as an important component of substance abuse prevention.

Through the sustained participation of MY Bharat, NSS, educational institutions and local communities, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports continues to strengthen youth-led awareness, community engagement and collective action towards the vision of a healthier, empowered and addiction-free India.

*****

Pawan Singh Faujdar

2321822.title: پردھان منتری دھن دھانیہ کرشی یوجنا  (پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی)
2321822.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
پردھان منتری دھن دھانیہ کرشی یوجنا  (پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی)
سو  (100) اضلاع میں زرعی ترقی پر مرکوز اقدامات کا ایک سال
प्रविष्टि तिथि: 10 OCT 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

ضلعی سطح کے اقدامات کے ذریعے زراعت میں تبدیلی لانا

ہندوستان کے زرعی شعبے میں مختلف خطوں اور کاشت کار برادریوں میں زرعی ترقی کے وسیع امکانات موجود ہیں۔ تاہم، ان امکانات کے باوجود، بہت سے علاقوں کو کم زرعی پیداوار، آبپاشی کی ناکافی سہولتوں، قرض تک محدود رسائی فصل کی کٹائی کے بعد کے بنیادی ڈھانچے کی کمی جیسے چیلنجوں کا سامنا ہے۔ اس کے نتیجے میں، یہ علاقے اپنی زرعی صلاحیت سے بھرپور فائدہ نہیں اٹھا پاتے اور معاشی ترقی کے معاملے میں پیچھے رہ جاتے ہیں۔

پردھان منتری دھن دھانیہ کرشی یوجنا (پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی) کا مقصد ان خامیوں کو دور کرنا اور ہدفی اقدامات کے ذریعے 100 امنگوں والے زرعی اضلاع کی ترقی کو فروغ دینا ہے۔ ضلعی سطح کی مخصوص ضروریات کو پورا کرتے ہوئے یہ اسکیم زرعی پیداوار میں اضافے، آبپاشی کی سہولتوں میں بہتری، قرض تک رسائی میں آسانی اور فصل کی کٹائی کے بعد کے بنیادی ڈھانچے کی ترقی کے نئے امکانات پیدا کر سکتی ہے۔ مرکزی کابینہ نے 16 جولائی 2025 کو مرکزی کابینہ نے پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی کو چھ سال کی مدت کے لیے منظوری دی تھی، جبکہ وزیر اعظم نے 11 اکتوبر 2025 کو اس کا باضابطہ آغاز کیا تھا۔ اس اسکیم کی پہلی سالگرہ اس سال 11 اکتوبر کو منائی جائے گی۔

مالی سال 2025-26 سے شروع ہونے والی اس چھ سالہ پہل کا مقصد 100 امنگوں والے زرعی اضلاع میں زراعت اور اس سے وابستہ سرگرمیوں کو فروغ دینا اور ان میں تبدیلی لانا ہے۔ ان اضلاع کا انتخاب تین اہم اشاریوں کی بنیاد پر کیا گیا ہے: کم زرعی پیداواری صلاحیت، فصلوں کی کم شدت (ایک سال میں فی رقبہ اگائی جانے والی فصلوں کی تعداد کے تناظر میں) اور زرعی قرضوں کی کم تقسیم یا زرعی قرضوں کا کم اجرا۔ انتخاب کے عمل میں ہر ریاست اور مرکز کے زیر انتظام علاقے میں خالص زیرِ کاشت رقبے اور زیرِ کاشت اراضی پر مشتمل زرعی ہولڈنگزکے حصے کو بھی مدنظر رکھا گیا ہے۔ ہر ریاست سے کم از کم ایک ضلع اس اسکیم کے لیے منتخب کیا گیا ہے۔

اس اسکیم پر عمل درآمد 11 وزارتوں اور محکموں کی شراکت سے کیا جا رہا ہے۔ اس کے تحت مرکزی حکومت کی 36 اسکیموں کو یکجا کیا گیا ہے، جن میں ریاستی اسکیموں اور نجی شعبے کی شرکت بھی شامل ہے۔ اس مربوط طریقۂ کار کے ذریعے مقامی ضروریات اور زرعی ترجیحات کے مطابق اقدامات کرنے میں مدد ملے گی۔

نفاذ کا انتظامی ڈھانچہ

پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی اسکیم پر عمل درآمد کے لیے تین سطحی انتظامی ڈھانچہ اختیار کیا گیا ہے:

  • ضلعی سطح: ضلع کلکٹر/ضلع مجسٹریٹ (ڈی ایم) کی سربراہی میں ضلع دھن دھانیہ کرشی یوجنا سمیتی ضلعی ایکشن پلان تیار کرتی ہے اور اس پر عمل درآمد کو یقینی بناتی ہے۔
  • ریاستی سطح: ریاست کے چیف سکریٹری کی سربراہی میں ریاستی دھن دھانیہ کرشی یوجنا سمیتی ضلعی منصوبوں کا جائزہ لیتی ہے اور ان کی نگرانی کرتی ہے۔
  • قومی سطح: اسکیم کی نگرانی کے لیے دو کمیٹیاں تشکیل دی گئی ہیں۔ قومی ایگزیکٹو کمیٹی کی سربراہی مرکزی وزیر زراعت و کسانوں کی بہبود کرتے ہیں، جبکہ قومی نگرانی کمیٹی کی سربراہی محکمہ زراعت و کسانوں کی بہبود (ڈی اے اینڈ ایف ڈبلیو) کے سکریٹری کرتے ہیں۔

ضلعی ایکشن پلان

  • ضلعی ایکشن پلان (ڈی اے پی) بنیادی معلومات اور تشخیصی تجزیے کی بنیاد پر تیار کیے جاتے ہیں۔ ان منصوبوں میں مقامی زرعی ضروریات کی نشاندہی کی جاتی ہے اور متعلقہ مرکزی و ریاستی اسکیموں کو یکجا کرکے ان ضروریات کو پورا کرنے کے اقدامات کیے جاتے ہیں۔ ڈی اے پی میں نتائج پر مبنی اہداف، سالانہ سنگِ میل اور متعلقہ اسکیموں سے منسلک اقدامات کا تعین کیا جاتا ہے۔
  • ڈی اے پی متعلقہ ریاستی محکموں کو بھیجے جاتے ہیں تاکہ انہیں ان کے سالانہ ایکشن پلان میں شامل کیا جا سکے۔ اس سے ضروری منظوریوں کے حصول اور ضروری منظوریوں اور فنڈز کے اجرا میں سہولت ہوتی ہے ۔
  • 36 اسکیموں کے تحت 121 اشاریوں کی مدد سے پیش رفت کا جائزہ لیا جاتا ہے، جن میں 74 آؤٹ پٹ اشاریے اور 47 نتائج کے اشاریے شامل ہیں۔ پیداوار سے متعلق اشاریوں کی بنیاد پر اضلاع کی کارکردگی کی ماہانہ درجہ بندی پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی ڈیش بورڈ (https://pmddky.niti.gov.in/)کے ذریعے کی جاتی ہے۔

نفاذ اور پیش رفت کا سال

پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی ڈیش بورڈ نے اکتوبر 2025 کے آخری ہفتے میں کام کرنا شروع کردیا۔ آؤٹ پٹ اشاریوں کی بنیاد پر ماہانہ درجہ بندینومبر 2025 میں شروع ہوئی، جس سے 100 اضلاع میں پیش رفت کی نگرانی کے لیے ایک منظم طریقۂ کار دستیاب ہوا۔

  • تمام 100 دھن دھانیہ اضلاع نے اپنے ضلعی ایکشن پلان تیار کر لیے ہیں اور ان پر عمل درآمد جاری ہے۔
  • جائزے اور نگرانی کے لیے ریاستی، ضلعی اور قومی سطح پر کمیٹیاں تشکیل دی گئی ہیں۔
  • تمام 100 اضلاع نے اگست 2026 تک پیداوار سے متعلق اشاریوں کے اعداد و شمار جمع کرا دیے۔ ان تمام اضلاع نے مالی سال 2025-26 کے لیے نتائج سے متعلق اشاریوں کے اعداد و شمار بھی پیش کیے۔
  • مرکزی نوڈل افسران باقاعدگی سے پیش رفت کا جائزہ لے رہے ہیں اور اضلاع کی رہنمائی کر رہے ہیں۔
  • محکمۂ سرکاری ادارے نے مالی سال 2026-27 اور 2027-28 کے لیے مرکزی سرکاری اداروں (سی پی ایس ایز) کے ذریعے کارپوریٹ سماجی ذمہ داری (سی ایس آر) کی سرگرمیوں کے تحت دھن دھانیہ اضلاع کو اختیار کرنے کی تجویز شامل کی ہے۔
  • چھ اہم مقاصد کے سلسلے میں 100 اضلاع کا اوسط اسکور اپریل 2026 میں 18.85 سے بڑھ کر اگست 2026 میں 46.89 ہو گیا، یعنی 28.04 پوائنٹس کا اضافہ ریکارڈ کیا گیا۔
  • اسی مدت کے دوران مختلف مقاصد کے تحت اوسط اسکور میں بھی بہتری درج کی گئی:
  • زرعی پیداوار میں اضافہ: 1.50 سے بڑھ کر 8.08
  • فصلوں میں تنوع اور پائیدار زرعی طریقوں کو فروغ دینا: 4.08 سے بڑھ کر 10.18
  • فصل کی کٹائی کے بعد ذخیرہ کرنے کی صلاحیت میں اضافہ: 2.14 سے بڑھ کر 5.19
  • آبپاشی کے بنیادی ڈھانچے کو بہتر بنانا: 1.38 سے بڑھ کر 4.91
  • قلیل مدتی اور طویل مدتی زرعی قرضوں تک رسائی میں اضافہ: 2.40 سے بڑھ کر 6.53
  • بہتر حکمرانی اور خدمات کی فراہمی: 7.41 سے بڑھ کر 12.05

اسکیم کے پہلے سال میں کسانوں اور کسانوں کی پیداواری تنظیموں (ایف پی اوز) کو تجربات کے تبادلے اور نئے مواقع تلاش کرنے کے لیے ایک پلیٹ فارم بھی فراہم کیا گیا۔ دسمبر 2025 میں منعقدہ پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی ایف پی او سنگم میں 15 ریاستوں اور پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی کے 33 اضلاع سے تعلق رکھنے والے 72 سے زائد ایف پی اوز نے شرکت کی۔ اس تقریب میں زرعی پیداوار میں اضافے، منڈیوں تک رسائی اور آمدنی میں اضافے سے متعلق تجربات پیش کیے گئے۔ اس کے علاوہ قدرتی کاشت کاری، تلہن کی پیداوار، شہد کی مکھیوں کی پرورش، محفوظ کاشت کاری، خرد آبپاشی (مائیکرو آبپاشی)،  ادارہ جاتی مالیات اور ڈیجیٹل زراعت جیسے موضوعات کا بھی احاطہ کیا گیا۔

دھن دھانیہ اضلاع میں بہترین طریقۂ کار

مقامی پروسیسنگ اور بہتر قیمت کا حصول

مہاراشٹر کے گڈچرولی ضلع میں، جو پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی کے تحت شامل ہے، دیسائی گنج فارمرز پروڈیوسر کمپنی لمیٹڈ نامی کسانوں کی پیداواری تنظیم (ایف پی او) کے 800 کسان اراکین ہیں۔ اس نے فی گھنٹہ 3 ٹن پروسیسنگ کی صلاحیت پر مشتمل چاول کی مل اور 900 میٹرک ٹن گنجائش والا گودام قائم کیا ہے۔ جے شری رام چاول کی قیمتی قسم کی پروسیسنگ اور فصل کی کٹائی کے بعد ذخیرہ کرنے کے لیے بنیادی ڈھانچے کی دستیابی سے مقامی سطح پر قدر افزائی اور بہتر قیمت وصول کرنے میں مدد ملتی ہے۔ اس ایف پی او نے مالی سال 2025-26 میں 1.24 کروڑ روپے کا کاروبار کیا۔

بہتر منڈیاں، زیادہ منافع

کرناٹک کے (تمکر)   تمکورو ضلع میں، جو پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی کے تحت شامل ہے، تپتور فارمر پروڈیوسر کمپنی لمیٹڈ نامی ایف پی او کے 750 کسان اراکین ہیں۔ یہ ایک فرانسیسی کثیر القومی کمپنی کو گول کھوپرا  (ناریل کی خشک گری کی مخصوص قسم)    فراہم کرتا ہے، جس سے اس کے کسان اراکین کو بہتر قیمتیں حاصل کرنے اور منڈیوں تک رسائی بڑھانے میں مدد ملتی ہے۔ ایف پی او نے مالی سال 2025-26 میں 1.60 کروڑ روپے کا کاروبار کیا۔ اس کے علاوہ، 12 ستمبر 2026 تک اس نے 1.9 کروڑ روپے سے زائد مالیت کا 138 ٹن کھوپرا جمع کیا تھا۔

جدید آبپاشی، بہتر زرعی پیداوار

راجستھان کے جیسلمیر ضلع میں، جو پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی کے تحت شامل ہے، جیسلمیر کرشی فیڈ پروڈیوسر کمپنی لمیٹڈ نامی ایف پی او کے 1,236 کسان اراکین ہیں۔ یہ تنظیم 2,000 ایکڑ رقبے پر کیڑوں کے مربوط انتظام  (آئی پی ایم) کے طریقۂ کار کے تحت زیرے کی کاشت کرتی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ، 500 ایکڑ رقبے میں شمسی توانائی سے چلنے والے اسپرنکلر نظام کے ذریعے آبپاشی کی جاتی ہے۔ یہ اقدامات پانی کے مؤثر استعمال، قابلِ تجدید توانائی کے فروغ اور زرعی پیداوار میں اضافے میں معاون ہیں۔

اضلاع میں زرعی ترقی کو تیز کرنا

پی ایم ڈی ڈی کے وائی نے 11 اکتوبر 2026 کو اپنا پہلا سال مکمل کیا۔ یہ سال ضلعی سطح پر ہدفی اقدامات اور زرعی ترقی کو فروغ دینے پر مرکوز رہا۔ اب 100 اضلاع میں ضلعی ایکشن پلان کے ذریعے کام کیا جا رہا ہے اور اشاریوں کی بنیاد پر پیش رفت کی نگرانی کی جا رہی ہے۔ ضلع کی مخصوص ضروریات کے مطابق کیے جانے والے اقدامات زمینی سطح پر زرعی ترقی کو تقویت دے رہے ہیں۔ اب تک حاصل ہونے والی پیش رفت آئندہ برسوں میں بہتر ہم آہنگی اور پائیدار زرعی ترقی کی مضبوط بنیاد فراہم کرتی ہے۔

2321729.title: Minister of State for Coal and Mines inaugurates Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026)
2321729.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Minister of State for Coal and Mines inaugurates Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026)
Economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits are reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”- MoS, Satish Chandra Dubey
CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for Viksit Bharat: Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State, Ministry of Coal and Mines, Government of India, inaugurated the Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026), organised by Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), under Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in New Delhi. The two-day Conference, scheduled on 6–7 October 2026, was organised around the theme “Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment.”

 

In his Keynote Address, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, emphasised the close relationship between national economic growth, regional development and the well-being of communities in resource-bearing areas. He observed that economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits were reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”.

He underlined that, for sectors closely connected with natural resources and local communities, growth and social development could not be viewed as separate objectives. On the occasion, he formally released the Comprehensive CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies, developed to provide sector-specific direction for more structured, need-based and outcome-oriented CSR interventions in the coal sector.

The inaugural session also witnessed the release of the India CSR Factbook 2024–25, providing a consolidated reference on the evolving CSR landscape in India. The session was graced by Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil, Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India; Ms. Shoko Ishikawa, UN Women Country Representative in India; Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA; and Prof. Garima Dadhich, Head, School of Business Environment, IICA.

Delivering the Inaugural Address, Smt. Pallavi Jain Govil, Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, placed CSR within India’s larger corporate-governance and national-development framework. She stated that the theme of NCCSR 2026 called upon stakeholders to “look beyond the annual obligation” and consider the larger contribution that responsible enterprise could make to India’s development journey. Referring to India’s distinctive statutory CSR architecture, she emphasised that the framework combined statutory obligation with company-level responsibility, Board oversight, public disclosure and impact assessment, and that CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for Viksit Bharat. She also released the India CSR Factbook 2024–25.

In his Welcome Address, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, highlighted the importance of keeping CSR discussions anchored in implementation and visible development outcomes. Noting that CSR brought together Government, industry, public sector enterprises, implementing organisations, development partners and academia, he observed that “decisions may be taken in Board rooms, but their value is ultimately seen in schools, health centres, livelihood programmes, villages, towns and districts where they affect the lives of people”. He said that the National CSR Exhibition had been designed not merely to display projects but to make outcomes visible and to serve as a space for learning, replication and partnership.

The inaugural session was followed by a fireside chat on “Social Stock Exchange: Purpose, Capital & Impact”, featuring Shri Shailesh K. Pathak, Senior Advisor – Policy, National Stock Exchange, and Prof. Garima Dadhich. The discussion examined the role of the Social Stock Exchange in connecting social purpose with capital and the importance of credible impact measurement, transparency and institutional trust in strengthening the social sector financing ecosystem.

In the post-lunch session, Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, delivered the keynote address. His address placed CSR in the wider context of corporate governance and emphasised the need for companies to approach CSR as an integral part of responsible corporate conduct and institutional decision-making. He also invited companies to register on the CSR Exchange Portal, highlighting its relevance as a mechanism for connecting CSR stakeholders and facilitating purposeful engagement.

The keynote address was followed by High-Level Panel discussion on “Board Governance and Strategic Commitment in CSR”. The panel discussed the role of Boards and senior management in ensuring strategic oversight of CSR, the importance of linking expenditure with clearly identified needs and outcomes, and the need for effective monitoring and accountability mechanisms.

The panel comprised Shri Ashok Kumar Gupta (Retd.), CEO, Dalmia Bharat Foundation and former Chairperson, Competition Commission of India and National Financial Reporting Authority; Prof. Maneesha V. Ramesh, Pro Vice Chancellor, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Shri Bhaskar Chowdary Nettem, Director (Production), ONGC; Shri Ayush Gupta, Director (Human Resources), GAIL (India) Limited; Shri Bibhuti Ranjan Pradhan, Executive Director (Coordination and CSR), Indian Oil Corporation Limited; Dr. Purvi Mehta, Independent Director, Mahindra Agri Solutions Limited; and Ms. Ruchi Sadhana, Vice President, HCLTech.

The discussions underlined that stronger Board engagement could improve the quality of CSR decision-making by ensuring closer attention to project relevance, implementation capacity, geographic and thematic need, monitoring, evaluation and sustainability. The panel also noted the value of partnerships and professional institutional mechanisms in translating CSR commitments into durable development outcomes.

The second Panel discussion on “Sector-Based Approaches to CSR Aligned with SDG Priorities” examined the case for closer alignment between CSR interventions, sectoral development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals. The session was chaired by Ms. Anita Shah Akella, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India. In her keynote address, she underlined the need for sector-specific approaches that recognise differing development challenges, institutional capacities and local priorities.

The panel included Shri Lucas L. Kamsuan, Joint Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises, Government of India; Ms. Reetu Jain, Economic Adviser, Ministry of Power, Government of India; Dr. Chetna Shukla, Deputy Director General, Ministry of Coal, Government of India; Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, Social Statistics Division, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India; Shri Rajeev Kumar, Deputy Director General (Data & Management), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India; and Shri Prabhakar L., EVP & Head – Social Investments, ITC. Shri Bharat Wakhlu, Founder and President, The Wakhlu Advisory, moderated the session.

The panel deliberated on the need to move beyond uniform approaches to CSR and to recognise the distinct development contexts, operational footprints and stakeholder needs associated with different sectors by highlighting the significance of sector-specific CSR frameworks developed by IICA for the Ministry of Coal and Coal India Limited, in addressing sectoral development priorities and community needs. Additionally, it emphasised the need to strengthen CSR reporting through alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), enabling systematic assessment of corporate contributions to national and global development priorities.

First day sessions concluded with a broad consensus on the need to strengthen the institutional quality of CSR—from Board-level oversight and evidence-based project selection to sectoral alignment, convergence, monitoring and assessment of outcomes. The proceedings reflected the Conference theme by placing emphasis on a transition from compliance alone towards sustained corporate commitment to inclusive and measurable development.

The Conference brought together senior representatives of the Government of India, public sector enterprises, private sector companies, international organisations, academia and civil society to deliberate on the evolving role of Corporate Social Responsibility in supporting national development priorities. The deliberations emphasised the need for CSR interventions to be guided by institutional responsibility, local development needs, measurable outcomes and effective convergence among stakeholders.

NCCSR 2026 is being organised by the School of Business Environment, IICA, with participation from Government, public sector enterprises, corporate organisations, international institutions, academia and civil society.

                        ***

2321728.title: Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) concludes, calls for stronger governance, convergence and outcome-oriented CSR for Viksit Bharat
2321728.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) concludes, calls for stronger governance, convergence and outcome-oriented CSR for Viksit Bharat
CSR is not merely as a statutory obligation but as a strategic instrument for India’s growth: Ajit Seth, former Cabinet Secretary, Govt of India
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, concluded the Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) at The Ashok, New Delhi. The two-day Conference, organised by the School of Business Environment, IICA, was held under the theme “Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment.”

The Conference concluded with the formal Valedictory Session on “From Compliance to Commitment”, in the presence of Shri Ajit Seth, former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India; Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA; and Prof. Garima Dadhich, Head, School of Business Environment, IICA. The session reviewed the principal issues emerging from the two-day deliberations and reflected on the further strengthening of India’s CSR ecosystem through improved governance, institutional coordination, evidence-based planning and greater emphasis on measurable development outcomes.

Shri Ajit Seth, former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India, in his Valedictory Address, emphasised that the success of Corporate Social Responsibility should not be judged only by the quantum of expenditure, but by the difference it made to people’s lives and to the country’s development. He noted that CSR had emerged as a substantial source of development expenditure and observed that the framework had deliberately placed responsibility with company Boards, thereby embedding CSR within the wider evolution of corporate governance and responsible conduct.

He cautioned against tokenism and underlined the need to scale up effective interventions, address geographical imbalances in CSR spending and extend greater attention to underserved districts. He also stressed that technology could strengthen visibility, monitoring and accountability, but could not substitute field knowledge and administrative judgement. Calling upon companies to view CSR not merely as a statutory obligation but as a strategic instrument for India’s growth, he said that stronger convergence among stakeholders and sustained attention to inclusive and sustainable outcomes would contribute to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Following the Valedictory Address, Shri Ajit Seth released the Compendium of CSR Best Practices 2025, which brings together the practices showcased by exhibitors during NCCSR 2025. The publication forms part of IICA’s effort to document and disseminate implementation experiences and replicable CSR practices for wider institutional learning.

Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, stated that the deliberations during NCCSR 2026 reflected the increasing breadth and maturity of India’s CSR ecosystem. He noted that the Conference had examined issues relating to Board governance, sector-specific CSR approaches, technology and Artificial Intelligence, convergence through the CSR Exchange, women’s economic empowerment, regional distribution of CSR resources, skills and employment, and assessment of social outcomes.

Prof. Garima Dadhich, Head, School of Business Environment, IICA, presented the key outcomes emerging from the Conference and acknowledged the contribution of participating Ministries, public and private sector organisations, international institutions, academia, civil society, exhibitors and delegates.

Earlier in the day, the proceedings commenced with High-Level Panel on “Transforming CSR through AI & Technology.” The session examined the use of Artificial Intelligence, digital tools and data systems in the planning, implementation, monitoring and assessment of CSR programmes. It also considered the need for technology adoption to remain anchored in development objectives, accountability and measurable social outcomes. The panel brought together representatives from SBI Foundation, ICICI Bank, HCLFoundation, IndiGo, GIVE and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham.

At the commencement of the session, the Compendium of CSR Best Practices showcased at the National Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility 2024 was released. The Compendium documented selected CSR initiatives presented during the previous edition of the National Exhibition, with the objective of facilitating wider dissemination, institutional learning and replication of effective practices.

This was followed by a Keynote Address by Shri Santanu Mitra, Senior Economic Adviser, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India. The address considered the evolving role of CSR within the broader framework of responsible business conduct and sustainable development and highlighted the importance of institutional mechanisms that could strengthen the interface between corporate resources, credible social-sector interventions and measurable outcomes.

High-Level Panel discussion on “CSR Exchange: Enabling Convergence, Collaboration and Collective Impact” examined the role of the CSR Exchange in enabling greater coordination among companies, implementing organisations and other development stakeholders. The session considered issues relating to project visibility, institutional credibility, collaboration and the potential for convergence in addressing development priorities. The panel was chaired by Shri Anil Swarup, former Secretary, Ministry of Coal and Department of School Education and Literacy, Government of India, and moderated by Prof. Garima Dadhich. Chairing the panel,  Shri Anil Swarup, former Secretary to the Government of India, remarked that the Portal should meet the expectations set out by the Committee on CSR Exchange. The panel considered how credible information on projects and implementing organisations, transparent processes and stronger institutional coordination could help the Portal fulfil its intended purpose and improve the effectiveness of CSR partnerships.

The panel emphasised the importance of strengthening the CSR Exchange Portal through data integration and automated processes, including mechanisms to facilitate the identification, assessment and selection of credible implementing organisations. It further underscored the need to strengthen the link between CSR expenditure and measurable social development outcomes, particularly through better project assessment, monitoring and reporting. The panel recommended that MCA and IICA should continue to support these priorities through research, capacity building, policy engagement and collaboration among Government, industry and development institutions.

An Expert Dialogue on “Investing in CARE: Reimagining CSR for Women Economic Empowerment” examined the relationship between care responsibilities and women’s participation in the economy. The discussion considered the potential for CSR to support childcare, elder care, community-based care infrastructure and skilling of care workers, while strengthening women’s access to employment and economic opportunities. Representatives from SEWA Bharat, Grant Thornton and UN Women participated in the dialogue.

In the afternoon, High-Level Panel on “Decentralising CSR for Inclusive Regional Growth” focused on the geographic distribution of CSR resources and the need for interventions to respond more effectively to regional and local development priorities. Representatives from the Department of Public Enterprises, NSE Foundation, Spark Minda Group, Tata Steel Foundation, Inclusion Foundation, Western Coalfields Limited and ONGC Foundation participated in the session.

The panel recommended the development of universal indicators for the assessment of CSR projects, enabling greater consistency and comparability of project outcomes across regions and sectors. It also emphasised that such indicators should be applied with due regard to local circumstances, and that district-level evidence and collaboration with local institutions should inform the identification of priority interventions.

The Conference also featured an Expert Dialogue on “Leveraging CSR and PMIS – From Skills to Employment”, with Shri Balamurugan D, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India,  Shri Lohit Bhatia, ED & CEO, Quess Corp Ltd, representatives from ONGC and Dixon Technologies India Ltd, moderated by D. Garima Dadhich. Shri Balamurugan D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, invited businesses to leverage opportunities under the Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme (PMIS). He highlighted the potential of structured workplace exposure and industry participation to narrow the gap between the skills young people possess and those required for employment. The discussion focused on improving the transition from skilling to employment, strengthening labour-market linkages and exploring the role of CSR in supporting employability and employment outcomes.

The proceedings also included a cultural presentation by artists from the Ministry of Culture before the formal Valedictory Session.

The two-day Conference brought together 600 plus senior representatives from Government, public sector enterprises, private sector companies, international organisations, academia and civil society. The deliberations reinforced the need for CSR interventions to move beyond expenditure and compliance towards stronger governance, evidence-based planning, institutional collaboration and measurable development outcomes, in alignment with national and regional priorities and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

                       ***

2321726.title: Defence Secretary to Visit Cyprus and Greece from 12-15 October 2026
2321726.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Defence Secretary to Visit Cyprus and Greece from 12-15 October 2026
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh will undertake an official visit to Cyprus and Greece from October 12 to 15, 2026. Maritime security and defence industrial cooperation will remain prominent themes during the discussions with both the countries.

During his visit to Cyprus on October 12-13, the Defence Secretary is scheduled to meet his counterparts in the Cypriot Ministry of Defence and also call on the Cypriot leadership. Following the visit of the President of Cyprus to India in May 2026, the India-Cyprus Strategic Partnership has gained further momentum. Defence Secretary’s visit is expected to underscore the shared commitment to deepening and expanding bilateral engagement, particularly in the maritime domain.

In the second leg of his visit, Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh will interact with the senior defence and military leadership of Greece. The Greek Minister of National Defence visited India in February 2026 and held talks with Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh. These high-level exchanges reflect the growing India-Greece partnership in the defence and strategic domains.

The visit assumes added significance as India seeks to further strengthen its defence and strategic cooperation with partners in the European Union, following the signing of the landmark India-EU Security and Defence Partnership.
